issues.title: Get familiar with Linear
issues.description:
Welcome to Linear! 

Watch an introductory video and access a list of resources below.

[LinearH264Version_1.mp4](https://uploads.linear.app/fe63b3e2-bf87-46c0-8784-cd7d639287c8/a044fb03-9b84-470c-ab6f-8eae613e2529/98d7274d-de7f-4910-b3f3-f72e8e286a98)

### **Choose your setup guide** based on your company stage:

* [Small teams](<https://linear.app/docs/how-to-use-linear-small-teams>)
  For early-stage startups and projects
* [Startups & mid-size companies](<https://linear.app/docs/how-to-use-linear-startups-mid-size-companies>)
  For growing teams with cross-functional needs
* [Large & scaling companies](<https://linear.app/docs/how-to-use-linear-large-scaling-companies>)
  For enterprise and high-growth teams with complex workflows

### **Need help getting started?**

* [Join our Slack community](<https://linear.app/join-slack>)
  Connect with other Linear users and get tips
* [Join a live ](<https://lu.ma/welcome-to-linear?utm_source=docs>)[onboarding](<https://lu.ma/welcome-to-linear?utm_source=onboarding>)[ ](<https://lu.ma/welcome-to-linear?utm_source=docs>)[session](<https://lu.ma/welcome-to-linear?utm_source=onboarding>)
  Learn the essentials and see demos of core workflows

---

If you have any questions hit `?` in the bottom left > Contact us.

![contactlinear (1).gif](https://uploads.linear.app/fe63b3e2-bf87-46c0-8784-cd7d639287c8/bc9bbf62-4192-411f-88f6-c89c9150503e/4df0346e-803b-4f58-8527-4aeb30d88411)

issues.title: Connect your tools
issues.description:
Integrations turn Linear into your source of truth around product development. Keep data in sync, and eliminate manual updates between tools.

![connect-your-tools.png](https://uploads.linear.app/fe63b3e2-bf87-46c0-8784-cd7d639287c8/c2eae035-37e2-4754-adcb-b8305431aa1f/c92d70c7-e6d0-4fa2-a0fd-78f6e780993a)

### **Key integrations**

* [**Slack**](<https://linear.app/settings/integrations/slack>)
  Create issues from Slack messages and sync threads
* **[GitHub](<https://linear.app/settings/integrations/github>) / [GitLab](<https://linear.app/settings/integrations/gitlab>)**
  Automate your pull request, commit workflows, and keep issues synced both ways
* [**Agents**](<https://linear.app/integrations/agents>)
  Deploy AI agents that work alongside you as teammates

### **Browse all integrations**

Discover 150+ available connections in our [integration directory](<https://linear.app/integrations>) – from bug creation via support tools (Intercom, Zendesk), to issues created from design explorations (Figma).

### **Linear API**

If you need something more custom, you can build directly on the Linear API (built on GraphQL). [See our Dev Docs to learn more](<https://linear.app/developers>).

issues.title: Set up your teams
issues.description:
This workspace is a container for your organization’s work. 

* [Learn more about Workspaces](<https://linear.app/docs/workspaces>)
  How to configure settings and workflows 

Teams are how you organize people and work in Linear.

* [Learn about Teams](<https://linear.app/docs/teams>)

issues.title: T012 — RLS helper functions + policies (verbatim 8.4)
issues.description:
PASS (1st attempt, clean, no findings): all three PRD 8.4 helper functions (`auth_role`, `is_staff`, `my_student_ids`) confirmed byte-verbatim via SHA-256 checksum match, not just eyeballed diff; all 14 T009/T010/T011 tables confirmed RLS-enabled with at least one real policy each — zero gaps; grep-swept every `create policy` statement and confirmed no self-referential same-table subqueries anywhere (all role/ownership checks route through the three security-definer helpers or safe cross-table subqueries only — e.g. an `events` policy subquerying `students`, never `events` itself). The `profiles.role::text` cast fix (needed because `auth_role()` returns `text` but `profiles.role` is `role_enum`) was independently reproduced as genuinely necessary: uncast form throws `operator does not exist: role_enum = text` on a live scratch Postgres, cast form works, and `auth_role()`'s own body confirmed untouched from ground truth — cast lives only in the policy. Two flagged deviations both adjudicated on the merits, not rubber-stamped: (1) Trap 1 — `students` "teammate visibility for leaderboard" deliberately scoped down to `staff_all` + `own_or_linked_read` only, gap explicitly deferred to T013's views; confirmed intentional and correctly reasoned, not a defect. (2) Trap 2 — `events`/`event_sessions` team-scope policy moved the `team_ids is null` check *inside* the cross-table `exists()` against `students` rather than a standalone top-level `OR`, so an authenticated session with zero linked `students`/`guardian_links` rows (including a bare orphan `auth.users` row with no `profiles` row) sees zero events rather than leaking every globally-scoped ("all teams") event; independently re-tested on a fresh scratch Postgres and confirmed correct — orphan sessions get 0 rows, while student1/parent1 still see both their own team's event and the all-teams event (2/2). Checker gave an explicit reasoned verdict that this is the security-correct default-deny posture per constitution item 4 (no links = no scope), not an over-restriction, even though it also denies a hypothetical "real profile, zero links yet" onboarding-lag edge case PRD 8.3 doesn't explicitly address. `teams`/`seasons` (`read_all` authenticated + staff writes) and `guardian_links` (`staff_all` + `own_read` via `parent_profile_id`/`my_student_ids()`) interpretations — both outside the literal 8.3 matrix — judged reasonable, spirit-consistent defaults, not disputes. T009/T010/T011 migration files confirmed zero diff (constitution item 10); no service-role keys/secrets in the file; no forbidden-file violations. Full evidence includes real scratch-Postgres commands/output for anon, orphan-authenticated, student1, parent1, and admin/coach sessions across `students`/`attendance`/`events`/`event_sessions`/`profiles`/`notification_prefs`/`calendar_feeds`, plus a `profiles` role-escalation block-attempt test and a no-infinite-recursion confirmation across every role type. See `docs/swarm/verification-log.md` T012 entry for full detail and `docs/swarm/archive/T012-worker-packet.md` / `docs/swarm/archive/T012-checker-packet.md` for the complete packets.

issues.title: T019 — DB trigger: invite acceptance → profile/link
issues.description:
PASS (1st attempt, MINOR finding, non-blocking — critical-path task, everything downstream in E4/E5/E6 depends on this): new additive migration `20260718000000_invite_trigger.sql`. Resolves T009's `profiles.avatar_url` nullability gap (dropped NOT NULL). `fn_handle_invite_acceptance()` (SECURITY DEFINER, same pattern as T011's audit triggers) + `AFTER UPDATE ON auth.users` trigger, WHEN-gated on the OR of two independent NULL→NOT-NULL transitions (`email_confirmed_at`, `last_sign_in_at`) — chosen specifically because `inviteUserByEmail` (T017) runs at invite-SEND time, so a naive INSERT trigger would fire too early; `encrypted_password` explicitly rejected as a signal since OAuth-only accounts never set it. Checker independently stood up its own scratch Postgres with its own fixtures and re-ran all 6 scenarios (student invite, parent multi-invite-row per ROS-05, idempotent re-fire via the *other* signal, no-invite no-op, expired-invite no-op, admin invite) plus 3 adversarial probes of its own devising: a role-leak probe (confirmed `raw_user_meta_data.role` is genuinely ignored, `invites.role` is the sole source), a WHEN-gate probe (confirmed the trigger does not fire early on unrelated `auth.users` updates), and a display_name-fallback probe. Checker rendered an explicit, weighed severity verdict on the signal-choice design (not a rubber stamp): false-positive risk judged negligible (any real transition IS a sign-in event, and the `status='pending' and expires_at>now()` guard backstops anything unrelated), false-negative risk judged low (both columns would need to be pre-populated at invite-send time for the OR to miss, contradicting `inviteUserByEmail`'s documented starting state), no real concurrency race (per-row AFTER UPDATE serializes on the row lock, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` is an independent backstop) — explicitly concluded this does NOT warrant boss-arbiter escalation, since there's no demonstrable failure mode and the only residual is unverifiable live-GoTrue behavior, the same already-accepted structural limitation as T015/T017/T032. Constitution item 10 confirmed via content-diff of all 5 pre-existing migrations (identical, additive-only). Role provenance independently grepped and adversarially tested. `avatar_url` nullability change confirmed to collide with no other insert path (only insert-into-profiles site in real source is this trigger). D001-method forbidden-file check clean. Two NITs (display_name email-local-part fallback, guardian_links.relationship='guardian' literal) — both clearly disclosed placeholders, not spec-derived truth, accepted as-is. issues.title: T131 — W5-P2b: compact icon-pair row actions — resolve T130's carried MINOR (420px actions column / ~42px internal scroll)

The BLOCKER was self-contradiction: "every interactive control ≥44px" became unsatisfiable the moment the title turned into a link, since a 44px title line box breaches the same packet's 72px row ceiling. The highest-value MAJOR: the packet prescribed nesting `<Text>` inside `Link`, but `Link` already wraps children in its own `Text` (`Link.tsx:323-331`) and forwards typography props — nesting silently defeats truncation, and `LinkProps.color` defaults to `'accent'`, which would have turned every event title purple while the packet's own criteria never checked colour. Also false: the claim that `style` is documented on Button/IconButton (it appears in exactly 7 props tables, none of them Button/IconButton/Link; `astryx-api.md:1116` is **Field**) — reframed as an installed-source-verified D004 deviation, which is what T130 had actually relied on. Implementation resolves UXC-02 fully: link moved onto the event title (`Link` with `weight="semibold" maxLines={1} color="primary"`, no `aria-label`), Cancel → destructive `IconButton icon="close"` with verbatim `label` + tooltip, actions column `pixel(420)`→`pixel(128)`. **Checker reproduced every number and measured the baseline the worker had carried forward from a comment rather than rendered**: scroll wrapper 1132/1174 → **1132/1132** on both tables, `<th>` widths 120/150/**474**/102/158/**128** summing to exactly 1132 — the ~42px internal scroll is gone. Rows 52.5–69px (≤72px); expander 101.81×44, Edit 48.13×44, `×` 44×44, identical at 375px. Title typography byte-identical at rest (weight 600, 14px, lh 20.0004px, `rgb(29,26,33)`, nowrap/ellipsis/hidden) — the `Text.tsx:165,226` prediction that `color="primary"` reproduces the default exactly held. Checker additionally **stress-tested truncation** the worker left unexercised (920px title into a 458px box: anchor does not overflow, wrapper stays 1132). Exactly one assertion changed, and it was **strengthened** (`toContain('View details')`→`toBe('Community Food Bank Sort')`); zero `.skip`/`.only`/`.todo` anywhere in the repo. 1414/1414, all gates green. issues.title: T133 — W5-P3b: calendar craft pass — UXC-04 title-as-link, UXC-01 labelled region, UXC-06 cap+centre
issues.description:
**PASS on attempt 1** (MINOR, NIT x3). Premise gate ran **three** rounds — the third explicitly authorized by the human owner past item 19a's two-round cap, and it earned its keep. Round 1 carried a BLOCKER: the packet prescribed dropping `List header` and keeping the `Heading`, which is none of PRD UXC-01's three authorized remedies and is **the exact approach T129 failed attempt 1 on** — `List` sets `aria-labelledby` only when `header` is non-null and has no rest spread, so dropping it removes the list's only accessible name and it cannot be re-labelled. The packet cited T129 by name and reached the opposite conclusion. Round 2 found the underlying premise false too (the `Heading` is inside the zero-session ternary, so the page has two empty states, not one) and that `maxWidth` caps without centring — no auto margin anywhere in `Stack`/`Center` — so the prescription could not satisfy its own criterion. Round 3 **measured** the corrected two-layer shape working. Checker verified the name relocated rather than being lost, and confirmed the packet's selector-scoping warning was real: Chromium shows two `role="group"` nodes with SideNav's first, so a bare `querySelector` verifies the wrong element. UXC-06 measured: 1120px content in an 1180px parent, 30px each side, `SegmentedControl` 1132px→320px; `scrollWidth === innerWidth` at 375px in all three branches incl. a synthetic 140-char title. Checker closed a gap the worker guessed at: 375px row heights [257,257,317,297]→[57,57,77,77], caused by deleting the long wrapping link, not the "pre-existing description wrapping" the worker assumed. **Checker's own first run would have been a MAJOR failure** — it traced that to its rig omitting `theme.css`, fixed it, re-ran, and the worker's figures reproduced exactly. **MINOR carried:** UXC-01 ships with no regression test; the packet contradicted itself (criterion 4 said assert, criterion 10 pinned the count) and the worker resolved toward the count. 1440/62, one assertion amended and strengthened to exact match. issues.title: T135 — W5-P4: MeetingsList coach rows → Astryx `Table` (UXC-02/03/07)
issues.description:
**PASS on attempt 1** (NIT x3 + one process MINOR). Strongest result of the wave. Premise gate ran two rounds and returned **2 BLOCKERs + 2 MAJORs on round 1, all orchestrator errors.** BLOCKER 1 was the subtlest defect this process has caught: the packet's remedy for `:842` was "add an expand step", which cannot work, because confirming a cancel flips the session status, `partitionCoachMeetingRows` recomputes, and the row **moves from the Upcoming section to the Past section** — so with T130's per-section expansion state the Past copy renders collapsed regardless. The gate's fix was also *cheaper*: lift the state to `CoachMeetingsView`, which additionally fixes a real bug T130 does not have (the coach silently loses their expanded row at the moment they cancel its last session). BLOCKER 2: nine breaking assertions across three tests, not three in one — two tests unmentioned, one of which *throws* rather than failing, since `clickButton(undefined)` is called on a button that no longer exists when collapsed. Round 2 established the list is **exhaustive** by extracting all 49 asserted strings in the coach tests and confirming exactly seven vanish under splicing. MAJORs: the fixture is 2 Upcoming / 0 Past, so four criteria demanded cross-section measurements no checker could take; and removing the per-row `MoreMenu` deviates from PRD MTG-01 — **George authorized it**, recorded beside MTG-01 in the PRD, and the packet then had to mandate amending `:791`, which would otherwise have passed while asserting an affordance that no longer exists. **The checker mutated the source three times rather than reading it:** injecting per-section state failed exactly `:842`, proving the placement load-bearing; renaming the hours label to `Planned` failed `:558`, proving that assertion is satisfied by the `StatCell` label and not the badge behind the expander; and running the old `:791` body against new source showed it passing vacuously while the new body failed when the Edit chip returned `null`. It also drove the cancel→re-partition flow in real Chromium and confirmed the row stays expanded with `aria-controls` resolving. Measurements reproduced to the same precision: `<th>` widths `[170,200,394,130,158,80]` = **exactly 1132**, wrapper `clientWidth === scrollWidth === 1132`, collapsed rows **69 / 68.5** against the 72px ceiling, all targets ≥44px, 375px `scrollWidth === innerWidth` before *and* after. Fourteen assertion changes, no fifteenth; test names byte-identical; all seven pure-function helpers proven byte-identical by programmatic extraction. Expander kept `Session details (N)` and measured one line in a 139.17px button inside a 170px column. ESLint 352→**353** warnings (one new `react-refresh` from added exported helpers), 0 errors. **Process MINOR:** the worker built from packet revision 2 while revision 3 — the commit carrying the corrected ruling — landed after its merge; it reached the right answer on its own reasoning but its output doc claims provenance it does not have. Standing fix recorded: pin the packet SHA in every dispatch. Worker packet archived at `docs/swarm/archive/T135-worker-packet.md`.

issues.title: T137 — W5-P5: stop calendar meeting rows linking to a route that does not exist (D009)
issues.description:
**PASS on attempt 1** (MINOR x2 + NIT x2), and the first packet this wave a worker read without finding a factual error in it. `detailHrefFor` returned `/meetings/${session.id}` for every meeting-type calendar row; that route is absent from `router.tsx`, which has **no catch-all**, and no meeting-detail component exists anywhere. Pre-existing (T112 built the link) but **T133 promoted it from a secondary "View details" link to the row title itself**, making a dead end each row's primary affordance. George chose option (b) — interim destination now, NAV-08's real detail page as its own task. Premise gate ran two rounds, **both findings orchestrator errors**. Round 1 MAJOR: the packet claimed the regex mismatch at `:487` would make the test "pass vacuously" — **false**, because `:489` (`toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4)`) sits between the filter and the loop, so it fails loudly instead. The gate's insight was the dangerous part: left unnamed, `:489` falls under criterion 7 as an unreported regression, and the worker's likeliest repair is weakening it to `>= 2` — *manufacturing the exact vacuity the packet existed to prevent*. Named as a sixth authorized site with "tighten, don't relax" guidance. Round 2 then caught that my corrected snippet **did not compile**: `links` is an `HTMLAnchorElement[]`, so comparing an element to `routePaths.meetings` is TS2367 and evaluates to `0` — verified by probe, not inferred. Also corrected: `routePaths.meetings` is `router.tsx:165` not `:164`; NAV-08 is PRD `:97` not `:89` (my own D009 annotation had displaced it); Trap 3's ternary spans `:492-496` not `:492-494`. **The checker proved the defect rather than describing it.** It mounted the real `AppRoutes` in jsdom and let the lazy chunks resolve: `/meetings` and `/outreach/:eventId` both render live components, while the **old href produced literally empty** `innerHTML` — no catch-all, blank page confirmed. It then dispatched a real click on the meeting-row anchor and landed on `MeetingsList`, and enumerated all four rendered anchors including the `competition`-type event routing through the `else` branch. **Both assertion changes mutation-tested.** Reverting the meeting branch leaves `expect(links.length).toBe(4)` *passing* — it is the worker's **added** meeting-share count that catches it, so the tightening is load-bearing rather than decorative. Narrowing the regex back fails the count loudly, satisfying criterion 5's "a future narrowing must fail the count". Both files restored and hash-verified. Zero-line diff on `router.tsx` — no stub route added. Three files touched, all Allowed. 1440/62 unchanged, 31 `it(` blocks at base and head, eslint 0 errors / 353 warnings. `void session;` verified correct rather than assumed: `tsconfig.json:18` sets `noUnusedParameters`, eslint has no unused-vars rule, and the idiom is real at both cited sites; dropping the parameter would have required editing a forbidden call site. **MINORs fixed by the orchestrator post-check** (doc-only, unreviewed, disclosed): the PRD NAV-08 annotation still said "awaiting George's decision" and asserted the rows "navigate to a blank page", and dispute-log D009 still carried the a11y claim packet revision 3 had explicitly retracted — corrected to record that both fixture meeting rows always shared one accessible name, so the change moves them from identical-name/different-destination (WCAG 2.4.4 violation) to conforming. **NIT, a packet error:** it told the worker to preserve T133's `role="group"` accessible-name assertions; no such assertions exist — that element has no test coverage at base or head. issues.title: T139 — D-2: give `RosterShell` the pass-through props its four tabs + `AdminToggles` already accept
issues.description:
**PASS on attempt 1** (NIT). D-2 said "add an injectable loader seam to `RosterShell`/`StudentsTab`"; inspecting it **shrank the task** — all five children already expose seams (`StudentsTab.tsx:1067`, `ParentsTab.tsx:943`, `TeamsTab.tsx:1104`, `InvitesTab.tsx:707`, `AdminToggles.tsx:318`), and `RosterShell` simply rendered them with no props at all, swallowing every one. Pass-through plumbing, not a new seam. **Premise gate round 1 returned MAJOR, and it disproved the packet's central trap empirically rather than arguing with it.** The packet asserted `AdminToggles` must stay `lazy()`-imported or a three-file cycle `router.tsx -> RosterShell.tsx -> AdminToggles.tsx -> router.tsx` breaks five unrelated suites — quoting module doc #6 as live fact. The gate cut an isolated worktree at the pinned SHA, reverted the import to a static one, and ran the full suite and a build: **zero failures, 62/62, 1440/1440, clean build.** Cause: **T093 (**`d43fb3a`**, a bundle-size fix) had already made** `router.tsx`**'s own import of** `RosterShell` **lazy** (`router.tsx:130`), independently breaking that edge. Same failure mode as T134's two BLOCKERs — trusting a module-doc comment over current code. The gate also found criterion 3 **unsatisfiable**: it told the worker to "name the five cycle-sensitive suites", but only one was ever named in the repo and identifying the rest required the very static-import conversion the packet forbade — an instruction satisfiable only by fabrication. Revision 2 retracts the claim by name, keeps `import type` and `lazy()` for honest reasons (type-only imports are erased here regardless; leaving `lazy()` alone is unrequested-scope avoidance, not risk avoidance), and authorizes correcting the two stale docs. **Checker mutation-tested all five new tests**: deleting each spread in turn killed **exactly one** test, the correct one every time. The `AdminToggles` case — flagged pre-check as the easiest to write vacuously, sitting behind `Suspense fallback={null}` and an admin role gate — fails properly, because the injected loader resolves the opposite value from the module mock and the assertion polls real DOM via `vi.waitFor`. The four tab tests are **two-sided**: each asserts the injected fixture present *and* the default fixture absent. Criterion 2 held exactly: the test file's diff is four hunks — an import, the helper signature, the two renders inside that helper, and a pure append — and **no hunk lands inside any of the 14 original** `it(` **bodies**. The new second parameter defaults to `undefined` rather than `{}`, so the 14 one-argument call sites render identically at runtime. `router.tsx` zero-line diff; **no child component gained a prop**. 1440 -> **1445**, arithmetic closed independently (one test file changed, 14 -> 19). Module docs #3 and #6 corrected rather than opted out of, and the checker specifically confirmed **no overcorrection** — doc #6 presents the cycle as history with mechanism and evidence and justifies `lazy()` as unrequested scope, without claiming the cycle is now impossible. **NIT fixed by the orchestrator post-check** (comment-only, unreviewed, disclosed): doc #6's *heading* line still read "a real, live circular-import bug" forty lines above the UPDATE that retracts it. I re-derived it independently and agreed: chaining the three confines both fills to one narrow luminance band on the same side of the track (light ceiling **3.061:1** only with a literally black fill; dark **3.096:1** only at near-white; **2.988/2.949** once restricted to recognisable green and purple). Revision 3 **withdrew** the demand and replaced it with a visible-boundary requirement satisfied by a 2px divider in the **track colour**, so its contrast follows transitively from the two fill-vs-track measurements. **The checker verified the transitive argument rather than accepting it**: in real Chromium against the *built* stylesheet, track and divider both compute to `rgb(175,169,183)` light and `rgb(74,69,81)` dark — identical, so divider-vs-fill contrast **is** fill-vs-track contrast (3.333/5.473 light, 7.091/4.669 dark, reproduced to three decimals). It also ran a **negative control** on the token work, inserting a custom key and confirming the exact `TS2353` that killed revision 1's prescription, and brace-matched `theme.css` against fresh `astryx theme build` output for an exact string match. **The no-sum invariant holds, proven live rather than read**: `GoalBar` contains **no** `+` **operator in code at all**, and an instrumented render reports `aria-valuenow` **17** on the coach fixture (9 confirmed / 7 planned / goal 52) where a summed bar would report 31. Fill widths render as 17.3077% and 13.4615% — 9/52 and 7/52 computed independently, with the planned fill's `left` being the offset, not a sum. **Four mutations all correctly fail**, including two `borderLeft` framings the checker devised itself to catch a divider that silently shrinks the planned segment. issues.title: T154 — the theme seed is not user-scoped: the previous user's theme on a shared browser
issues.description:
**PASS with MINORs on attempt 2; attempt 1 was FAIL (1 MAJOR).** Merged with all five gates re-measured by the checker at the worker's tree: tsc clean, vite ✓, prettier clean, eslint **0 errors / 355 warnings** (unchanged), vitest **66 files / 1536 tests** (from 1528). Sabotage check clean on both the work commit and the worker's own merge (`deea4ff` touched only its output doc; no ledger, constitution, verification-log or dispute-log path). **Attempt 1's MAJOR, and the reason it existed:** per-uid keying fixed only the *fresh-load* case. The seed is read once per mount, and `logout()` (`guards.tsx:319`) sets `{user: null}` without a reload while `login()` (`:297`) sets the next user — so the ordinary in-app sign-out → sign-in-as-B flow never remounted the provider, and B kept A's theme **persistently**, not for one frame. Shipped source asserted the opposite twice ("moot regardless"). **The orchestrator chose to fix rather than defer** (recorded as the coordinator's override, explicitly **not** George's — his ruling covers the design, not this call) because a persistent wrong theme on a shared machine is the bug the task exists to close, and the remedy is in-memory state in a file already in scope, never touching Forbidden `guards.tsx`. **The orchestrator's prescribed rule was wrong and the worker caught it.** I specified re-seeding only on a non-null → different-non-null `user.id` transition; the real flow is **A → null → B**, so that rule never fires. Both the worker and the checker implemented my literal rule and measured it: **3 failed / 33 passed, with** `re-seeds on a DIRECT Alice → Bob switch` **PASSING** — i.e. my prescription would have shipped a green suite with the MAJOR entirely unfixed, catchable only by the A→null→B test the worker chose to write. Shipped instead: `lastSeededUserId` tracks the last non-null user seeded for, re-seeding during render (React's sanctioned adjust-state-on-input-change, which is what preserves the no-stale-frame property). The checker could not break the three prohibitions across 14 adversarial probes (null flapping, repeated nulls then first user, same-id-new-object, A→B→A, invalid stored value, throwing `getItem` mid-switch, cross-tab broadcast, write-through) and found no render loop. **Disclosed residual, stated in three places and pinned by its own test:** between sign-out and next sign-in the login screen still shows A's theme — resetting on null would fire on every normal page load while the session resolves, re-introducing T148's flash. | No | **Filed as a ledger row rather than a module comment, on the exact reasoning that produced this whole bug class.** `volt.themeMode` is a single browser-scoped key, so if user A sets Dark and signs out, user B's first paint on the same machine may use A's stored value for one frame until B's own `theme_mode` resolves. **Deliberately not fixed.** The obvious remedy — clear on logout — is impossible in scope (`logout()` is at `guards.tsx:311-321`, a Forbidden File) and its only in-scope alternative was gate-proven destructive: clearing whenever `user` is null wipes the seed on every boot while auth resolves, permanently on a rejecting loader, and on any anonymous visit with nothing to restore it. Measured both cases. A one-frame theme bleed on a shared machine is strictly better than silently breaking the feature for everyone. Recorded so a future reader finds a decision rather than an oversight — which is precisely what T101, T121 and `SettingsPage` did NOT do, and why George hit three production bugs in one afternoon. **Revision 2 (foreman-planner, 2026-07-30):** adopts the checker-premise gate's [CP1] — the app now owns `SUPABASE_AUTH_STORAGE_KEY` via `client.ts`'s one `createClient(..., {auth:{storageKey}})` call rather than deriving `supabase-js`'s internal default, closing a fail-dangerous orphaned-key branch the gate measured (`auto-mode-decisions.md`, "2026-07-30 — T154: adopting the app-owned storage key…"). Tier bumped sonnet→opus (item 18: this is now real auth configuration). [CP2]'s drift detector is dropped as unnecessary — nothing is derived, so nothing can drift. Fixed a citation error carried from revision 1: the existing-tests non-negotiable is `constitution.md:10`, not `:11` (**this sentence was itself backwards until 2026-07-30, when the audit session caught it: it asserted** `:11` **was the correction when** `:11` **is "No worker may mark its own work complete" and** `:10` **is the existing-tests rule — the ledger's own account of fixing a citation error was the surviving instance of it, even though** `T154-worker-output.md:477` **had it right**), and the authorization to rewrite the four affected tests is the orchestrator's own delegated authority, not George's — his ruling covers the design, not the test files. issues.title: T157 — `ParentRsvp` is fully built and mounted nowhere — render it in `OutreachDetail.tsx`, per the owner's ruling
issues.description:
**PASS, merged.** Packet revision 2 cleared **gate round 2 → DISPATCH** (5 MINOR, 4 NIT, no BLOCKER, no MAJOR); all nine round-2 findings folded into the packet before dispatch. Worker opus/worktree, checker `checker-reviewer` opus. Shipped: `profile_id` threaded through `StudentDbRow`/`queryAllStudents`/`mapStudentDbRowToRosterStudent`; new `makeLoadGuardianLinksForParent` — **the only** `guardian_links` **read in the repo that selects** `relationship` (`parents.ts:190`, `checkin.ts:399`, `meetings.ts:510` all omit it), filtered `.eq('parent_profile_id',…)` server-side; `isParentViewer` gate; a `GuardianLinksLoadState` seam fetched only for parents; the new pure `resolveParentLinkedRosterStudents` composed over the team-scoped `roster`; one `<ParentRsvp>` per (session × linked student) with real `currentUserProfileId`/`studentProfileId`/`guardianLinks`. `GuardianLinkRow` reused from `ParentRsvp.tsx` per §6c. Measured: tsc exit 0, `vite build` ✓, vitest **1546 → 1567** (+21 = 17 + 4 new tests, zero baseline broken), eslint 0 errors / 355→356 warnings (+1 = `react-refresh/only-export-components` on the new exported pure function, matching this file's own convention). **The checker independently re-executed all nine prescribed mutations plus four supplementary ones — none was unexecutable** — reducing multi-line deletions to equivalent single-line edits. Two confirmations worth keeping: criterion 2a's two cases are **measurably non-redundant** (dropping the `parentProfileId` predicate fails *only* case 2, 1 failed / 59 passed) and case 1's exact-array `toEqual` is load-bearing (`toContain` would have passed); and criterion 4's omitted-prop mutation writes `respondedBy: 'profile-placeholder-current-parent'` into `rsvps.responded_by`, a column that `references public.profiles (id)` — a plausible row attributed to a nonexistent profile, which is exactly the defect class this task closes. The checker also ran its own vacuity probes on criteria 3 and 8 and found neither vacuous, confirming the gate's MINOR-5 correction (parent viewer starts in `loading`, not `idle`) is correct and not merely present. **Non-Negotiable #2 verified by diff, not by count:** six removed lines total across all three source files, five of them fixture literals gaining `profileId` at the ten sites §6a authorizes; no existing `it(` body modified; the `vi.mock`/`afterEach` edits are pure additions. **One MINOR, fixed at merge, not deferred:** `npm run format:check` regressed from clean to failing on two prettier deviations in the new test file (a type-annotation wrap and a quote style); `npm run format` applied at merge, gate restored to clean, suite re-verified 1567 green. **One packet error, correctly flagged not followed:** §8 criterion 4 prescribed a `submitRsvpChange` mock returning an `RsvpRow`, but `SubmitRsvpChangeFn` is `(params) => Promise<void>`; the worker used `vi.fn(async () => {})` and the checker confirmed the packet was wrong. **Orchestrator dispatch error, recorded against this task:** the worker's worktree was created from `f7ff055` (main) rather than the branch tip, so it began against **revision 1** — the version that gated REVISE with 4 MAJORs. Caught mid-task and corrected; the worker discarded ~320 lines and rewrote against revision 2 rather than salvaging, which was right on the merits (rev 1 would have declared a third `GuardianLinkRow`, collided with `checkin.ts`'s query name, used a name-only heading, and written `currentUserProfileId={user.id}` behind a non-narrowing gate that would not have compiled). Follow-ups filed as **T174**/**T175**. **Round-1 gate history below.** **GATE ROUND 1 (2026-07-30,** `checker-premise` **at** `0b932d0`**): REVISE.** Round 2 of 2 remains available under item 19a. **The four MAJORs:** (1) the packet says worker tier **sonnet** with a four-point argument that item 18 does not fire, while this very row says **opus** — a dispatcher reads the packet, so the contradiction must be resolved; the gate agrees with opus and argues item 18's trigger 4 ("permission logic") is *arguable*, not clearly non-firing, since the task adds a role gate and a new client-side authorization predicate over minors' family linkage. (2) **No criterion detects a broken cross-family scoping filter** — the gate traced a mutation removing `linkedStudentIds.has(student.id)` against all six criteria and every one still passes, and the same holds for the team-scope half; the file's own convention gives dedicated describe blocks to both comparable pure functions and the packet breaks it for the one with a security rationale. (3) **Criterion 3 self-expires on 2026-08-02** — no `now` seam is prescribed, so `ParentRsvp` uses the real clock; `isRsvpEditable` locks once `now >= session.startsAt`, `handleChange` early-returns when locked, and the fixture sessions start 2026-08-02/08-09 (`park-cleanup` at 2026-07-26 is **already locked**), so the criterion goes permanently red in three days with no code change and criterion 8 would then report a false regression. (4) **§7c's four-state machine has zero criteria, and §12 contradicts §10** — §12 cites item 12 to make loading/error/retry/empty all mandatory while §10 waives the empty state. **The BLOCKER the orchestrator hypothesized does NOT hold, and the gate measured rather than assumed it:** `students`' `own_or_linked_read` policy (`rls.sql:101-103`) is `id in (select my_student_ids())`, so `queryAllStudents` is already server-scoped to the parent's own linked students, and `rsvps`' `own_or_linked_write`/`own_or_linked_update` (`:205-212`) require `student_id in (select my_student_ids()) and responded_by = auth.uid()`. A wrong client-side filter therefore cannot surface or write another family's data — §7d is defence-in-depth, not the primary control. The criteria gap stands as MAJOR; cross-family exposure does not. **TWO ORCHESTRATOR ERRORS CORRECTED HERE, both stated confidently to the owner before being checked.** (a) This row and the dispatch brief both claimed *"the repo's only* `guardian_links` *query,* `parents.ts:190`*"*. **There are three read queries**: `parents.ts:190` (`select('id, parent_profile_id, student_id')`), `checkin.ts:398` (`select('student_id')`) and `meetings.ts:509` (`select('student_id')` + `.limit(1)`), plus a delete at `parents.ts:252`. The *conclusion* survives and is in fact strengthened — **none of the three selects** `relationship`, so none can be reused as-is, and three separate casts against one table each able to hide a column omission is the T146 81-cast class in miniature. (b) The brief cited `ParentRsvp.tsx:334-335` for the required props; those lines are `resolveRsvpResponderAttribution`'s **parameter list**. The props are at `:467` and `:481`. Line numbers were taken from grep output without checking which construct they belonged to — the same failure mode as the `:2396`/`:2320` and `:1392-1397`/`:1391-1396` errors on T155. The foreman's symbol-based citation was correct and the line-based brief was not, which is `architecture-review-parallelism.md` §3.1's argument arriving as evidence. **Three cheaper paths the gate found:** import the already-**exported** `GuardianLinkRow` from `ParentRsvp.tsx` (`:258-263`) instead of declaring a third structurally identical copy; extract T146's `parseSelectedColumns` (`outreach.test.ts:29-33`) rather than reimplement it, since T161's row already names T157 as the second call site that decision was waiting for; and use `checkin.ts:393-403` as the structural template rather than `meetings.ts`, whose query is `.limit(1)`-shaped. Also: `checkin.ts:393` already **owns the name** `queryGuardianLinksForParent` that §6d prescribes, and T165 will extend the same `outreach.test.ts` — an unflagged future conflict. **Dispatch-design error, mine, worth recording for the architecture review:** the gate was instructed to run all six prescribed mutations, but `checker-premise` has no Write or Edit tool and the sandbox refused every file-creation route, so it could only apply single-line `perl -pi` changes. It measured §6a's exact 10-site blast radius and §6b's additive-select no-op that way, and stated the rest as reasoned-from-measured-source rather than claiming execution. **Asking a read-only role to build a prescription is not a task it can do**; either grant write-in-own-worktree for round 2 or require the worker's executed failure output with the opus checker re-running each. **Authority scoping was graded exemplary** — the packet attributes only the host screen to George and explicitly disclaims the rest; no promotion finding. **SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-07-30 by** `foreman-planner`**, against this row's own assertion and the orchestrator's framing.** **OWNER RULING (**`auto-mode-decisions.md`**, "2026-07-30 — George's rulings on T157/T158", verbatim: "ParentRsvp in OutreachDetail"):** host `ParentRsvp` in `OutreachDetail.tsx`. This matches the component's own doc comment (`ParentRsvp.tsx:113`), so the ruling confirms the code's stated intent rather than choosing against it. **SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-07-30 by** `foreman-planner`**, against this row's own assertion and the orchestrator's framing.** Both said "no loader work is needed — placement plus data threading". **That is true only for the RSVP *write* path and false for the *read* side.** Verified here: `ParentRsvp.tsx:334-335` requires `studentProfileId: string | null` and `guardianLinks: readonly GuardianLinkRow[]`, and neither has any data source in `OutreachDetail.tsx` or `loaders/outreach.ts` — `RosterStudent` has no `profileId`, `queryAllStudents` never selects `profile_id` (zero `profile_id` hits in `outreach.ts`), and nothing under `loaders/outreach.ts` queries `guardian_links` at all. The component's own doc comment (`:114-115`) says the host must pass each student's `studentProfileId`/`guardianLinks` slice and that it was "not built here". **Sharper than the foreman put it:** the only existing `guardian_links` query in the repo, `parents.ts:190`, selects `id, parent_profile_id, student_id` — it omits `relationship`, which `ParentRsvp` needs for its "{relationship} signed you up" line. So the existing query cannot simply be reused, and the failure mode of getting it wrong is precisely the T143/T146 class: a select string missing a column the UI needs, with a green suite. The packet prescribes the bounded loader addition rather than leaving the worker to fabricate the values or fall back to fixture defaults — which would have reproduced the exact defect family this task exists to close. **Tier raised sonnet→opus by the orchestrator (a judgement call, not an item 18 trigger — item 18 does not fire since no migration, RLS authoring, metric SQL, or auth/role-resolution change is involved):** the new query reads parent-child linkage for minors, so an incorrect filter exposes one family's data to another. Recorded as the orchestrator's decision, not the owner's. **Scope narrowed on that ruling:** `RsvpControl` **is split out to T169 and is NOT in this task** — the owner named `ParentRsvp` only, and inferring the student control's host would be a fourth authority-promotion incident. Everything beyond placement (loader design, test shape) is the orchestrator's call, not his. **Source: external audit session, branch** `claude/loader-tests-audit-inbox` **@** `2ec47d8`**, based on** `af28914`**; folded in by the orchestrator. Independently re-verified here, measured, not relayed.** `RsvpControl.tsx` and `ParentRsvp.tsx` are each imported by **exactly one file — their own test** (`RsvpControl.test.tsx:33`, `ParentRsvp.test.tsx:34`); zero production importers, zero JSX renders anywhere outside tests. **This is a wiring gap, not unfinished logic, and that is what makes it the more serious of the two:** the mutation path is real and Supabase-backed (`makeSubmitRsvpChange` at `loaders/outreach.ts:929`, `submitRsvpChange` at `:953`), and `outreach.ts:108` states both `RsvpControl.tsx`'s and `ParentRsvp.tsx`'s flows use it. `RsvpControl` even exports a default (`:560`). The codebase's own comments treat these as the canonical flow that other components deliberately do not duplicate (`OutreachList.tsx:3565`, `OutreachDetail.tsx`, `MarkDayCompleteDialog.tsx`) — and `ParentRsvp.tsx:113` says `OutreachDetail.tsx` "is expected to render one `<ParentRsvp>` per linked" student, which it does not. So OUT-03 has no reachable self-service RSVP UI for students or parents at all, while its tests pass. **Why every gate missed it:** nothing in this project asserts reachability. A component's own test file is an importer, so "is it used" greps clean, and a green suite says the component works without saying anyone can get to it. Same class as CoachHome's unwired widgets, but for a whole feature area. **Needs the owner:** which screen hosts `RsvpControl` (a student-facing outreach/event screen per PRD OUT-03) is not recoverable from code.

Scope narrowed to the real loader + a new supporting migration only — the embed half is **T203**. **Heaviest gate history this session: hit item 19a's 2-round cap twice on one packet, each escalation owner-authorized.** The RLS/view-visibility mechanism at this task's core — that `students` has no `read_all` policy and a new view is needed for the leaderboard to work for non-staff viewers at all — was **empirically verified live, twice during gating and a third time by the checker independently reproducing its own from-scratch harness**, via `@electric-sql/pglite` (an in-process WASM Postgres, no Docker/server needed). Every measurement matched: a `student`-role session sees only its own row on the base table, all active students' names/hours through the new view and `v_student_hours`, a deactivated student excluded, and a `security_invoker=on` negative control collapsing both back to 1 row — with a deliberate non-vacuity self-test (reproducing an incomplete RLS setup) confirming the harness would have caught its own round-2 false positive. **Checker found one genuinely new thing, MINOR, not a defect in what shipped:** the new view is also readable by Supabase's fully **unauthenticated** `anon` key (which ships in the public frontend bundle), not just logged-in users — measured live, and confirmed the first view in this schema to expose `display_name`. This is a different threat model than T185's "any authenticated caller can read hours" ruling (item 25), so not extended to it without asking. Filed as **T205**, routed to the owner rather than decided unilaterally. **SCOPE NARROWED AT PACKETING TIME (foreman-planner, 2026-07-31): this row now covers ONLY the real loader + its supporting migration** (`docs/swarm/active/T158-worker-packet.md`). The "embed in `CoachHome`" half is split out as its own follow-up, **T203** (below), because it needs its own investigation (a real `Section`-nesting CSS hazard in `CoachHome.tsx`, and two different test-file fixes) and because item 18's migration trigger forces this row to opus/full-gate regardless — bundling a sonnet-shaped UI-wiring task into it would cost that tier for no benefit to the UI half. Mirrors every prior split this session (T155→T173, T157→T169, T173→T198). **Real finding that reshapes the loader design, not anticipated by this row's original text:** `students` has no `read_all` RLS policy (`rls.sql:82-102` — only `staff_all` and `own_or_linked_read`), and `Leaderboard.tsx` deliberately has no role gate at all (module doc #6 — visible to every role, OUT-08). A naive loader copying `coachHome.ts`'s plain `.from('students').select(...)` would RLS-filter a student/parent viewer down to at most their own row while a staff viewer saw everyone — the exact role-dependent silent-breakage class this project keeps finding, here caused by schema, not a missing prop. `rls.sql:90-92` and `student_teams.sql:47-53` both independently name the fix already: a **view**, not a table-policy change — the packet builds exactly that (`v_leaderboard_students`, two columns, `where is_active`, no metric math). **MERGED,** `OutreachDetail` **half only.** Worker commit `7647820dab68cd89c5077faa5aa437219cc77dfa` (on packet-pin `9dd4e1f`, itself on `de6ae13`). Two NIT, log-only, no fix required: an unguarded optional-chain in the clock-seam test (not currently vacuous, mutation-proven RED, but could silently pass-through if the locator ever returned `null`) and a substring (`toContain('Attendance')`) rather than structural positive control for the coach/admin role-gate cases. **Worker's own worktree started stale** (cut from `main` at `f7ff055`, 24 commits behind the packet commit — the exact item-24 failure mode T157 was burned by) **and the worker caught it itself** before writing any code, verified via `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, fast-forwarded to the packet-pin commit, and disclosed the deviation in its output rather than silently proceeding or silently staying stale. **Follow-up filed: T193** (the `OutreachList.tsx` student-facing half — silent-data-loss bug, now unblocked since T170 merged, previously described as blocked in this row's own now-superseded text below). **Superseded history retained verbatim beneath, for provenance — the ruling and the original problem statement are unchanged; only the sequencing/scope claims in it are stale (see T193).** **OWNER RULING (**`auto-mode-decisions.md`**, "2026-07-30 — George's ruling on T169", verbatim: "the student can control belong on OutreachDetail alongside the parent's (one screen, role-gated), AND on the student-facing outreach"):** host `RsvpControl` on **both** surfaces — `OutreachDetail.tsx` role-gated beside the parent control, **and** the student-facing outreach view in `OutreachList.tsx`. The two give students materially different flows and the answer is not recoverable from code — `outreach.ts:108` names both components as users of the mutation without saying which screen hosts either.

issues.title: T171 — T154's no-stale-frame property is true in the code and pinned by nothing
issues.description:
**MINOR carried from T154's PASS, measured by the checker and worth more than its grade suggests.** Moving the re-seed out of the render body into a `useEffect` keyed on `[user, lastSeededUserId]` — a change that demonstrably reintroduces a stale frame — leaves **all 36 tests passing**. The property IS true in the shipped code (measured: commits are `["none:dark","user-bob:light"]` shipped vs `["none:dark","user-bob:dark","user-bob:light"]` under the mutation, the middle entry being Bob signed in with Alice's theme still on screen), but nothing would notice if it broke. **Two independent causes, both instructive.** (1) `RecordingProbe` consumes only `useThemeMode()`, and the provider's `useMemo(() => ({mode, refresh}), [mode, refresh])` memoizes the consumer away when `user` changes but `mode` does not — so a stale commit is structurally invisible to it. Only a **dual-context** recorder (`useThemeMode()` **and** `useAuth()`) can see it. (2) The test literally named `the stale theme never reaches the DOM even for one frame during the switch` does `renders.slice(beforeSwitch).filter((m) => m !== 'dark')` and asserts on the survivors — **it filters out the very value it should assert absent**, so `['dark','light']` passes. **This is the round-1 failure shape recurring inside the one test written to prevent it**, which is why it is filed rather than logged. Fix: dual-context recorder asserting `not.toContain('user-bob:dark')` on commits after the switch, and drop the `.filter`. Acceptance: moving the re-seed into a `useEffect` must fail the suite; it currently does not. The checker also corrected itself here — its own first strict `not.toContain('dark')` probe reported no stale frame under the mutation and was worthless for the same structural reason.

issues.title: T172 — make the placeholder-default class structurally hard to reintroduce, instead of sweeping for it forever
issues.description:
**Filed 2026-07-30 because the owner caught the orchestrator treating "audit the class" and "fix the class" as one thing.** T168 finds instances; T151/T155/T158/T159/T170 fix individual instances; **nothing yet stops the sixth pattern becoming a seventh.** Every instance has the identical shape — an optional prop, a plausible fixture default, and a call site that passes nothing — and it has produced **three of the owner's four production bugs**, plus two more found only by audit. The instance-by-instance approach cannot converge: `src/pages/**` and `src/components/**` are still unswept, and a new component added tomorrow can reintroduce it with a green suite. **Candidate mechanisms, to be chosen in the packet, not here.** (a) A lint rule or `tsc`-level check flagging an optional prop whose default is a module-level fixture constant — cheap, mechanical, runs on every commit, and directly encodes the discriminator. (b) Generalise T151: make these props **required** wherever a fixture default exists, which the T151 probe measured as far cheaper than feared (34 TS2741 errors, **zero in production source**, all in two test files) — the compiler then enforces it permanently. (c) Naming convention plus a grep gate, weakest of the three. **Prefer (b) then (a):** (b) is enforcement by the type system rather than by a convention someone must remember, and today's measurement shows the cost is a test-file change, not a refactor. **A fourth shape, found during T176:** the same *metric* coalesce is duplicated in TypeScript in **four** places (`StudentHome.tsx:815`, `HoursTab.tsx:449`, `csvExport.test.ts:372`, `CoachHome.tsx:979 sumGoalHours`) against **one** SQL definition in `v_student_goal_projection`. T176's MAJOR was one instance of exactly this, and consolidating the four is the general form of that fix. **Sequenced after T151** so the pattern is proven on three real dialogs before being generalised, and after T168 so the true instance count is known rather than estimated. issues.title: T188 — two different "confirmed hours" numbers exist in the app and can legitimately disagree
issues.description:
**Found while verifying T170's constitution-item-3 question; not a T170 defect and not blocking it.** `v_student_hours` (`metric_views.sql:3-19`) computes confirmed hours from `attendance` — real check-in/check-out timestamps, `status in ('present','late')`, joined to completed sessions on events that count volunteer hours. `computeStudentHours` (`OutreachList.tsx:1184-1203`) computes them from **RSVP status** `going` on a session whose status is `completed`, and never touches `attendance` at all. **These answer different questions** — "did they show up and check in" versus "did they say they were going and did the session happen" — so item 3 is not violated and T170 is unblocked. **But a student who RSVPs** `going` **and does not attend accrues hours on** `/outreach` **and none in** `v_student_hours`, so the same student can see two different hour totals on two screens. `computeStudentHours`'s heuristic is disclosed (BEH-02), so this is a deliberate design that has drifted rather than a bug — but nothing reconciles the two, and the owner is the one who would field the question. Cheap to resolve: either name them differently on screen, or make the outreach page read the attendance-backed number. **DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-05 — validity confirmed, scope is WIDER than filed. No code changed.** **A hypothesis worth killing first:** T201 (merged same day) fixed a two-numbers-disagree bug in the same family, so it might have dissolved this. **It did not** — T201 was roster filtering (`is_active`); T188 is RSVP-vs-attendance. Different mechanism entirely; checked before any work. **The row's own finding still holds, verified against current code:** `computeStudentHours` (`OutreachList.tsx`) still computes confirmed hours from RSVP `status = 'going'` + session `status = 'completed'`, and still never touches `attendance`. **But THREE more divergences exist that the row does not name, and two hit NORMAL usage:** **(2)** `hours_override` **is invisible to it.** `v_student_hours` honours it first in its coalesce; `computeStudentHours` uses raw session length, so any coach adjustment diverges. **(3) check-in/check-out clamping is invisible to it.** A student who arrives late or leaves early gets the clamped span in `v_student_hours` and the FULL session length on `/outreach`. Neither number is wrong; nothing on screen says they answer different questions. **(4) it counts NON-OUTREACH events — MEASURED, not inferred.** A probe called `computeStudentHours` with a completed MEETING session and a `going` RSVP: it returned **2.0 confirmed hours**. The function takes only `(studentId, sessions, rsvps)` — it has no access to event `type` or `countsVolunteerHours`, so it CANNOT filter — and `loaders/outreach.ts:739` queries `events` for the season with **no type filter**, with no JS filter between. **This directly contradicts T322's ruling** (*"volunteer hours =* `type = 'outreach'` *ONLY"*), which landed AFTER T188 was filed, so the row could not have known. **Honest limit of the measurement:** the probe proves the FUNCTION counts a meeting and the loader applies no type filter. It does not render the live page, so "a meeting's hours appear on screen for a real user" is inferred from those two facts, not observed. **Owner ruling needed — the row's two suggested fixes point opposite ways:** (a) **name them differently on screen** (cheap, honest, keeps both numbers, but the `/outreach` figure keeps contradicting T322); (b) **make** `/outreach` **read the attendance-backed number** (one number everywhere, but that page's whole purpose is planned-vs-confirmed from RSVPs, which attendance cannot express). **Divergence (4) may be separable from the product question** — making `computeStudentHours` respect `type = 'outreach'` is arguably just conforming to an existing owner ruling rather than a new decision, and could ship without settling (a)/(b).

issues.title: T194 — `SubscribePopover`'s `onResetFeedToken` fabricates a new feed token locally instead of writing one
issues.description:
**Resolved with T195 on** `codex/t195-t194-calendar-feed-lifecycle`**.** The production default now calls `reset_calendar_feed(p_revoke_feed_id)` once through `.rpc(...).single()`. A lost HTTP response triggers an authoritative feed reload, and a second failure hides the possibly stale URL. **Disclosed by T177's worker at both attempts, not discovered separately — filed here so it is tracked once T177's row moves to MERGED rather than left implicit.** `defaultOnResetFeedToken` in `SubscribePopover.tsx` is a `console.warn`-then-fabricate stub: it generates a new token client-side via `crypto.randomUUID()` and returns it as if the reset succeeded, but writes nothing to `calendar_feeds` — so a user who clicks "reset my link" sees a token that will never actually work and, worse, silently invalidates nothing server-side (the old, real token if one ever existed keeps working). Same defect shape T177 just fixed for `loadCalendarFeed` (optional prop, plausible-looking fixture-shaped default, call site passing nothing), one function over in the same component. **Sequencing note, carried from T177's own framing:** this task and **T195** are related but distinct — T195 is "nothing creates a feed row at all"; this task is "the reset action doesn't persist a new one to an existing row." A real fix likely wants a single-transaction RPC (revoke old row + insert new row) rather than two separate client-side calls, per `SubscribePopover.tsx`'s own module doc section 1. Reverted, `MeetingsList.tsx` confirmed byte-identical to `79e159d`. issues.title: T303 — One outreach event reports **`12h recorded`** while the KPI strip on the same screen reports **`Season hours 0.0` / `Outreach 0.0h`**
issues.description:
**Both numbers are correct under their own rule, and they contradict each other in one viewport.** `AttendancePanel.tsx:779-787` computes `eventTotalHours` by reducing `computeSessionAttendanceTotalHours` over `eligibleSessions`**, with no session-status filter at all** — so attendance typed against a still-`scheduled` session counts immediately. `v_student_hours` (`20260717000003_metric_views.sql:16`) joins `event_sessions es on es.id = a.session_id and es.status = 'completed'` — so the same rows contribute nothing to season hours until the day is marked complete. **Reproduction, from the owner's own data:** an event with three sessions dated in the future, hours typed into the attendance panel, shows `12h recorded` on the event while the strip above it shows `Season hours 0.0`, `Outreach 0.0h`, `Events logged 0`, `0% toward season goal`. **Not a T179 regression** — `AttendancePanel`'s badge predates it and T179 added no hours arithmetic. **T179 does make it easier to resolve**, since the completion flow that flips `status` to `completed` is now reachable from the UI for the first time. **Do not just add** `status === 'completed'` **to the badge and call it done.** The open question is which number is wrong: the badge may be right to show what a coach just typed (immediate feedback on unsaved-looking work), in which case the **label** is what lies — `recorded` reads as *counted*. The likely correct fix is wording plus a qualifier (e.g. `12h pending` / `12h recorded · counts when the day is marked complete`), not silently zeroing a coach's visible input. **This needs an owner ruling on which reading is intended before a packet is written**, exactly as T189 did. **Check while scoping** whether `events.counts_volunteer_hours` is a third, independent reason the strip can read 0 — `v_student_hours:17` joins on it, and an event with it false would produce this same screen for a completely different reason. **— CLOSED 2026-07-31.** Owner ruled the number right and only the word wrong: *"12h recorded is right, just fix the wording to say 'scheduled'."* Implemented as a **status-aware noun**, not a literal one-word swap: new exported pure `resolveEventHoursNoun(sessions)` returns `'scheduled'` while any contributing session is still `scheduled`, `'recorded'` once all are `completed`. A blind swap would have moved the lie rather than removed it — once a day IS complete those hours really do reach `v_student_hours`, and calling them *scheduled* would then be the false half. `eventTotalHours`**'s arithmetic is byte-for-byte unchanged.** **Both mutations reproduced by the orchestrator, not relayed:** forcing the noun to `'recorded'` turns **3 of 41** red (both unit branches plus the render-level test); forcing it to `'scheduled'` turns **2 of 41** red. The worker proved only the first — the orchestrator added the reverse, so neither branch rests on an unmutated assertion. Gates re-measured in the shared tree: `tsc` 0, `vite build` ✓, prettier clean, eslint **0 errors / 360 warnings**, vitest **70 files / 1701 tests** (+4), targeted file exit 0. **Disclosed:** warnings rose 359→360 — one further `react-refresh/only-export-components`, the pattern this file already carries many times over, caused solely by adding an export. Zero errors.

issues.title: T304 — An outreach event whose sessions all ran three weeks ago still sits under **Upcoming**
issues.description:
`buildEventGroups` (`OutreachList.tsx:1650-1670`) partitions on **session** `status` **alone and never consults the date**, so an event dated Jul 6–10 was still *Upcoming* on Jul 31. Found by the owner running the app against real data. **He first ruled for a third bucket ("Needs recording"), then reversed** once scoping showed the function has **two** consumers — coach (`:3023`) and student/parent (`:3645`), four render sites — and would need a `now` parameter it does not take: *"having a 3rd bucket may make things more difficult. keep the current two buckets and i'll have to remember to close the days as they go by."* **Current behaviour is correct as specified.** An event leaves *Upcoming* when its days are marked complete, not before. A future session seeing a stale event under *Upcoming* is looking at intended behaviour — read `auto-mode-decisions.md` (2026-07-31, T304) rather than opening a new row. **Accepted residual risk:** when a coach forgets, the event sits in *Upcoming* indefinitely, its hours never reach `v_student_hours` (which joins `es.status = 'completed'`), and season totals under-report. T303's wording change makes those hours visibly uncounted but does not make them count. **Cheaper middle ground if it ever bites — not authorized:** keep two buckets and mark any *Upcoming* row whose sessions have all passed, which needs no new bucket, no second consumer, and no signature change.

issues.title: T305 — Students with recorded attendance and hours still show under **"No response"** in the same event's Signups, and the mark-complete dialog opens at **"0 attended · 0 h"**
issues.description:
**Attendance and RSVP are deliberately separate records and that separation is correct** — `AttendancePanel.tsx` contains **zero** references to `rsvp`, and `OutreachList.tsx:1685-1687` records the reason in a CHECKER FIX from T121's rework: *"RSVP is intent, not a real attendance record."* Writing a `going` RSVP when a coach ticks an attendance box would **falsify the intent record**, claiming a student said yes beforehand when they never responded. **The fix is not to sync them.** **What is wrong is that one screen shows both and lets them contradict.** On the owner's Jul 6–10 event every session reads *Going (0) · No response (2)* while the Attendance panel directly below shows both students ticked with hours and the event badge reads `18h`. **Second symptom, same root cause:** `computeInitialAttendedStudentIds` (`MarkDayCompleteDialog.tsx:442-453`) seeds the checklist from `rsvps` **with** `status === 'going'` **only** — it never reads `attendance`. So on a session that already has recorded attendance the dialog opens with everyone unchecked and its confirm button reads **"Mark complete — 0 attended · 0 h"**, misdescribing the session it is about to complete. **Verified NOT data loss** — checked before filing, because this is the shape that got T196 parked. The backfill is `.upsert(..., { onConflict: 'session_id,student_id', ignoreDuplicates: true })` (`endMeeting.ts:377-386`), so a student who already has an `attendance` row keeps it and is never overwritten with `absent`. The dialog **understates** what will happen; it destroys nothing. **Likely fix:** for a past or being-completed session show attendance where Signups currently shows RSVP intent (or show both, explicitly labelled), and seed the dialog's checklist from `attendance` first, falling back to `going` RSVPs only where no attendance row exists. **Owner ruling needed on the Signups display**; the dialog seeding is the clear-cut half. **— PACKET v1 STOPPED BY THE GATE, v2 WRITTEN 2026-08-01.** v1 (`0525378`) claimed the change was non-destructive and cited `loaders/endMeeting.ts:377-386`'s `ignoreDuplicates: true`. That citation is accurate but it is **T178's meetings backend, not this dialog's write path**. This dialog's real path is `markDayComplete` (`loaders/outreach.ts:1200`, built by `makeMarkDayComplete` `:1125`), whose attendance upsert names `check_in_at`/`check_out_at`/`hours_override`/`method`/`recorded_by` and passes `{ onConflict: 'session_id,student_id' }` with **no** `ignoreDuplicates` (`:1150`) — a full-column overwrite. `buildAttendanceWriteRows` (`MarkDayCompleteDialog.tsx:489-505`) hardcodes `status: 'present'`, `checkInAt: null`, `checkOutAt: null`, `method: 'coach'` and reads `hoursOverride` from a map `resetForm` empties on every open. **Today that is safe only by accident** — no student with recorded attendance ever starts checked, so no row is emitted for them; making them start checked (the whole point of the ruling) makes the same code destroy the record it means to respect. Gate measured: a student recorded `present`/3h/`qr` displayed **7h**, totalled **14h** against a true 10h, and confirming wrote `{hoursOverride: null, checkInAt: null, checkOutAt: null, method: 'coach'}`. **v2 is therefore two changes, not one:** seed from recorded attendance (falling back to `going` RSVPs where no row exists, `isAttendingStatus` imported from `AttendancePanel.tsx:308` rather than re-derived) **and** carry the loaded row's `status`/`checkInAt`/`checkOutAt`/`hoursOverride`/`method` through the write, using `resolveAttendanceWriteMethod` (`loaders/attendance.ts:218-222`) — the same delegation `AttendancePanel` already does at `:718` and `:791`. `recordedBy` deliberately stays the acting coach (pinned by criterion W4), per `UpsertAttendanceParams.recordedBy`'s own doc. **Second v1 error, also corrected:** v1 warned that adding a defaulted `loadAttendance` would break `OutreachDetail.test.tsx` — that file already partial-mocks the attendance loader at `:110-118` with `loadAttendanceForSessions: vi.fn(async () => [])` and is immune. The real trap is `MarkDayCompleteDialog.test.tsx`, which has **no** `vi.mock` **at all** and renders the dialog at ~13 sites. Because v2's fallback is graceful, those tests stay green while leaking post-teardown async state — **a green count there does not mean the seam was handled**, so S6/I1 must assert the mock was called. Baselines measured at `9c34f6a`, `.env.local` absent: `tsc` 0, `vite build` ✓, prettier clean, eslint **0 errors / 360 warnings**, vitest **72 files / 1746 tests**; `MarkDayCompleteDialog.test.tsx` **26**, `OutreachDetail.test.tsx` **94**. Two consequences disclosed in the packet and filed rather than solved: **T307** (`makeMarkDayComplete`'s upsert is destructive by construction) and **T308** (the confirm label can now legitimately disagree with `v_student_hours`). Follow-up on the ruling's other half: **T306**. **— GATE ROUND 1: REVISE (2 BLOCKER, 4 MAJOR, 4 MINOR, 1 NIT). Packet v3 written.** The gate built the prescription in its own worktree rather than reading it, and that is what found both BLOCKERs. **BLOCKER 1 — v2 was not implementable inside its own Allowed Files.** Making `buildAttendanceWriteRows`' 5th parameter required breaks a **fifth, production** call site v2 never found: `MarkEventCompleteDialog.tsx:187`. Measured: `TS2554: Expected 5 arguments, but got 4` at that line plus the four known test sites, `TSC_EXIT=2`. §11 forbade that file, so every worker would have hit a mandatory dispute on its first `tsc` run — Definition of Ready item 3. v3 adds the file with a two-line authorization and criterion W6 pinning the bulk payload byte-identical. **BLOCKER 2 — v2's "harmless only by accident" scoping was wrong, and the truth is worse: the bulk path destroys recorded rows TODAY.** `buildMarkEventCompletePayload` (`MarkEventCompleteDialog.tsx:176-192`) seeds from `computeInitialAttendedStudentIds` — `going` RSVPs — and feeds the result into the same destructive `markDayComplete` with an empty hours map, so a student who RSVP'd `going` and has a real check-in or a coach-typed override is overwritten with one click, no coach intent required. **That is the owner's own workflow.** Split out and re-filed as **T307** at bug severity. **The destructive-write premise itself was CONFIRMED by execution** — the gate drove the real `makeMarkDayComplete` over a stubbed transport at unmodified HEAD and captured `{check_in_at: null, check_out_at: null, hours_override: null, method: 'coach'}` with `{onConflict:'session_id,student_id'}` and no `ignoreDuplicates`. **Four of fourteen criteria did not discriminate.** W1's `hoursOverride` arm: green under its own mutation (`exit=0 failedCriteria=[NONE]`) because §4's seeding puts the recorded `3` into the coach map, so correct and mutated values coincide — v2's claim that W1 and W3 paired made neither vacuous was false; v3 splits it into a pure-function arm with an explicitly empty map. W2's named mutation was **impossible**: dropping the `existing !== undefined` guard compiles with 0 tests red, because `isAttendingStatus` takes `AttendanceRow['status'] \| undefined` and returns false for `undefined` — the guard is dead code, and no single-token mutation of the §5 matrix can leak preservation into the no-row case. S3's mutation was ambiguous across §4's two RSVP fallbacks, and one reading leaves it green. **v2's mock-hardening list was inverted:** with the mock deliberately broken, S6 and I1 go red on their own while S3/S4/S5/S8-late/W2/W3 all silently pass — v3 moves the `toHaveBeenCalledWith` requirement onto those six. **v2's stated harness failure mechanism was also wrong** — the un-mocked file does not leak a post-teardown setState (measured `26 passed, exit 0`); the mock is required because six criteria need to control the resolved value. §6's module-doc table was incomplete: four more false claims (`:359-361`, `:363`, `:402-404`, `:621-624`) plus a separate 13-line paragraph at `:138-150`, and the `:121-140` range was mis-bounded. **Confirmed correct and not to be re-litigated:** every baseline figure (72 files / 1746 tests, tsc 0, build ✓, prettier clean, 0 errors / 360 warnings, 26 / 94 per target file); the prescription builds and the full suite stays green at exit 0; `isAttendingStatus` imports from `./AttendancePanel` with no cycle (proven by building, not reading); `OutreachDetail.test.tsx` already immune at 94/94; S8's race reachable and testable with today's harness; §7(a)'s SQL reading and its "disclose, don't solve" call; sonnet tier defensible; and 10 of 14 criteria discriminating. eslint +2 measured for two new value exports. **— GATE ROUND 2: DISPATCH. Packet v4.** Round 2 built the complete prescription in its own worktree and all six gates came back green (`tsc` 0, `vite build` ✓, prettier clean, eslint **361** — +1 for one new value export — **73 files / 1757 tests exit 0**, its own scratch criteria file included). **The prescription is known to work before a worker ever sees it.** All eleven round-1 fixes verified landed; seven further findings, all folded into v4. **The one that was a real design bug, not a wording problem:** v3 seeded the hours map only for students who *start* checked, so an `absent`-recorded student with `hoursOverride: 3` whom the coach deliberately checks showed **7 h** in the input and counted **7 h** in the confirm label while the write emitted **3** — measured `LABEL: … 1 attended · 7 h` vs `WRITTEN hoursOverride: 3`. That also falsified module doc #2(b) (`:109-119`, `:455-458`), the constitution-item-3 legitimacy argument for `computeTotalHoursForCheckedStudents` existing at all. **v4 seeds the map for every recorded row with a non-null override, checked or not** — inert for unchecked students, since the label, the write and the per-student inputs all read the map only for checked ones — and makes the merge explicitly ungated by the touched-ref. New criterion **W6** pins label==write; the doc claim stays true. **Three more criteria were not what they claimed.** S3b was **vacuous** as a DOM assertion — under §4's imperative shape the component only calls the seed function from inside `.then()` with a non-null array, so the null branch is dead in the DOM path and its mutation left all 11 criteria green; now a direct pure-function call. The mock-hardening list still carried v2's numbering (it named "W2", which v3 had renamed W4) and omitted both new criteria; corrected to S4/S5/S8-late/S8b plus S3/W3/W4-if-DOM-level, with S6/W1/I1 measured red on their own and S3b/W2 structurally immune as pure calls. The old W6 (bulk payload byte-identical) was **dropped as redundant** — `MarkEventCompleteDialog.test.tsx:206-216` already pins it for free and reddens under the same mutation (`1 failed \| 14 passed`); item 25. **Two more stale doc claims found in the newly-in-scope bulk file** (`:22` and `:44-51`), the latter being the *"this does not invent attendance"* argument a future T307 implementer would rely on; §5.1's authorization extended to cover both. **One gate finding rejected as wrong:** F5 claimed `onMarkSessionComplete`'s default is at `MarkEventCompleteDialog.tsx:294` — verified `:291` is the default parameter and `:294` is `partitionEventSessions`, so v3's citation was already correct and was left alone. **Deferral of T307 confirmed defensible by measurement:** with `{}` passed at `:187` every field collapses to today's values and `MarkEventCompleteDialog.test.tsx` stays untouched at 15/15 — T305 changes the bulk path's behaviour, reachability and blast radius not at all. **— PASS-with-MINORs, first worker attempt. Full writeup in** `verification-log.md`**.** Checker `checker-reviewer` (opus): highest finding **MINOR** (2 MINOR, 3 NIT), no BLOCKER, no MAJOR. Gates re-measured three times independently: `tsc` 0, `vite build` ✓, prettier clean, eslint **0 errors / 361 warnings**, vitest **72 files / 1767 tests** exit 0, both targeted files exit 0. Sabotage check clean — five Allowed paths, and `git diff \| grep '^-' \| grep -E 'expect\|toBe\|toEqual\|toHave'` returns nothing, so no assertion was removed or weakened. **The worker refused a bad criterion rather than shipping past it:** S8b's named mutation leaves the suite green; it measured that, found a different mutation that does redden, and reported it. **The checker went further and was right to** — the two stale-load guards are *mutually redundant*, not one-dead-one-live: delete either alone and 44/44 stays green, delete both and the anti-clobber assertion reddens. `isMounted` only wins the race because `act()` flushes passive effects synchronously in tests; under React 18's real async scheduling the refs update during render while cleanup is pending, which is exactly what the same-session check covers. Both stay, and the redundancy is now documented in-source (NIT-1, fixed in place per item 25). **MINOR-1 also fixed in place, not filed:** two properties §4 calls load-bearing had no criterion — reversing the hours merge, and dropping the touched-ref set from `setStudentHoursOverride`, both left the suite fully green. Closed with one `describe` (W3b, two tests); **both mutations reproduced by the orchestrator rather than relayed**, each reddening exactly its own test (`1 failed \| 45 passed`). 1765 → **1767**, exact. **Checker-invented edge cases all behaved correctly** — `'excused'`, duplicate rows, non-roster rows, `hoursOverride: 0` — and the T179-class defect (a student's profile id in `attendance.recorded_by`) is structurally impossible here. **All fourteen module-doc corrections landed and are true**; the PRD quotation at `:4-10` verified **byte-identical by hash** (`d173f86c…` at both revisions), not assumed. **One gate finding rejected as wrong:** round 2's F5 misplaced `onMarkSessionComplete`'s default at `:294`; `:291` is correct and was left alone.
