issues.title: T307 — "Mark event complete" overwrites a student's real check-in/check-out, hours override and QR provenance with nulls and `'coach'` — one click, no coach intent
issues.description:
**Proven by execution, not argued.** `buildMarkEventCompletePayload` (`MarkEventCompleteDialog.tsx:176-192`) seeds its attendance rows from `computeInitialAttendedStudentIds` — `going` **RSVPs** — and passes them to `buildAttendanceWriteRows` with an empty hours map (`:187`), then feeds each payload to the same `markDayComplete` the per-day dialog uses. That loader's upsert (`loaders/outreach.ts:1136-1152`) names `check_in_at`/`check_out_at`/`hours_override`/`method`/`recorded_by` and passes `{onConflict:'session_id,student_id'}` with **no** `ignoreDuplicates` (`:1150`), so `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET` nulls every one of them. Captured payload at unmodified HEAD: `{status:'present', check_in_at:null, check_out_at:null, hours_override:null, method:'coach'}`. **Reachability is the reason this is a bug and not debt:** unlike the per-day dialog — where the defect is latent because no student with recorded attendance ever starts checked — the bulk path checks anyone with a `going` RSVP and writes immediately. A student who RSVPs `going`, then checks in by QR or has hours typed into the `AttendancePanel`, is destroyed the moment a coach clicks "Mark event complete". **That is the owner's own reported workflow** (T305 was filed off a screenshot of him typing 3h into that panel). **Deliberately excluded from T305** rather than folded in: the fix needs its own load seam across N sessions and — critically — a **different failure rule**. The per-day dialog may fall back to RSVP seeding when the load fails because it only *displays* the seed to a coach who then confirms; the bulk path has no display, so a failed load must **abort the write**, not fall back. Folding that into T305 would roughly double it and mix two failure models in one packet. **T305 leaves this exactly as-is, pinned by its criterion W6**, so the row stays real and findable rather than half-done. **Also owns:** `loaders/outreach.ts:125-128`'s now-false *"*`checkInAt`*/*`checkOutAt` *pass through as* `null` *verbatim"*, and the question of whether the bulk path should ALSO seed from recorded attendance (the owner's T305 ruling is written in display terms and the bulk dialog shows no checklist, so the ruling does not cleanly reach it). **Sequence: needs an owner call on whether it goes before T305, after it, or in parallel** — it is live today and T305 does not make it worse. **— PACKET WRITTEN 2026-08-01, in parallel with T305's worker** (packet authoring reads code and writes none, so there is no collision; a parallel *worker* would collide directly, since both tasks edit `buildAttendanceWriteRows`' signature and `MarkEventCompleteDialog.tsx:187`). **Hard dependency: cut the branch from** `claude/t305-attendance-over-rsvp` **after T305 merges, not from** `main`**.** T305's §5.1 already passes an empty recorded-rows map at `:187` with a comment naming this row, so this task is in essence "replace the empty map with real rows" plus the load seam and failure rule needed to obtain them honestly. **Gate scope: light, one round (item 19b)** — the load seam, the preservation matrix and the `resolveAttendanceWriteMethod` delegation were all verified by execution across T305's two full rounds and must not be re-audited; the genuinely new surface is the failure rule and the seeding decision. **The failure rule is the crux and is deliberately the OPPOSITE of T305's.** T305 may fall back to RSVP-only seeding when its load fails, because it shows the coach an editable checklist he reviews before confirming. This dialog shows no checklist and no review step, so falling back here means silently destroying rows on the one path where nobody can catch it. Therefore: an in-flight or failed load **blocks the write** — confirm disabled, DES-12 error state with a real retry, and criterion F1 asserts `onMarkSessionComplete` is called **zero times**, since "no rows destroyed" is only provable by the write never firing. The packet requires this asymmetry be disclosed in the module doc naming T305's opposite choice, so a later reader does not harmonise them. **Seeding decision recorded as the ORCHESTRATOR'S, not the owner's:** the bulk path will also seed from recorded attendance using T305's rule. George's T305 ruling is written in display terms and this dialog displays no checklist, so it does not cleanly reach here — but the rows are loaded anyway for preservation, a recorded student's write-back is effectively a no-op, and *not* doing it would make the per-day and bulk paths disagree about who attended the same session, which is the T188/T303 two-numbers family. Cheap for him to overrule: it inverts criterion P3 and leaves P4 untouched. **— LIGHT GATE: DISPATCH. Packet v2.** The gate built the complete prescription in its own worktree — load seam, block-on-failure rule, §4 seeding, the new parameter — and ran all six gates green (`tsc` 0, `vite build` ✓, eslint 361/0 errors, **72 files / 1771 tests exit 0** including its own scratch criteria). Seven findings, all folded. **MAJOR-3, the most important: F1 as written was VACUOUS** — "`onMarkSessionComplete` called zero times" is free when `remaining` is empty, so it passed green *and stayed green under its own mutation*. Would have been the project's eighth vacuous absence assertion. Now requires four clauses: a fixture with ≥1 `scheduled` session, `expect(confirm).toBeDefined()`, an actual click on the disabled button, and `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` on the loader (a mock that never intercepts leaves the real loader rejecting, producing an identical error state). **MAJOR-1/MAJOR-2: the block-on-failure rule reddens six existing tests, and v1 predicted the wrong reason for all of them.** It said `OutreachDetail.test.tsx` would stay green on its resolved-`[]` mock and warned only about a *rejecting* mock; in fact 2 tests fail in the **loading** state (`:1217`, `:1255` — they click confirm synchronously, so the promise has not settled and the button is disabled), and 4 of `MarkEventCompleteDialog.test.tsx`'s 15 fail the same way. **This is the exact inverse of T305**, where a graceful fallback kept the un-mocked file green and the gate had to argue a green count proved nothing; here the new contract announces itself. Fix measured: one `await flushMicrotasks()` before each click, plus an injected loader → `95 passed` and `21 passed`, both exit 0. Authorized explicitly in v2 as the new contract, not a regression. **MINOR-1: the** `handleConfirm` **guard has no possible criterion** — jsdom's `disabled` attribute suppresses the dispatched click, so F1 passes with the guard deleted. v2 requires the guard as defence-in-depth and says plainly that its mutation is green, so a worker does not rediscover that and conclude it is dead code (the trap T305's W2 set). **MINOR-2: §4's "effectively a no-op" claim was false in one column** — `makeMarkDayComplete`'s upsert also names `recorded_by`/`updated_at`, so the write re-stamps `attendance.recorded_by` from the original recorder to whoever clicked, on a row this path never touched, for a student the coach never saw. Consistent with the documented convention and with T305's W5, but every prior instance involved a coach actively editing that student's row; v2 requires it disclosed in the module doc. Reassuringly, the gate confirmed §4 **cannot** insert a row for a student who previously had none — qualifying requires already having one. **MINOR-3: every citation into the bulk file was stale by \~+23 lines**, v1 having been written pre-T305-merge; all re-verified at `e583e89`. **MINOR-4:** `buildRecordedRowsByStudentId` is deliberately unexported and its file is Forbidden, so the worker must re-derive a four-line filter-and-key locally — in tension with that file's own "REUSE, DON'T RE-DERIVE" doc, now explicitly authorized. **Confirmed correct and not to be re-litigated:** Allowed Files are sufficient (the required parameter produces exactly three errors, all in an allowed file; `buildMarkEventCompletePayload` has zero callers elsewhere — the test T305 v2 failed and this one passes); §3 fits the component without fighting it; blocking the confirm is reachable; the load must be gated on `isOpen` since the dialog is mounted whenever `user !== null`; L1's fixture already exists; P1/P3/P4 discriminate; no import cycle; sonnet tier defensible. **— FAIL on attempt 1 (1 MAJOR), reworked and closed. Full writeup in** `verification-log.md`**.** **The MAJOR: PostgREST truncation is a third state the design never modelled**, and the one surviving way this dialog could still destroy a row. `config.toml`'s `[api] max_rows = 1000` caps every response and `queryAttendanceForSessions` issues a bare `.select('*').in(...)` with no `.range()`. **A capped response is not an error** — 200 with a partial `Content-Range`, so `result.error` is null, `createLoader` (`loader.ts:174-176`, throws only on `result.error`) resolves the truncated array, and the dialog reaches `success` holding only some students' rows. The whole block-on-failure rule never engages because nothing failed, and a truncated-away student is indistinguishable from one who never had a row — so the write nulls their real check-in/hours/method, reproducing byte-for-byte the payload this task exists to eliminate. Verified independently by the orchestrator before acting. **Fixed fail-closed** per the checker's own option (a): a resolve at or above `ATTENDANCE_ROW_CAP` routes to the **error** state, which can only ever block a write and never permit one, turning the design's assumption that the array is complete from assumed into checked. Both mutations reproduced by the orchestrator (`1 failed \| 24 passed` each), plus a companion test one row below the cap proving it is not a blanket block. Loader-side `.range()` pagination filed as **T310**. **Also fixed: the load-effect** `isOpen` **gate was entirely unpinned** and the packet's cited criterion did not exist — `OutreachDetail.test.tsx:1063` has `user === null`, so this dialog is never mounted there. Removing the gate left both suites green; an ungated load would fire an `attendance` SELECT for every signed-in viewer on every outreach detail page. **Twelve of thirteen adversarial paths were already safe**, on the checker's own fixtures. It also closed two would-be-vacuous mechanisms: `createLoader` throws on `result.error` so a failed query cannot resolve `[]` and masquerade as "nobody attended", and RLS `staff_all on attendance for all` means read visibility equals write reach. **The checker disproved the packet's own F1b claim** — the `handleConfirm` guard IS pinnable; the reason a DOM-level force fails is that Astryx's `Button` guards on the `isDisabled` prop, not the attribute. By mutation layering it proved the rule holds at two independent layers. The worker correctly followed the packet in not inventing a criterion; the packet was wrong, not the worker. **The worker found a fact the packet did not know:** this dialog is mounted for any signed-in user and its content sits in the DOM while closed, so its first loading state leaked `aria-busy` onto every page; its `isOpen` render gate is load-bearing and reddens **two** pre-existing a11y tests (T157 parent, T169 student), not the one it reported. `aria-busy` **cleared against item 2** — a native ARIA attribute already used at `AttendancePanel.tsx:835`, `Leaderboard.tsx:483` and `OutreachDetail.tsx:1801`. **P2 was not unpinned** — the checker ran the mutation in its own worktree, which item 23 authorizes. **No fresh checker round on the rework** (item 25): remedy specified by the checker, ~4 lines plus three tests in Allowed Files, both mutations reproduced directly. Same posture as T302/T303. Gates after rework: `tsc` 0, build ✓, prettier clean, eslint **0 errors / 361 warnings** (unchanged — `eslint.config.js:39` sets `allowConstantExport: true`), vitest **72 files / 1777 tests** exit 0.

issues.title: T308 — The mark-complete confirm label can legitimately disagree with `v_student_hours` for a QR-checked-in student with no hours override
issues.description:
**Cause, traced through the real view.** `v_student_hours` (`20260717000003_metric_views.sql:7-14`) is `coalesce(hours_override, «clamped check_out − check_in when both non-null», «session duration»)`. Today the dialog writes `checkInAt: null, checkOutAt: null` for every row, so tier 2 can never fire for its rows and `computeTotalHoursForCheckedStudents`' local sum (`hoursOverride ?? sessionDuration`) is guaranteed to match the SQL — that guarantee is written into `MarkDayCompleteDialog.tsx`'s module doc #2(c) as part of its constitution-item-3 argument. **T305 preserves those timestamps instead of nulling them, so tier 2 can now fire and the button's total can differ from what SQL computes.** This is strictly better than today, where the number agrees *because the write destroys the data — the label is honest only about a value it corrupted*. **Do not close it by computing the clamped span in TypeScript**: selecting between MET-03's tiers in TS is the re-derivation constitution item 3 makes a BLOCKER, and that file's module doc #2(a) already states it does not do that. Plausible resolutions, none chosen: qualify the label, seed the hours input from the recorded row's own effective value supplied by the loader rather than derived client-side, or accept and document it. **Same family as T188** (two confirmed-hours numbers that can legitimately disagree) and likely wants the same owner ruling.

issues.title: T309 — Unchecking a student who has recorded attendance in "Mark day complete" does nothing — their recorded `present` row survives
issues.description:
**Pre-existing, and T305 did not cause it — but T305 makes it materially more reachable, which is why it is filed now rather than closed.** `markDayComplete` (`loaders/outreach.ts:1125`) upserts only the rows the dialog emits, and `buildAttendanceWriteRows` emits only *checked* students. So unchecking someone emits nothing for them and their existing `attendance` row is left untouched in the database. **Before T305 this was nearly unreachable**: recorded students never started checked, so there was nothing to uncheck. **After T305 recorded attendance drives the checkbox**, so unchecking a student who is shown as attending reads unambiguously as "mark them absent" — and silently does nothing. **Not fixable inside T305's Allowed Files:** the fix needs either a DELETE or an explicit `'absent'` write, both of which live in Forbidden loaders. **Mitigated today** by the `AttendancePanel` directly below on the same page, whose uncheck path does an unconditional DELETE for every `method` per T119/D-7 — so a coach who notices has a working control a few inches away. **Sequence after T307**, which is already opening the same write path and will have to decide the same question. **Open design question for that packet:** DELETE (matching `AttendancePanel`'s D-7 precedent, the coach is ultimate authority) or write `status: 'absent'` (matching `endMeeting.ts`'s absence-backfill shape)? The two disagree about whether "not present" is an absence of data or a recorded fact, and `v_student_hours` filters `status in ('present','late')` either way.

issues.title: T320 — `queryAttendanceForSessions` has no `.range()`/`.limit()`, so a >1000-row response is silently truncated by PostgREST and looks like success
issues.description:
**STATUS CORRECTED 2026-08-04.** This row read *"Awaiting merge (W1 branch* `claude/w1-checkin`*)"* long after it had merged. **Verified by the CODE, not the row text:** `.range(` pagination is present in `loaders/attendance.ts` on `main`, and `claude/w1-checkin` is an ancestor of `main`. The work shipped in **PR #28** (`bc53aab`, *"W1 (check in) — T321, T161, T320, T403 steps 1-3"*) and no one updated the three rows afterwards. **Original row text follows.** **Fixed by** `.range()` **pagination, the stronger of the two options the row offered.** `makeLoadAttendanceForSessions` now pages until a SHORT page returns; a full page means "at least this many", never "exactly this many", so an exact-multiple result costs one extra empty request rather than dropping what followed. `.order('id')` **is load-bearing, not cosmetic** — page N+1 is an offset into a result set and Postgres guarantees no ordering without an explicit `order by`, so paging an unordered query can return one row twice and never return another; `id` is the uuid PK. A page-count bound turns a server that ignores `.range()` into a diagnosable throw rather than an unbounded loop, and it throws rather than returning what it gathered — returning a partial set would reintroduce the very truncation being removed. **Scope discovery: this loader is shared across three workflows** — `endMeeting.ts:191` (W3) imports it and three W2 pages consume it — so six tests in `endMeeting.test.ts` and `AttendancePanel.test.tsx` stubbed the old chain and broke on `.order()`. **Owner authorized crossing that boundary** rather than weakening the fix; both edits are stub-only, no production change in either file. **Two follow-ups filed: T401** (the `ATTENDANCE_ROW_CAP` guard this row was meant to delete is now a false positive) and **T402** (`loaders/outreach.ts:745` carries the identical defect, which T320 never named). Verified true in both contexts (dialog standalone, console mount). **The performance trap was avoided AND measured:** as shipped `mount=1, after5keys=1`; rewritten as an inline factory call it reproduces the packet's own `mount=4, after5keys=9`. **One vacuous test was DELETED, not inverted a third time** — it asserted the End-meeting button was *absent*, clicked `undefined`, and checked for just-deleted stub copy, under a name describing the opposite. In production that is a coach shown fabricated tallies, and an "End meeting" button that silently does nothing. Two wiring tests added; **both of the checker's own Y1/Y2 mutations now red at exit 1**. **MINOR-2 filed as T601/T602.** **Cost, recorded honestly:** 3 packet versions, 2 gate rounds, 1 worker restart, and two orchestrator/worker collisions where the orchestrator edited files a live worker was writing. **All 3 round-1 BLOCKERs and both round-2 MAJORs originated in the orchestrator's own packet, not the worker's code.** Gates: `tsc` 0 · eslint **0 errors** / 366 warnings · prettier clean · vitest **79 files / 1999 tests, exit 0**. **Original detail follows.** **UNPARKED.** Owner closed both round-2 MAJORs: **(1)** test approval extended to `LiveConsole.test.tsx:868`, scoped to the two `it` blocks `:839-855`/`:857-869`; **(2)** **C4 DROPPED** — his own ruling 1 removes the correction list, and `AttendanceCorrectionRow` is the only caller of `onEditAttendance`, so nothing in the console can reach that path; any test would mock its way in to prove a wire attached to an unreachable switch. Coverage is not lost — `endMeeting.test.ts:626` already proves the fresh-read contract, and the wiring is still prescribed. **Packet v3 also folds in six round-2 MINORs** left unfixed when the row parked, including that **v2's own §5 re-created the performance defect §4 warned about** (a default-parameter expression re-evaluates every render: measured `mount=4, after5keys=9`; the module-level const at `LiveConsole.tsx:616` measures `1`/`1`). **A verified-green reference implementation is committed** at `active/T196-reference-implementation.diff` — the round-2 gate built the whole prescription and measured `tsc` 0 · eslint 0 · prettier clean · 78 files / 1952 tests, exit 0. **Original parked detail follows.** **All three round-1 BLOCKERs are fixed and round 2 found NO blocker.** The gate built the full prescription in a worktree and ran it: `tsc` 0 · eslint 0 · prettier clean · **78 files / 1952 tests, exit 0**. **A reference implementation is saved at** `active/T196-reference-implementation.diff` — the work is essentially done and verified; it is parked on authorization, not on difficulty. **⚠️ The owner's ruling was VINDICATED by measurement:** the gate rendered a completed session and drove it — the console's roster stays editable, clicking `Late` produced a real write `[{studentId:'student-ada',status:'late',recordedBy:'coach-aaa'}]` with the identity resolved at call time, and the QR panel still renders. With only the two authorized lines changed the suite is still **red at** `:868`, so a compliant worker must stop. **Non-negotiable #2 makes this an owner ruling, not a packet edit.** Cleanest fix: authorize the two `it` blocks at `:839-855` and `:857-869` rather than a line list. **DECISION 2 (MAJOR-B) — C4 is unmeasurable on this surface, by consequence of ruling 1.** `AttendanceCorrectionRow` is the ONLY caller of `onEditAttendance`; suppressing the correction list means **no affordance in the console can invoke it**. issues.title: T198 — Does `CoachHome` need a real per-coach "team" concept, or should its remaining team-scoped widgets go season-wide like T124's already-shipped ones?
issues.description:
**CLOSURE 2026-08-04.** Both halves shipped together, deliberately: wiring the queries WITHOUT de-scoping the page would have added real network cost for zero visible effect, since `PLACEHOLDER_CURRENT_TEAM_ID` matches no real id and every widget it touched floored to zero. **Loader** — `events` → `event_sessions` → (`rsvps`, `attendance`) chained on ids with the empty-`.in(...)` guard, plus `v_student_hours` and `v_season_attendance_rate`, all season-scoped, columns verbatim, conventions matched to `dashboard.ts`. **Page** — six helpers lost their `teamId` parameter; `isEventInTeamScope`, which this file's own comment called *"the ONLY team-scope predicate"*, is **deleted** rather than left dead; the `teamId` prop is gone from both component tiers. **Scope was larger than this row implied: six helpers, not four.** `teamParticipation` **→** `seasonParticipation` — `v_team_participation` is per-team with no season-grain rollup, so the figure now comes from `v_season_attendance_rate`; two consequences disclosed in-code and filed as **T803** (the denominators differ — the old view excludes excused absences, the new one does not — and the new view was **already** loaded and rendered elsewhere on this same page, so one metric now shows in two tiles from two load states). Tile relabelled "Team participation" → "Participation"; **"Hours vs. team goal" deliberately NOT relabelled**, since D-2's "we are just a team" framing keeps it honest. **Test edits were owner-approved 2026-08-04 and are NOT shape-only** — unlike T187's, they recompute expected values (`sumGoalHours` 18→23, `sumConfirmedHours` 7→107, fixture goal 38→48, attendance rate 75%→60%, upcoming 2→4, `0 / 1 hrs`→`0 / 18 hrs`) and **delete** `describe('isEventInTeamScope')` **outright** because the function no longer exists. Two team-scope exclusion assertions were **inverted rather than deleted** — same fixture, opposite expectation — as the sharpest proof the scoping changed. Two new fake-client dispatchers learned the six tables; without that their own `unexpected table` throw MASKED the error a test existed to assert. **Mutations replayed:** dropping `.eq('season_id', …)` reddens the query-shape spy; re-introducing a team filter in `selectCheckInSession` reddens 2 tests including the inverted one. Gates: `tsc` 0 · `format:check` 0 · `eslint` **0 errors / 363 warnings (down from 364 — deleted code)** · `vitest` **78 files / 1996 tests** · build 0. **Original row text follows.** **OWNER RULED 2026-08-03: season-wide, option (b).** Verbatim: *"yes, season-wide is fine option b"* — full ruling in `auto-mode-decisions.md`. **No per-coach team concept will be built.** The remaining team-scoped `CoachHome` widgets render season-wide figures, matching the five T124 widgets on the same page that already do (module doc #13(a)). **This is a widget-semantics change, NOT a schema or auth change** — none of constitution item 18's triggers fire and no migration is needed, which is exactly what the row asked to establish before anyone started building. **Now unblocked with it:** the deferred bundle this row always carried — real `events`/`sessions`/`rsvps`/`attendance`/`teamParticipation`/`studentHours` queries for `CoachHomeData`, literal honest-empty since T173 and parked pending precisely this answer. **Not authorized:** inventing any staff→team association, or treating `PLACEHOLDER_CURRENT_TEAM_ID` as real | **Filed by the orchestrator on** `foreman-planner`**'s T173-packeting investigation, before T173 was dispatched, so the gap is disclosed rather than silently resolved either way.** `AuthUser` (`guards.tsx:49-53`) carries no team field, no table anywhere links a staff profile to a team, and every `staff_all` RLS policy (`supabase/migrations/20260717000002_rls.sql:62-64, 96-98`) grants program-wide, not team-scoped, access — confirmed directly, not inherited from T173's original ledger text (which speculated a schema/auth change might be needed without checking). This is most likely a **product-scope question, not a pure engineering gap**: PRD HOME-01 names a "team goal" (`VOLT_Portal_PRD.md:275`) but the data model has no representation of which team a given coach belongs to, so there's no way to compute that scoping per-viewer — the gap is in the schema, not in the PRD's wording. `CoachHome.tsx`'s own module doc #13(a) already reached the identical conclusion for T124's five newer widgets (deliberately season-wide, citing D-2's "we are just a team" ruling in `state-summary.md`). T173 itself does NOT resolve this — it lets `teamId`/`PLACEHOLDER_CURRENT_TEAM_ID` fall through to an honest zero (same "placeholder never matches a real id" resolution T155 already shipped elsewhere) rather than building or guessing at team-scoping. **Resolve the question first; only then decide whether it needs a real schema/auth change (opus tier, its own migration task per constitution item 18) or a widget-semantics change (no migration at all).** Bundle in once resolved: real `events`/`sessions`/`rsvps`/`attendance`/`teamParticipation`/`studentHours` queries for `CoachHomeData` (currently literal honest-empty after T173, same proportionality-narrowed shape as T183/T199) — building these before the team-scoping question resolves risks building the wrong shape twice. **CORRECTION 2026-08-04:** this row's closure also filed **T804**, which is now WITHDRAWN as incorrect — `v_student_participation` was already migrated onto ACTIVE `student_teams` by `20260722000000_membership_views.sql`. issues.title: T199 — `StudentHome`'s `events`/`sessions`/`rsvps`/`participation` still have no real loader — T183 narrows to just the fabricated name, so this residue needs its own row
issues.description:
**CLOSURE 2026-08-07.** **The reported symptom was corrected before any work started, and the correction mattered.** Reported as "the student home page is blank"; the owner corrected it to *"it doesnt crash, it a missing loader"* — accurate, and it stopped a hunt for a crash that does not exist. `makeLoadStudentHomeData` resolved a real `displayName` (T183) and then returned `events: []`, `sessions: []`, `rsvps: []`, `participation: null` as **hardcoded literals**. **The cost was larger than "some empty sections"** — those three arrays are the sole input to every dynamic element on the page, so five surfaces were dark at once: "Next up" could only render its `EmptyState`, "Sign-up opportunities" likewise, `selectHeroState` was pinned to `'quiet-greeting'`, participation always read `—`, and **the live check-in hero was unreachable for every student in every state** — a student standing in the meeting had no way to check in from Home. That last one is not a cosmetic empty state. **No signature change, and team scope stays CLIENT-side on purpose.** `LoadStudentHomeDataFn` is still `(studentId, seasonId)` and the `events` read is SEASON-scoped, because `isEventInTeamScope` (`StudentHome.tsx:686`, its own comment: *"The ONLY team-scope predicate in this file"*) already runs inside all three consumers against the page's own `teamIds`. A server-side team filter would be a second implementation of "in scope", in PostgREST array syntax, free to drift — and would have forced stub churn in `StudentHome.test.tsx`/`DashboardPage.test.tsx`. A negative-control test pins that the page-side predicate does real work: an event scoped to another team is fetched and must not reach the screen. **DISCLOSED LIMIT, filed as T806:** `own_or_linked_read` on `events`/`event_sessions` (`20260717000002_rls.sql:153-188`) scopes by the LEGACY `students.team_id`, while T187 moved this page onto ACTIVE `student_teams`. A dual-team student's second-team events pass `isEventInTeamScope` but are filtered out by RLS before arriving. Pre-existing (T187 opened it), **and T199 is what makes it observable** — until now the page had no rows at all, so nothing could be missing from them. Needs a migration (item 16), so it is filed rather than worked around with a client-side compensation that would hide a policy bug inside a loader. Read from the policy text, which is unambiguous; **not measured live**. **Three fields stay literal, on a different judgement than T183's:** `defaultGoalHours`/`goalHoursOverride`/`studentHours` are not on this row's scope list and are **provably unread** — T176 round 2 moved those numbers onto props from `v_student_goal_projection`. A `v_student_hours` read would buy a round trip that changes no pixel (the trade T198 weighed on `CoachHome`). Inert, not unimplemented; a test pins that no such query is issued. **Dual-team participation, and a stale sibling found on the way.** `v_student_participation` groups by `(student_id, team_id, season_id)`, so a dual-team student has multiple rows WITHIN one season; `rows[0]` is the mistake `meetings.ts:437-446` already records `.limit(1)` making. This sums, using `v_team_participation`'s own expression rather than an invented one. That surfaced **T807**: T509 removed the `greatest(expected_ct - excused_ct, 1)` floor, but `meetings.ts:516` and `checkin.ts:375` still apply it when aggregating, and `meetings.ts:283`/`checkin.ts:239`/`reports.ts:221` still type `participation_pct` as non-nullable `number`. Not patched from here; deliberately not copied into the new code either. **Mutations: 8 written, 8 killed, each verified applied by printed line number** (M1 drop `.eq('season_id')` on events → 2 red · M2 drop `.eq('student_id')` on rsvps → 1 · M3 restore the pre-T509 floor → 2 · M4 `rows[0]` instead of summing → 2 · M5 coerce `team_ids` `null`→`[]` → 2 · M6 drop the empty-`.in()` guard → 1 · M7 revert all four fields to literals → 4 · M8 drop `.eq('season_id')` on participation → 1). **Two fake clients had to learn the new tables**, or tests would have passed for the wrong reason: both threw `unexpected table` for anything but `students`, which surfaced as a rejected `loadData` and the "Couldn't load Home" banner — the same masking shape T198 hit. **The pre-existing criterion-11 enumeration test passes identically before and after this change** (every one of its assertions is satisfied by an empty page), so three new render tests were added to make the difference observable. Gates: `tsc` 0 · `format:check` 0 · `eslint` **0 errors / 375 warnings (unchanged from** `main`**, measured by stashing)** · `vitest` **82 files / 2139 tests, up from 2121** · build 0. **Original row text follows.** **Filed by the orchestrator on** `checker-premise`**'s round-2 recommendation, before T183 was dispatched to a worker, so the gap is disclosed rather than silently left implicit.** T183's ledger row (above) closes with "Building a real `StudentHome` loader is this row's scope," but its own concrete evidence names exactly one user-facing defect — the fabricated `'Ada Reyes'` greeting — and everything else on the page (`events`/`sessions`/`rsvps`/`participation`) is independently classified in the same row as "honestly empty," not fabricated. T183's worker packet deliberately narrows to the display name only (proportionality, item 25): building real per-student event/session/RSVP/participation queries is materially larger, unscoped work (new queries against `events`/`event_sessions`/`rsvps` scoped to team+season, new interfaces, new tests) that nothing in T183's concrete evidence justifies bundling in. **The dangling reference:** `StudentHome.tsx:277-279`'s own module doc states this remaining seam "is filed as its own follow-up" — before this row existed, that sentence pointed at nothing once T183 lands narrowed, the exact documentation-trap class (a false or orphaned claim in a module doc) that cost T176 a full round and is called out by name in `RESUME-HERE.md`'s process-lessons section. This row is that follow-up. **Scope, not yet designed:** real `events`/`sessions`/`rsvps` queries scoped to the signed-in student's team+season (likely reusable patterns exist in `loaders/dashboard.ts`'s `CoachHome`-side event/session/RSVP queries, though those are season/team-aggregate shaped, not per-student — check before assuming direct reuse), plus a real `v_student_participation` read (already proven elsewhere, e.g. `loaders/reports.ts`/`ParentHome`'s own participation wiring) scoped to this student. Sequence after T183 lands (this row's own dependency, now merged).

issues.title: T201 — a deactivated student's real historical hours sit in `v_student_hours` (no `is_active` filter) but are invisible everywhere a consumer reads through `v_student_goal_projection` instead (`where s.is_active`)
issues.description:
**Found while packeting T191** (`src/lib/supabase/loaders/parentHome.ts:482-483`'s `confirmedHours: scope?.confirmedHours ?? 0` treats a deactivated linked student as having zero hours). `v_student_hours` (`supabase/migrations/20260717000003_metric_views.sql:3-19`) is a real, already-shipped view with **no** `is_active` filter and may hold nonzero real hours for her; `v_student_goal_projection` (`supabase/migrations/20260723000001_dashboard_views.sql:334`, `where s.is_active`) is what actually hides them from every current consumer. **Unlike T184's fix, relaxing** `v_student_goal_projection`**'s own filter is unsafe** — `resolveStudentScope`'s `null` return for an inactive student is exactly the signal T184's `{kind:'inactive'}` branch on `StudentHome` depends on, so any fix here needs a new, separate read, not a change to that view. **Scope genuinely unknown, same posture as T189**: establish where, if anywhere (a parent's card, a coach-facing view, nowhere), a deactivated student's historical hours should be shown before designing a fix — not decided by this row. Sequence after T191 resolves in the ledger, since T191's own fix touches the same card. **DIAGNOSIS 2026-08-05 — this row asked for scoping before a fix, and that is what this is. No code changed.** **Premise re-verified against the LIVE view definitions, not the originals the row cites** (`v_student_hours` was create-or-replaced by T322's `20260804000000`): it still has no `is_active` filter — it never joins `students` at all, so one is not even possible — and `v_student_goal_projection` still ends `where s.is_active`. Both halves hold. **Surveyed every consumer. Three of four are SAFE, and the row did not know which:** `leaderboard.ts:138` reads `v_student_hours` unfiltered but joins `v_leaderboard_students`, which is `where is_active`; `reports.ts:414` carries three `.eq('is_active', true)` roster filters; `coachHome.ts:350` filters in JS (`sumConfirmedHours` on `student.isActive`). **The leak is** `v_team_hours` (`20260722000000_membership_views.sql`), which sums `v_student_hours` joined only to `student_teams` — **no** `is_active` **filter at any level** — and feeds `dashboard.ts:308` → CoachHome's **"Hours by team"** widget. **MEASURED on live PG16.13**, two students on one team who both attended the same 4 h outreach session, one since deactivated: **"Hours by team" reports 8.0 h while the students a coach can actually see sum to 4.0 h.** The coach sees a team total DOUBLE the roster shown, with nothing on screen to account for the gap. That is the `is_active` family's third instance, made concrete. **NOT FIXED, deliberately — the remaining question is a product ruling this row explicitly reserves:** should a departed student's historical hours still count toward their team's total? **(a) No** — filter them, so the total always equals the visible roster; consistent, but understates what the team really did. **(b) Yes** — the hours were genuinely volunteered for that team; keep them, but the total legitimately will not match the roster sum and needs a visible explanation or coaches read it as a bug. **(c) Yes, and surface departed students' hours per-student** so the arithmetic reconciles — largest change, and note this row's own warning that `v_student_goal_projection`'s filter CANNOT simply be relaxed, since T184's `{kind:'inactive'}` branch depends on its null-for-inactive signal; it needs a new read. **OWNER RULED 2026-08-05: the hours COUNT** — verbatim *"that's actual work that was done regardless if that person is no longer with the team or not. That's like asking if your work done today counts for my token usage if i deactivate your session."* Owner chose **(c)** — keep the total AND surface departed members per-student — and delegated the goal-column sub-decision. **So** `v_team_hours`**'s 8.0 was RIGHT and HoursTab was wrong**: it hid the person, and the hours went with them. **NO MIGRATION** — `v_team_hours`, `v_student_hours` and `v_student_goal_projection` are all untouched, so T184's null-for-inactive signal (this row's own stated hazard) is unaffected. **The fix was cheap because the data was already there:** `queryHoursStudentHours` reads `v_student_hours` UNFILTERED, so departed students' hours were already being fetched and then discarded by the roster query's `.eq('is_active', true)`. Removing that filter (and selecting `is_active` so rows can be marked) was the whole data change. `buildStudentRows` keeps an inactive student ONLY when they have hours, so a departed student with nothing never appears. **Goal column, delegated and decided:** a past member shows `—` for goal and %, contributes 0 to the goal subtotal, and renders no ProgressBar. Counting their goal would make a team's "% to goal" DROP because somebody left — trading one wrong number for another. Confirmed and planned hours still count in full, which is what makes the subtotal reconcile. **4 mutations replayed.** Dropping past members again → RED; giving one a real goal → RED. **Removing the goal-subtotal filter alone → GREEN, and that is correct, not a gap:** `goalHours: 0` already enforces the rule, so the filter is a second, independent mechanism — applying BOTH mutations together is the only way to defeat it, and the subtotal assertion catches that. Defence in depth, each single-point failure pinned. **One of my own T163 tests was INVERTED**, not deleted: `makeLoadHoursData` *"scopes students to active only"* asserted the very filter that was the defect. It now asserts the filter is absent, and notes that the participation loader legitimately still filters. Two fake-client doubles were reshaped to the real `.select(...).order(...)` call rather than left permissive. issues.title: T202 — zero-goal `ProgressBar`s elsewhere still announce a fabricated `aria-valuemax` to assistive tech, even where the visible copy is honest
issues.description:
**Found by T191's checker-reviewer while confirming no sibling surface needed the same fix.** `src/pages/reports/HoursTab.tsx:942` carries the identical clamp `max={row.goalHours > 0 ? row.goalHours : 1}` T191 just removed from `ParentHome.tsx`. It doesn't leak the fabricated `1` into visible copy there (`formatValueLabel` prints only a percent), but Astryx's `ProgressBar` emits `aria-valuemax={safeMax}` unconditionally regardless of `formatValueLabel`, so a zero-goal row announces a fabricated max of `1` to screen readers even though sighted users never see it. Not covered by any other filed row — `CoachHome.tsx`'s instances are already T173/T198's territory, `StudentHome.tsx:1425`'s is covered by T184's inactive union. **Fix, not yet scoped:** audit `max={x > 0 ? x : 1}` `ProgressBar` usages for a11y-tree fabrication, starting with `HoursTab.tsx:942` — likely the same "should a zero-goal row show a bar at all" question T191 just answered for `ParentHome`, not a blanket clamp rewrite. **CLOSURE 2026-08-05.** The row named ONE site (`HoursTab.tsx`) and carved out the rest. **The audit it asked for found both claims wrong.** **(1) T191 did NOT remove the clamp from** `ParentHome.tsx`**.** Its owner ruling was *"no bar at all"* for a DEACTIVATED child — it replaced the bar with a marker on `!isActive`. The clamp survived at `ParentHome.tsx:1281` and still fired for an **ACTIVE** child with a genuine zero goal, which is the very page T181 existed to stop fabricating on. **(2) The CoachHome carve-out was empty.** The row deferred four `CoachHome.tsx` clamps to "T173/T198's territory" — but **T173's row does not mention ProgressBar, aria, valuemax or clamp at all**, and T198 (closed 2026-08-04) never touched them. They were orphaned. `StudentHome.tsx:1465`'s carve-out IS real — T184's row does name progressbar — so it is deliberately left alone. **Mechanism verified in the component, then by rendering, not from the row.** `ProgressBar.js:212` emits `aria-valuemax={safeMax}` unconditionally, and `:160` is `Number.isFinite(max) ? max : 0` — it passes 0 **straight through** rather than flooring it, and `:162` already guards the percentage with `safeMax > 0`. So the app-level `: 1` was the ONLY thing inventing the number, and passing the real 0 is safe. A throwaway render probe confirmed it: `max={1}` announces `aria-valuemax="1"`, `max={0}` announces `"0"` and does not crash. **Six clamps removed**, in two kinds recorded separately in-code: four real GOALS (`HoursTab:939`, `ParentHome:1281`, `CoachHome:2040`, `CoachHome:2441`) and two chart SCALES (`CoachHome:1982`/`:2012`, where an all-zero bar chart announced a scale topping out at 1 h). **Regression test + mutation:** a new `ParentHome.test.tsx` case pins `aria-valuemax="0"` for a zero-goal ACTIVE child, reusing T191's own scoped `hoursVsGoalProgressBars` helper. Reinstating the clamp turns it RED (`expected '1' to be '0'`). It asserts on `aria-valuemax` deliberately: `formatValueLabel` only shapes the VISIBLE label, so a text-only test would pass while assistive tech still heard the invented number — **which is exactly how this survived T191**. | Original status | **VERIFIED 2026-08-03 by direct measurement — this row previously read "Plausible, not independently verified" and that is now superseded.** Measured in **real Chromium at 390×844** via a throwaway Playwright rig (the T131/T142 convention: real dev server, real provider stack, rig deleted afterwards and the deletion declared). **The defect is REAL: 213px of horizontal overflow** — `document.scrollWidth` **603** against `clientWidth` **390**. **The audit's description is misleading, and the mechanism is not what it implies.** Nothing "collapses": the row **overflows**, and the culprit is **not** the RSVP `SegmentedControl` (the obvious suspect — the orchestrator guessed it from source and was wrong). It is the student row's `endContent` **action span**, `display: flex` with `flex-shrink: 0`, measured **563px wide inside a 342px** `ListItem` **whose own** `flex-shrink` **is 1**. It therefore refuses to compress or wrap. It is wide because the button labels embed the full event title — *"Hide session details – Canned Food Drive"* (563px) and *"Mark attendance – Canned Food Drive"* (241px) — the accessible-name pattern T131/T132 deliberately established, so **the labels are correct and must not simply be truncated**; the shrink/wrap behaviour is what is wrong. **Structural root cause:** the coach table got a full `isNarrow` branch under T130/T132; the **student view has none** — `isNarrow` appears nowhere in it, so it renders one layout at every width. **Blocked while T190 is in flight** — same file (`OutreachList.tsx`). **DIAGNOSED FURTHER 2026-08-04 — and the obvious fix does NOT work, measured.** The `endContent` `HStack` **already has** `wrap="wrap"`, so "make it wrap" is not the fix. Adding `maxWidth="100%"` — the component-level prop, item 11's first escalation step — was applied and measured: **still 213px overflow, unchanged.** The DOM shows why: our props land correctly, but the constraining element is **Astryx's own** `endContent` **slot wrapper**, one level above ours — a `span` at `flex-shrink: 0`, `max-width: none`, sized to its content at 563px. Our `HStack` inherits that 563px box, so its `maxWidth: 100%` resolves against 563 and its `wrap` never fires. Measured chain: `span(563, shrink 0, maxW none)` > `div.astryx-stack(563, wrap, maxW 100%)` > `button(285)` + `button(265)`, inside a **342px** `li`. **Each button would fit at 342px if wrapping engaged** — the content is not too wide, the box is unconstrained. **Shortening the labels is NOT available:** `Button.label` is the visible text AND the accessible name (`astryx-api.md:1811`), so trimming it would undo T131/T132's distinguishable-accessible-name work; and nothing on `ListItem` exposes the slot's width. **This therefore needs an item-11 escalation decision, not a prop change.** Options: **(a)** move the two actions out of `endContent` into the row body / expanded content — stays within component composition and is the **orchestrator's recommendation**; **(b)** `xstyle`; **(c)** custom CSS targeting Astryx's slot. **(a) is the only one that does not reach into a component's internals.** **Not packeted** — the escalation step is a judgement worth stating before building. **CLOSED 2026-08-04. Owner chose option A** (`auto-mode-decisions.md`, 2026-08-04): move the actions into the row body rather than override the slot or write custom CSS. **Measured after: 213px → 0**, all five buttons present, labels unchanged. **Shipped with NO new test, deliberately** — jsdom does no layout, two structural tests were measured **vacuous**, and a third was redundant with existing T170/T126 guards. The evidence is the measurement. |

issues.title: T400 — A student who cannot scan at all has no session id, so the kiosk's short code alone cannot check them in
issues.description:
**This is the half of audit LIVE-002 that T321 could not close, and neither the audit nor the T321 row saw it.** Both describe the fix as *"UI-only on a working backend"*. That is true for the expiry case — the URL already carries `?s=`, so T321's form reuses it. It is **false** for the case the audit actually named (*"a student who cannot scan has no fallback"*): `validateCheckinRequest` (`supabase/functions/checkin/validation.ts`) rejects any body without a uuid `session_id`, and `verifyShortCode` (`supabase/functions/checkin/hmac.ts:133-145`) HMACs the presented code over `` `${sessionId}:${bucket}` `` — a short code is meaningful **only** relative to one specific session. **The kiosk (**`Kiosk.tsx`**) displays the QR and the 6-char code but never the session id in readable form**, so a student reading the TV has no way to supply one. T321 deliberately does not render a form when `s` is absent, because that form could only ever fail. **Three candidate fixes, none UI-only:** (a) a live-session picker on `/checkin` — needs a loader listing open sessions, adjacent to T196's `LiveConsole` work; (b) the kiosk also displays a short session identifier the student types; (c) the edge function resolves a code against currently-live sessions — a backend change in `supabase/functions/**`, which **W1 does not own**. **(c) needs an owner call before anyone scopes it: it weakens the code's session binding and widens the 5/min rate-limit surface.** **RULING (**`auto-mode-decisions.md`**, "George's ruling on T400"): option (a), the live-session picker.** `/checkin` offers a list of currently-open sessions; the student taps the event they are at, which supplies the session id, then types the kiosk code. **(b) is closed** (two things to type on a phone in a noisy shop). **(c) is closed** — it would break the code's session binding, letting a code issued for one event match another running concurrently, while widening the 5/min rate-limit surface; it also lives in `supabase/functions/**`, which W1 does not own. **Sequencing: (a) needs a currently-open-sessions loader, which T196 must build anyway — so this is folded into T196's wave and must not be started before it.** **⚠️ THAT SEQUENCING CLAIM WAS FALSE — measured 2026-08-04 before starting.** T196 shipped and built **no such loader**. Every loader it produced takes a `sessionId` and returns one session: `makeLoadEndMeetingSummary` (`endMeeting.ts:288`), `makeOnEndMeeting` (`:373`), `makeOnEditAttendance` (`:448`), and `makeLoadLiveConsoleData` (`kiosk.ts:430`). Nothing anywhere in `loaders/` listed open sessions — grep for `openSessions`/`liveSessions`/`'live'` returned **zero** hits. So the row understated its own scope: T400 was never 'UI on a loader T196 leaves behind', it had to build that loader. issues.title: T502 — A `{data: null, error: null}` page resolves as end-of-data, so a paged attendance load can still come back silently short
issues.description:
`attendance.ts:363` does `const pageRows = (await loadPage({…})) ?? [];` and treats a short page as end-of-data. But `createLoader` returns `result.data ?? null` **without throwing** when `data` and `error` are BOTH null (`loader.ts:177`), and postgrest-js really can produce that pair — an empty 2xx body (`PostgrestBuilder.ts:488-490`) and a 404 with an empty body (`:551-554`, which sets status 204 and leaves `error` null). So an empty-bodied page resolves as "done" and the loader returns fewer rows than exist, silently. **T401 is what makes this reachable on the write path:** the `>= 1000` guard used to block precisely the sub-case where this landed on a page boundary. **Remote in practice** — needs >1000 attendance rows across one event's remaining sessions; the live DB holds 79 — and item 25 does not downgrade it, since this is data integrity, not security. Fix is one line in **W1's** `loaders/attendance.ts` (treat a `null` page as an error, not a short page), so W2 filed rather than reached across the boundary. **Also narrows** `verification-log.md:6454`**'s claim** that "`createLoader` throws on `result.error` so a failed query cannot resolve `[]`". Related: offset pagination can skip a row if a concurrent DELETE lands mid-page; keyset on `id` would remove the class. **FIXED 2026-08-04 — the premise was re-verified against the code first, and both halves were still exactly as filed** (`attendance.ts:360` still `?? []`, `loader.ts:177` still `result.data ?? null`). The fix is in `attendance.ts` and NOT in `createLoader`: `null` is a legitimate 'no row' for other callers — `querySessionUserId` (`checkin.ts`) depends on it for 'nobody is signed in' — so changing `createLoader` would have broken unrelated loaders to fix this one. The paging loop now throws on a `null` page, matching the page-cap branch three lines below it. A genuinely empty result set arrives as `[]`, never `null`, so the ordinary 'no attendance yet' path is untouched — **asserted directly, and mutation-proven** (forcing `[]` to throw as well turns that test red). **3 mutations, all red at exit 1:** reverting to `?? []` (2 failed); guarding only page 0 so mid-stream truncation stays silent (1 failed); throwing on empty too (2 failed). The middle one matters most — it is the real shape of the bug, a full page 0 of genuine attendance followed by an empty-bodied page 1, which the old code resolved as a complete-looking list short by however many rows followed. **Also narrows this row's own citation:** `verification-log.md:6454` said '`createLoader` throws on `result.error` so a failed query cannot resolve `[]`' — true for `result.error`, but silent for the `{data: null, error: null}` pair, which is the whole gap. Suite 2024 → **2027** (+3), exit 0.

issues.title: T700 — An auto-updatable single-table view owned by a `BYPASSRLS` role silently bypasses RLS for writes; only `v_leaderboard_students` qualifies today and T205 closes it
issues.description:
**Measured, not inferred.** A view with no `security_invoker` executes as its owner; in Supabase that owner is a `BYPASSRLS` role, so RLS on the base table does not constrain it. If the view is also *simple* (single table, no aggregate/join) Postgres makes it **auto-updatable** (`information_schema.views.is_updatable = YES`), and Supabase's stock `alter default privileges ... grant all on tables to anon, authenticated, service_role` hands every role INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE through it. Measured on Postgres 16.13: as `anon`, `delete from public.v_leaderboard_students` returned `DELETE 2` and emptied `students`, while the base table correctly denied `anon` (`DELETE 0` / 0 rows readable). **Surveyed all 16 public views on the full migration set:** `v_leaderboard_students` **is the ONLY** `is_updatable=YES` **view** — the other 15 aggregate or join and are read-only by construction. **So this row is a guard, not an open bug:** T205 closes the only instance. Scope: add a cheap standing check (an assertion in `supabase/tests/` that no `public` view is both `is_updatable=YES` and write-granted to `anon`/`authenticated`, or a documented convention in the migration header template) so a future single-table view cannot silently reintroduce it. **Do not re-fix** `v_leaderboard_students` **here** — that is T205. **CLOSURE 2026-08-05 — standing guard shipped, mutation-proven.** `supabase/tests/t700_updatable_view_guard_assertions.sql` + its runner: A1 fails if ANY `public` view is both `is_updatable=YES` and write-granted to `anon`/`authenticated`; A2 pins the survey non-vacuous (views exist AND some are write-granted, so A1 cannot pass for the wrong reason); A3 names `v_leaderboard_students` specifically. **Two of my own errors, caught by running rather than reasoning.** (1) A3 originally asserted `is_updatable = NO` — wrong: **T205 never changed the view's shape** and never claimed to. It is still `select id, display_name from students where is_active`, simple and therefore still auto-updatable; T205 fixed the hazard by REVOKING grants. A3 now pins the absent write grant, which is the property that actually matters. (2) The runner first applied blanket `grant ... on all tables` AFTER the migrations, which silently UNDID T205's own `revoke` and made the guard fail against a correctly-fixed database. It now uses `alter default privileges` BEFORE the migrations — how the real platform behaves, leaving later explicit REVOKEs standing. **Mutations replayed:** commenting out T205's two `revoke` lines turns A1 and A3 red (A3 naming `anon:DELETE, anon:INSERT, …`); adding a NEW simple view (`select id, display_name from students`) turns A1 red naming it — **that second one is the guard's actual purpose**, a future view reintroducing the class.

issues.title: T701 — `tests/rls/run.sh` can no longer apply the migration set on a bare Postgres, and no CI job runs it
issues.description:
**Measured while scoping T205.** That runner's own header promises it applies "EVERY file under `supabase/migrations/` UNCHANGED and in filename order". That stopped being achievable as migrations were added: it fails at **three** separate files on a bare Postgres — `20260719000000_cron.sql` needs `pg_cron` **and** `pg_net` (`pg_net` is Supabase-platform-only and not packaged for Debian/Ubuntu), and `20260720000001_avatar_storage.sql` needs `storage.buckets`. It also assumes the `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` roles pre-exist (`tests/rls/auth_stub.sql:67-70`), which is true on Supabase and false on bare Postgres. **Nothing caught this because nothing runs it** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs only `npm ci` / typecheck / lint / test / build. **The fix already exists in-repo and is proven:** W6/T195's `supabase/tests/run_calendar_feed_lifecycle.sh` skips `cron.sql` by name (`:29-31`, "requires Supabase pg_cron, pg_net, and Vault") and `supabase/tests/calendar_feed_platform_stub.sql` creates the three roles (`:7-13`) and stubs `auth` and `storage` (`:16-61`). That suite was measured green in a clean container (exit 0, ALL PASS). Scope: bring `tests/rls/run.sh` onto that pattern, and consider whether either SQL suite belongs in CI — today neither runs there, so both can rot again. **CLOSURE 2026-08-05 — both halves: the harness fixed, AND the reason it rotted removed.** **Harness.** The row named `cron.sql`/`avatar_storage.sql` and the missing roles, but measuring first showed the ORDER was different: the roles break it FIRST, at `20260717000002_rls.sql`'s `grant ... to authenticated`, long before either platform migration is reached. `tests/rls/auth_stub.sql` now CREATES the three roles idempotently instead of assuming them — its own comment used to claim they "already exist... (confirmed directly)", true on the box it was authored on and false on bare Postgres. Both runners now skip the two platform migrations by name with reasons, and `run.sh`'s header no longer promises "EVERY file". **The sibling suite was rotten too, and worse.** `supabase/tests/run.sh` had the same class of failure (its `auth.users` stub lacked `email_confirmed_at`/`last_sign_in_at`/`raw_user_meta_data`, so the invite trigger failed at apply time). Fixing it revealed **a genuinely failing assertion that had been invisible for two weeks**: `seed.sql` seeds `students`/`teams` but ZERO `student_teams` rows, because `20260721000000_student_teams.sql`'s backfill runs at MIGRATION time and this seed loads AFTER migrations. The moment `20260722000000_membership_views.sql` moved `v_student_participation` onto ACTIVE memberships, `a-excused-shrinks-denominator` broke — and nobody knew, because the runner could not start. **That is the cost of the rot, made concrete.** Memberships added; all 5 cases now pass with real arithmetic (`expected_ct=2 present_ct=1 excused_ct=1 → 100.0%`). **CI.** A new `sql` job in `ci.yml` runs all EIGHT suites against a `postgres:16` service container, one step each so a failure names its suite. Dress-rehearsed locally against live PG16.13: **8/8 PASS**. The RLS suite was mutation-proven too — weakening `own_or_linked_read on students` to `using (true)` turns 2 assertions red and exits non-zero. **Nothing can rot silently here again.**

Same absence-only failure class this project has shipped 7+ times, wearing a positive-assertion costume. **Fix:** give the meeting fixture non-zero adult figures and assert the resulting total explicitly, so the "all event types" contract is actually load-bearing. **Sequence after T702** — if the owner rules that non-outreach events should be excluded, the corrected assertion must encode the new rule rather than the old one, and doing this first would mean writing the test twice. **CLOSURE 2026-08-05 — the defect no longer exists, and T702's own implementation already said so.** This row's own text sequenced it *"after T702"*, anticipating exactly this. Verified four ways rather than taken on the row's word: **(1) The fields it names are GONE.** T703 rests on the meeting fixture carrying `adultVolunteersCount: 0, adultVolunteerHours: 0`. T702 DELETED both figures — `HoursSeasonTotals` has neither field, and `buildSeasonTotals` no longer computes them. **(2) The regression it guards is now structurally inexpressible.** `buildSeasonTotals(sessions)` no longer takes an `events` argument at all, so it cannot see event `type` and therefore cannot "silently drop non-outreach events" however it is written. **(3)** `HoursTab.tsx` **module doc #6 ALREADY records this**, by name: *"an earlier plan (T500/T703) to exclude sessionless events' adult-volunteer figures from the season sum ... is superseded and removed along with the figures it guarded; there is nothing left for that guard to protect once the sum itself is gone."* The row simply outlived its own resolution, exactly as T204's did. **(4) Both surviving claims are mutation-proven load-bearing** — the concern behind T703 checked against today's code rather than yesterday's. Truncating `buildSeasonTotals`'s loop turns 2 tests red; mis-bucketing nulls into the total turns the same 2 red; and the meeting fixture's *new* advertised proof (that `countsVolunteerHours: false` excludes it from planned/confirmed hours) reddens 2 tests when that guard is removed, one named for precisely that behaviour. **Nothing here advertises a proof it cannot deliver.** **One error of mine, recorded because it nearly became a false finding:** the first mutation attempt targeted `for (const session of sessions)` with a single replace, which hit line 443 — a DIFFERENT function — leaving `buildSeasonTotals` at 596 untouched. The test passed, and that looked exactly like T703's defect confirmed. Checking that the mutation landed where intended is what caught it. **A mutation that did not apply is indistinguishable from a test that does not guard.**

issues.title: T509 — MET-01's denominator becomes explicit marks rather than eligibility
issues.description:
**Authorised by D014 + the owner's ruling; PRD text deliberately unedited (D002/D013 pattern).** `v_student_participation` (`20260717000003_metric_views.sql:22-41`) builds `expected` as a cross product of eligible students × completed sessions and LEFT JOINs `attendance`, so `expected_ct` **counts eligibility, not attendance rows** — an absence row does not move the denominator by one. It becomes `present+late` ÷ (`present+late+absent` − `excused`) over sessions where the student **has a row**. **Why:** the sub-teams that decide who is expected (business/build/software) sit *below* `teams` and are deliberately unmodelled, so expected-attendance is **not derivable from any data the app holds** — see D014. **DEPENDENCY IS LOAD-BEARING: this is a no-op until T508 ships.** While `backfillAbsences` writes a row for every eligible student, "explicit marks" and "eligibility" select the same set, so the denominator would not change. **Also required:** re-derive T014's MET-01 fixture tests by hand (they encode the old denominator), and `—` must now cover a student with no marks at all. **Known cost, recorded in D014:** this inverts the failure direction — forgetting to mark now inflates rather than deflates. RPT-02's visible `expected/present/late/excused` counts are the mitigation; **if RPT-02 stops showing them, D014 must be revisited.** **W4's surface** (metric SQL). Owner applies the migration (item 16). **BUILT 2026-08-05.** Premise gate run FIRST on live PG16.13, and it found the row understates the defect: with a two-student fixture, the shipped view reported `expected_ct=2, present_ct=0 -> 0.0%` for a student with **zero attendance rows**. Nobody had marked them; the view returned 0% for them. **T508 made that the DEFAULT case** (absences are now an explicit coach opt-in), so this is a real defect in shipped code, not only a PRD deviation. **WORDING CORRECTED 2026-08-05:** this row first called it "a live user-facing lie". That overstated it. The 0% was measured on a FIXTURE built for the premise gate, and the owner has confirmed there is no live system and no attendance records — so no user was ever shown a wrong number. The defect is real and would produce one the moment real attendance exists; "live" was wrong and implied an urgency that did not apply. **Shipped** `20260806000000_met01_explicit_marks.sql`: the `expected` CTE's LEFT JOIN to `attendance` becomes an INNER join, so the denominator counts marks. Both views now return **NULL rather than** `greatest(...,1)` when there is no denominator, which the UI already renders as an em dash. `v_team_participation` moved with it, or student and team rows would disagree. **Two row instructions were wrong and are corrected in-file.** (1) The stated denominator *"present+late+absent − excused"* would DOUBLE-SUBTRACT: `attendance.status` is a four-value mutually-exclusive check, so `present+late+absent` already excludes excused. Implemented as `count(*) − excused` ("every mark except an excused one"). (2) *"re-derive T014's MET-01 fixture tests, they encode the old denominator"* — **measured: they do not.** `supabase/tests/run.sh` passes IDENTICALLY with T509 applied and withheld, because `seed.sql` marks every student for every session, so eligibility and marks coincide there. Its assertions are still correct, just blind — the same fixture-cannot-tell shape as T703. A diverging fixture was written instead. **A DECISION WAS MADE AND THEN REVERSED, recorded because the first estimate was wrong.** `expected_ct` now counts marks, so a rename to `marked_ct` was drafted and proven to work (`ALTER VIEW ... RENAME COLUMN`; the dependent view auto-follows by attribute number). **Reverted:** `expected_ct` is selected FROM THIS VIEW BY NAME in `reports.ts:253`, `checkin.ts:336` and `meetings.ts:425`, so the rename would break three surfaces AT RUNTIME. The column name stays, a catalog comment carries the meaning, and the correction lands where a user can see it: **RPT-02's header "Expected" → "Marked"**, which is what D014's mitigation actually depends on. **Proof:** `supabase/tests/t509_explicit_marks_assertions.sql` + runner, wired into CI's `sql` job (now 12 steps). 5 assertions PASS on live PG16.13; **withholding the migration turns 4 of 5 RED** with exact diagnostics (`expected 0 rows, got 1 (the pre-T509 0% lie is back)`, `pct=0.0`, team `25.0`). A2 correctly stays green — a fully-marked student scores the same either way, so the change is surgical. All 8 pre-existing SQL suites still pass. **MIGRATION APPLIED by the owner 2026-08-05**, against a database with no attendance records — so nothing observable changed, which is precisely why applying it before real data was the cheap moment. **The migration FILE itself is deliberately NOT corrected:** it is now applied, and constitution item 10 makes editing an applied migration a BLOCKER. Its own header describes the finding as a "user-facing defect", which is weaker than this row's original wording but still generous — it is on a user-facing screen that no user has seen. If that is ever worth correcting it needs a NEW file, the route T801 took, not an edit. Gates: `tsc` 0 · `format:check` 0 · `vitest` 81 files / 2051 tests · 9 SQL suites green.

issues.title: T801 — `dashboard_views.sql` carries two wrong comments that constitution item 10 forbids fixing in place
issues.description:
**This is the half of T186 that could not be shipped.** `20260723000001_dashboard_views.sql` is an applied migration, and **item 10 makes editing an applied migration file a BLOCKER**, so both corrections below live only in TypeScript today and a reader who opens the `.sql` file sees neither. **(1)** `:311-320` says `v_student_goal_projection.team_id` is "used here ONLY for the row's display badge … never for any rollup math". Still true as of T187, but it names only one reader; a **second** reader exists (`loaders/students.ts`'s `queryStudentGoalProjectionById` → `StudentScope.teamId`) and that reader once used the column for functional scoping, which was the T187 defect. An editor trusting this comment cannot see that history. **(2)** `:49-52` says none of its views are `security_definer`/`security_barrier` "so each runs under the querying session's own RLS against its base tables". **Wrong as written** — `security_definer` is a *function* attribute, the view-level knob is `security_invoker` (PG15+), which defaults **OFF** and appears zero times in `supabase/`; these views execute as their OWNER and bypass base-table RLS. **Measured, not reasoned:** `20260731000000_leaderboard_students_view.sql:32-46` records a live PGlite run proving it. Originally T185's finding; T185 closed no-change on the owner's proportionality ruling (the exposure is the product) and folded the comment residue into T186. **No behaviour change and no security work is implied** — this is comment accuracy only. **Two ways to close, both needing an owner call:** (a) a new additive migration using `comment on view …` to write the corrections into the catalog (item-10-compliant, costs a migration to apply for a comment fix), or (b) amend item 10 to exempt comment-only edits, then fix in place (changes a BLOCKER-class rule). Owner ruled 2026-08-04 to do **neither for now** and file this row instead. **CLOSURE 2026-08-04 — option (a), the additive migration.** Owner said work it; between T801's own two options I took **(a)** and deliberately not **(b)**, because (b) amends a BLOCKER-class constitution rule and that is the owner's call, not something an implementation task should smuggle in. (a) needs no rule change and has adjacent precedent (`20260804000000_volunteer_hours_outreach_only.sql` fixes applied views from a new file, citing item 10 by name). **Shipped:** `20260805000000_dashboard_views_comment_corrections.sql` — `comment on view` for all nine `dashboard_views.sql` views (correction 2, the RLS claim) and `comment on column v_student_goal_projection.team_id` (correction 1, the second reader). Both wrong comments are quoted verbatim in the new file's header, so a reader who finds only that file still learns what was wrong and where. **Both claims re-verified before writing, not taken from the row:** `security_invoker` appears 6× in `supabase/` but as a real `with (security_invoker = …)` clause **zero times** (the row said "zero times" without that distinction — substance correct, wording imprecise); and the second reader is real — `students.ts:464` `queryStudentGoalProjectionById` selects `team_id` into `StudentScope.teamId`, with `students.ts:434-443` recording that it once drove scoping (the T187 defect). `comment on` **had ZERO prior use in this repo** — a new mechanism, named in the migration header rather than slipped in. **Disclosed limitation:** a reader opening `20260723000001_dashboard_views.sql` still sees the two wrong `--` comments. Item 10 is precisely the rule forbidding their rewrite; catalog comments and the new file are additive reach, not a replacement. **Verified live on PostgreSQL 16.13**, not reasoned: every migration applied to a fresh DB (2 skipped — `_cron`/`_avatar_storage` need Supabase-managed extensions absent locally and neither defines or reads a dashboard view), then 4 assertions PASS. **4 mutations replayed:** drop a view's comment → A1 red naming it; **reintroduce the ORIGINAL wrong text** → A1 red; strip the second reader → A2 red while A3 stays green (proving they're independent); `security_invoker=on` → A4 red. Re-applying the migration verbatim restored all green, proving idempotency. `pg_get_viewdef` **digest identical before and after — the "changes no view definition" claim is measured, not asserted.** **New test file:** `supabase/tests/t801_dashboard_views_comment_assertions.sql`, following the T322/T205 convention (PASS/FAIL collected, one raise at the end), but with **no fixture INSERTs** — a comment-only correction has no row behaviour to construct. Gates: `tsc` 0 · `format:check` 0 · `vitest` 80 files / 2010 tests.

issues.title: T512 — `WORKFLOWS.md` reports three different open-row totals (~60, 42, 36); item 29 moved the source to the Linear export
issues.description:
The script this row specifies cannot be built as written. Constitution item 29 froze `docs/swarm/task-ledger.md` on 2026-08-09 and moved state to Linear, in these words: *"Do not add rows to it, and do not edit a row's Status to reflect new work."* A count derived from that Status column is wrong by construction for anything filed or closed since.

What the row was protecting is still broken. `WORKFLOWS.md` carries three different open-row totals right now: `~60` in its opening line, `42` if you sum the assignment table's `Open rows` column, and `36` in `linear-export.md`'s header for the same board.

## What item 29 changed

**The structured source this row wanted already exists.** `scripts/linear-export.mjs` writes `docs/swarm/linear-export.json` whole on every run, on a schedule, behind a DO-NOT-EDIT banner (item 29b and 29c). Counting open rows is now a filter and a group-by over JSON. No pipe-table parse, no locating `Status` by header name, no fail-loudly-on-column-drift requirement. That erases most of the work this row describes, including the "normalise the 30 rows" companion fix.

**The grouping key changed too.** Item 29a retires the `Tnnn` block allocation the row proposed mapping through, because Linear allocates `GAM-nnn` and new work carries no `Tnnn`. The replacement is already applied: every migrated row carries an `area/w*` label in the export.

## What survives

`WORKFLOWS.md`'s numbers are stale, and so are the state notes beside them. W5's cell still says T802 is open and T803 is in flight in PR #93; both closed 2026-08-05. W4's cell says T509 is blocked on T508; T509 closed 2026-08-05. The preamble at `:8-10` still says *"*`task-ledger.md` *remains authoritative for row status"*, which item 29 makes false.

That leaves one real choice, and it is worth making deliberately rather than drifting into:

1. **Regenerate the column.** Emit `Open rows` from `linear-export.json` grouped by `area/w*`, and fix the preamble's source-of-truth sentence. This keeps the file's durable half, the "safe to run beside" matrix, which is decided by file overlap and does not rot.
2. **Retire the column.** Drop the counts, keep the parallelism matrix, point at Linear for state.

Take (1) if anyone still dispatches from this file, (2) if nobody does. That is the owner's call and the only open question left in the row.

## The one constraint

Do not read the ledger for status. Item 29 leaves it authoritative for the provenance of anything filed before 2026-08-09 and for nothing after.

## Size

One script reading a JSON file, plus a regenerated table and one corrected sentence in `WORKFLOWS.md`. No application code, no schema, no write path. Suggested Allowed Files: `scripts/**`, `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`.

## Suggested priority: low urgency, low cost

Do it, or close it as superseded, next time anyone opens `WORKFLOWS.md`.

1. No user is affected. This is an internal dispatch view, and item 28 moved dispatch to Linear's `Todo` column, so nothing now depends on these numbers.
2. Nothing is blocked on it.

It stops being deferrable the moment someone dispatches a machine off this table, because the counts and the state notes are both wrong today.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`fcaa66d`) on 2026-08-10.

* **The premise is superseded, and that is the headline.** The filing predates item 29 by four days. Its diagnosis of PR #89 still stands; its prescribed source does not.
* **The column-consistency measurement moved, and no longer matters.** The filing measured 278 `| Tnnn |` rows on 2026-08-05: 248 matching the header's 10 columns, 30 disagreeing. Re-run today with escaped pipes handled: **293 rows, 256 matching, 37 disagreeing** (2 with 9 columns, 26 with 11, 8 with 12, 1 with 13). The ledger kept growing until the freeze. Since nothing needs to parse it any more, normalising those rows is moot rather than cheaper.
* **One requirement survives the change of source.** Fail loudly rather than return a plausible number. That was the lesson of PR #89's two defects, and it applies to a JSON reader exactly as it applied to a Markdown one.

**Filed because hand-recounting produced two wrong numbers in one PR.** `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md`'s assignment table carries an open-row count per workflow. PR #89 recomputed those counts by reading `WORKFLOWS.md` — which is the artifact under repair — and shipped **two** defects the owner caught in review. (1) The helper treated `NARROWED` as a closed status, so T333 was silently dropped from every count and W9 read `3 — all human gates` while the same cell described T333's machine-workable ETL half. (2) The helper split the file into sections on `^## (W\d+) — `; W10 is the **last** workflow section, so its section ran to EOF and swallowed the Coordination-rules block-allocation table that follows, counting `T333`, `T600-699` and `T700-799` as W10 rows — W10 went 8 → 9 when the true figure was **6** (8 listed, T157 and T301 merged). Two requirements carried from the failures above — it must treat `NARROWED` as **open**, and it must **fail loudly** rather than return a number when a row ID maps to no workflow block or a status string matches none of the known keywords. issues.title: T807 — Two loaders still apply the `greatest(x, 1)` floor T509 removed, and three row types still declare `participation_pct` non-nullable

**Found while writing T199's own participation aggregate, by looking for an in-repo expression to reuse rather than inventing one (constitution item 3).** T509 (`20260806000000_met01_explicit_marks.sql`, APPLIED) replaced `v_student_participation`'s `round(100.0 * present_ct / greatest(expected_ct - excused_ct, 1), 1)` with an explicit `case when ... = 0 then null else round(...) end`, precisely so that a student whose every mark is `excused` stops reporting a fabricated `0.0%` and reports NULL (which the UI already renders as an em dash). **Two loaders re-apply the removed floor when they aggregate a dual-team student's per-team rows:** `loaders/meetings.ts:516` (`Math.max(expectedCt - excusedCt, 1)`, in `aggregateParticipationRows`) and `loaders/checkin.ts:375` (identical expression). issues.title: ~9 closed ledger rows are sitting in Linear as pickable Backlog, because their closure never touched the Status column
