issues.title: T808 — Students and parents see raw float hours (`3.9999983633333334 / 100 h`) beside a rounded percentage
issues.description:
> **CORRECTION, added 2026-08-09 after this row shipped. One sentence below is measured false.**
>
> This row says *"The coach looking up the same student sees* `4.0`*"* and treats that as coach-vs-student. **The coach's home dashboard has the same bug** — `CoachHome.tsx:2050` prints `row.confirmedHours` raw from the same `v_student_goal_projection` passthrough. The `4.0` comes from the **Reports → Hours tab** (`HoursTab.tsx:1017`, `renderHoursCell`). So the inconsistency was real but it is **reports-vs-home, not coach-vs-student**.
>
> Measured twice independently: by the agent implementing this row, and by an agent on `claude/w1-linear-autoclose` which reached the same line unprompted. The CoachHome half is filed as [GAM-308](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-308/coachhomes-goal-projection-row-prints-the-same-raw-float-hours-t808); it is not fixed by this row.
>
> The original text is left intact below rather than edited, since it is what was believed when the work was scoped.

A student opening their home page sees their volunteer hours as `3.9999983633333334 / 100 h (4%)`. The percentage in that same label is rounded. The hours are not.

Parents see it on their page too. The coach looking up the same student sees `4.0`, so the app shows one fact two ways depending on who is logged in.

## Why it is worth fixing

Volunteer hours are the number students are measured on. A 17-digit float reads as broken arithmetic, and it visibly disagrees with what the coach sees for the same student. That puts it in the hours-honesty class rather than styling.

## Why it happens

`confirmedHours` is a verbatim passthrough from the `v_student_goal_projection` SQL view (`StudentHome.tsx:1431-1439` says so explicitly), and the render prints it as-is. Float division inside the view produces the long decimal. The percentage on the same line looks clean only because it goes through `round1` on the way to the screen (`:884`, called at `:1440`).

There is a `round1` a few hundred lines up at `StudentHome.tsx:868`, but it belongs to `computePlannedHours`, which this render path no longer calls. Anyone skimming the file will assume that helper covers these numbers. It does not.

## Where it renders

| File | Line | What renders |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1483 | progress-bar label |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1485 | supporting text below the bar |
| `ParentHome.tsx` | 1293 | progress-bar label |

`goalHours` is printed on those same lines and is also a raw passthrough. It reads fine today because the seeded goals are whole numbers, so an override like `62.5` would expose it the same way. Round both sides of the `value / max` pair.

## The one constraint

Round at the format boundary only. Do not round `confirmedHours` before the progress bar does its own arithmetic, which module doc #82-105 is explicit about.

## Size and tier

Three display strings. No schema change, no write path, no exported signature change, and nothing to coordinate across workflows. This is a FAST-tier row under item 26.

One decision the implementer has to make: there is no shared hours formatter to call. `src/lib/format/` holds date helpers only, and `StudentHome`, `ParentHome`, `CoachHome` and `HoursTab` each define their own private `round1`. So either call `.toFixed(1)` at the three sites, or add a shared formatter and leave the four copies of `round1` for a later cleanup. The second is tidier and slightly wider than FAST's "presentation-only" framing, so pick one deliberately rather than drifting into it.

## Suggested priority: low urgency, low cost

Fix it when someone is already in these files. Two reasons it can wait:

1. No student appears to have seen it. T509 records the owner confirming there is no live system and no attendance records as of 2026-08-05. Confirmed hours derive from that data, so the wrong-looking number is most likely reaching nobody yet. Worth confirming, because it stops being true the moment real hours land.
2. Nothing is blocked on it. No dependencies, and no other row cites it.

It should be fixed before real students use the app, since it is one of the first numbers they will look at.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` on 2026-08-09 rather than taken from the filing. The core claim holds. Three details in the original were off:

* **ParentHome is at** `:1293`**, not \~1280.**
* **ParentHome does not "do the same" in full.** It renders the progress-bar label only. There is no second supporting line there, so this is three render sites, not four.
* **The filing did not say why the value is unrounded.** Naming `v_student_goal_projection` as the source matters, because it rules out fixing this by reaching for the local `round1` sitting a few hundred lines up in the same file.

issues.title: T809 — `StudentHome`'s Sign up / Can't go control writes nothing and says nothing — a documented deferral with no follow-up row
issues.description:
A student taps **Sign up** on their home page, the button flips, and the answer is thrown away. Nothing on screen says so, and a reload restores the old state.

The same student answering the same question on `/outreach/:eventId` gets a real database write. The control there calls the shared upsert; the home-page control calls `setRsvps` and stops.

## Why it is worth fixing

A discarded `going` does more than reset a toggle. `v_planned_rsvp_hours` is built `from rsvps ... where r.status = 'going'` (`20260723000001_dashboard_views.sql:71-80`), and two figures read through it:

* the student's own **planned hours**, via `v_student_planned_hours` (`:95-98`) into `v_student_goal_projection`, printed on this same page;
* the coach's **upcoming 30-day committed hours** tile, via `v_season_upcoming_committed_hours` (`:112-116`).

A student who signs up here stays invisible to headcount planning, and the planned figure on their own screen never moves. Data-honesty class, not cosmetics.

## Why it happens

`StudentHome.tsx:1442-1445` is the entire handler, and it documents its own defect:

```ts
function handleRsvpChange(sessionId: string, status: RsvpStatus): void {
  // Module doc #7: local-only. No Supabase write happens here.
  setRsvps((prev) => withLocalRsvpOverride(prev, studentId, sessionId, status));
}
```

The write it should call already exists and already has two callers. `makeSubmitRsvpChange` (`loaders/outreach.ts:1219`) is documented as *"the ONE real* `rsvps` *upsert, shared by both* `RsvpControl.tsx` *(student self-RSVP) and* `ParentRsvp.tsx` *(parent RSVP-on-behalf)"*. Both components are imported and rendered by `OutreachDetail.tsx` (`:807`, `:812`), routed at `/outreach/:eventId` behind `RequireAuth` with no role gate (`router.tsx:248-255`). Nothing needs building. This control was never connected.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1442 | `handleRsvpChange`, local state only |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1243 | "Can't go" menu item on a Next-up row |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1268, 1273 | "Sign up" / "Can't go" buttons on a sign-up opportunity |
| `ParentHome.tsx` | 1255 | the same non-writing handler, not named in the filing |

`ParentHome` **carries the same control and the same silence, and its stated reason has expired.** Its module doc at `:194-196` defers the write to *"OUT-06's full scope, owned by* `ParentRsvp.tsx`*/T043, currently Blocked, a Forbidden File never imported here"*. T043 passed, and `ParentRsvp` is imported and rendered at `OutreachDetail.tsx:807`. Fix both sites together, or record why not.

## The one constraint

RLS rejects the obvious wiring. Both write policies on `rsvps` require `responded_by = auth.uid()` (`20260717000002_rls.sql:205-212`), and `makeSubmitRsvpChange` takes `respondedBy` from its caller and never re-derives it (`outreach.ts:1210-1211` says so explicitly). `StudentHome`'s `studentId` is the `students` row id, not the auth user id, so passing it gets the write denied rather than saved wrong. Read the responder from the session.

The two controls also hit different policies. A sign-up opportunity has no `rsvps` row yet, so it inserts under `own_or_linked_write`; the Next-up "Can't go" only renders for a row the student is already going to (`StudentHome.tsx:1246`), so it updates under `own_or_linked_update`. Both need the same `responded_by`.

## Size and tier

Two handlers and one existing loader function. No new schema, no new write path, no new view. The real addition is the pending and error states a network write needs and a no-op does not.

Tier unjudged, because item 28c makes that the picker's first act.

One thing to decide rather than drift into: `responded_by` became visible to teammates after T504 widened `rsvps` reads, disclosed in D013. A parent answering on a student's behalf is legible to the whole team, which is intended but worth confirming before wiring the `ParentHome` half.

## Suggested priority: medium urgency, low cost

Wire it before students get accounts.

1. **No student appears to have hit it yet.** Public go-live is still an unopened human gate (`GAM-80`/T070, Backlog), as is the MIG-06 cutover (`GAM-75`/T065). A production database does exist, so confirm rather than assume.
2. **Nothing is blocked on it.** No row cites T809.

It stops being deferrable at the go-live gate. This sits on the first screen a student sees, and the failure is silent, so nobody reports it as a bug. They go missing from the headcount instead.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`fcaa66d`) on 2026-08-10. The filing's line numbers and its quoted comment are exact and still current. Three things it does not say:

* **It names one render site; there are two.** `ParentHome.tsx:1255` carries the same non-writing handler, and the comment justifying that deferral cites a blocker that has since cleared.
* **"the existing rsvp upsert path" now has a name and two callers to copy.** `makeSubmitRsvpChange`, `outreach.ts:1219`.
* **The consequence reaches the stored numbers**, through `v_planned_rsvp_hours`, which feeds both the student's planned figure and the coach's committed-hours tile.

**Traced in source, not driven in a browser.** The central claim needs no observation, since the handler states in a comment that it does not write. The two derived figures above are read from the view definitions and the render path. Confirm them with the `e2e-personas` harness before quoting them as observed.

issues.title: T1300 — Sweep the four non-"fixed" closures for residual work left behind when the row closed
issues.description:
Four rows closed on 2026-08-04/05 without anyone changing the code they named. This row re-reads those four against current `main` and asks one question of each: does anything in the tree still claim something the closure made untrue?

The four are **T163, T204, T801 and T805**. They are the non-`fixed` subset of the eleven rows the Linear migration surfaced as live issues because their `Status` cell was never updated when the Epic cell was marked closed.

**Default to "no residual". This row is not an instruction to find something.** A sweep that reopens all four has restated the closures, not swept them. Reopen a row only where the remaining work can be named with `file:line` evidence.

## Why it is worth fixing

Documentation-accuracy class. No user sees a difference and no behaviour changes.

The cost is that comments in this repo get cited as evidence. T204's own closure measured that happening: one wrong sentence in `ParticipationTab.tsx` was copied into `reports.ts`, which `dashboard.ts` then cited in turn, so a single bad premise became three files of wrong reasoning, each pointing at the previous as its source. Agents read these module docs before touching the code under them.

## Why residuals hide here

A row that closes because someone fixed the thing leaves a diff. A row that closes because something *else* changed leaves prose describing a world that no longer exists.

T703 is the worked example and the reason this row exists. It closed 2026-08-05 as superseded by T702, correctly. `HoursTab.tsx` module doc #6 went on saying the meeting fixture existed *"specifically to prove this file does not silently drop non-outreach events from this sum"*, a proof T702's deletion had already made undeliverable. An agent measured that on 2026-08-09: filtering `buildSeasonTotals`'s sessions to `type === 'outreach'` leaves `peopleReachedTotal` at 125, unchanged. Entry at `verification-log.md:11408`.

## The four rows in scope

| Row | Closed | Why it closed | Verification log |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| T163 | 2026-08-05 | Premise wrong. The row said `loaders/reports.ts` had 0 tests; all six exports were already exercised by the `pages/reports` tab suites. | `:10511` |
| T204 | 2026-08-05 | No change to the named site. `loaders/students.ts` was already corrected by T186 in PR #75; the closure corrected three other files instead. | `:10184` |
| T801 | 2026-08-04 | No change to the named file. Corrections landed in a new migration's catalog comments, because item 10 forbids editing the applied one. | `:9814` |
| T805 | 2026-08-05 | Unreproducible. Eight failed reproductions across isolated, loaded and full-suite-loaded runs. | `:10107` |

The other seven of the eleven are out of scope: T201, T509, T700, T701, T802 and T803 closed as `fixed`, and T703 is now resolved.

## The one candidate found so far, with evidence

`src/lib/supabase/loaders/kpi.ts:64-75` still carries the RLS claim T204's closure corrected everywhere it looked:

> `v_season_kpis`/`v_season_kpi_team_counts` are plain views with no `security definer`/`security barrier` clause (this task's own migration), so both run under the querying session's own RLS

Two things make it a live residual rather than a fourth copy nobody reads:

1. **It cites the paragraph that now contradicts it.** `kpi.ts:64` names `loaders/reports.ts`'s module doc #7 as its authority. That doc starts at `reports.ts:125`, and `:135-143` is a **T204 CORRECTION** block stating the opposite conclusion. The citation still resolves; the source has changed its mind.
2. `kpi.ts` **is the only file in this family without a correction block.** `students.ts:369` (T186), `reports.ts:135` (T204), `dashboard.ts:77` (T204) and `ParticipationTab.tsx:63` (T204, the origin of the chain) all carry one. `grep -n CORRECTION src/lib/supabase/loaders/kpi.ts` returns nothing.

issues.title: CoachHome's goal-projection row prints the same raw float hours T808 fixed for students and parents
issues.description:
Found while implementing [GAM-303](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-303/t808-students-and-parents-see-raw-float-hours-39999983633333334-100-h) (T808), by tracing `v_student_goal_projection`'s consumers rather than the three render sites T808 named. Measured against `main` at `d709bab`, not inferred.

## The defect

`CoachHome.tsx:2050` (`GoalProjectionRowItem`) renders:

```
`${row.confirmedHours}h confirmed + ${row.plannedHours}h planned = ${totalHours}h / ${row.goalHours}h · ${percent}% · ${annotation}`
```

`totalHours` (`:2046`) and `percent` go through the file's private `round1`. `row.confirmedHours`, `row.plannedHours` and `row.goalHours` do not — they are printed raw.

Those three fields come from `v_student_goal_projection` via `loaders/dashboard.ts:404` (`queryGoalProjection`), which applies no rounding. It is the same view, the same unrounded columns, and the same passthrough shape as the student and parent surfaces T808 fixed through `loaders/students.ts:457`. The view itself (`20260723000001_dashboard_views.sql:322-334`) coalesces `v_student_hours.confirmed_hours` straight through, and that is where the float division happens.

So a coach opening the dashboard sees the identical `3.9999983633333334h confirmed + 0h planned = 4h / 100h` reading, mixing a raw float and a rounded total inside one sentence.

## This corrects a claim in [GAM-303](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-303/t808-students-and-parents-see-raw-float-hours-39999983633333334-100-h)

[GAM-303](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-303/t808-students-and-parents-see-raw-float-hours-39999983633333334-100-h) states that "the coach looking up the same student sees `4.0`", and treats that as evidence students are shown a number the coach is not. **The** `4.0` **comes from the Reports → Hours tab** (`HoursTab.tsx:1017`, `renderHoursCell` → `value.toFixed(1)`), which is a different surface. **The coach *dashboard* has the bug too** — nobody had checked it. The cross-role inconsistency in [GAM-303](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-303/t808-students-and-parents-see-raw-float-hours-39999983633333334-100-h) was real, but it was reports-vs-home, not coach-vs-student.

## Why it was not folded into [GAM-303](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-303/t808-students-and-parents-see-raw-float-hours-39999983633333334-100-h)

[GAM-303](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-303/t808-students-and-parents-see-raw-float-hours-39999983633333334-100-h)'s scope is an explicit three-site table in two files, and `CoachHome.tsx` is in neither. Filed rather than silently widened, per constitution item 20.

## Fix

Same shape as T808: format at the render boundary only, one decimal, matching `HoursTab.tsx`'s `renderHoursCell` convention. Do **not** round `row.confirmedHours` before `ProgressBar` at `:2055` receives it — `aria-valuenow` must keep the real number, which is the constraint T808's own tests now guard on the student and parent pages.

`percent` and `totalHours` already read correctly and need no change.

## Tier

FAST under item 26: one display string, no write path, no schema, no exported signature change. `CoachHome.test.tsx` will have assertions pinned to the current unformatted digits — check them for the vacuous-negative shape T808 hit (`not.toContain('0 h confirmed …')` passes trivially once the format changes).

---

*Generated by [Claude Code](<https://claude.ai/code>)*

---

## Corrections to this issue's own citations, and to a nearby one

**My line numbers were 12 low and are fixed above.** Re-measured against `origin/main` at `252e400`: the render is `:2050`, `totalHours` is `:2046`, the `ProgressBar` is `:2055`. An agent on `claude/w1-linear-autoclose` reached `:2050` independently — same defect, same line, two measurements.

**One thing to get right before fixing this.** That agent's commit message says the Reports Hours tab "rounds at `HoursTab.tsx:605`". `:605` rounds **team subtotals only** (`round1(group.rows.reduce(...))`). The `4.0` a coach reads on a **per-student** row comes from `renderHoursCell` at `:1017`, which is `value.toFixed(1)`.

The distinction decides this fix: `round1` renders `4`, `.toFixed(1)` renders `4.0`. [GAM-303](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-303/t808-students-and-parents-see-raw-float-hours-39999983633333334-100-h) shipped `.toFixed(1)` to match `renderHoursCell`, so matching `round1` here would reintroduce a smaller version of the same cross-surface mismatch.

issues.title: replay.py cannot read Python test-runner output, so mutating a Python file needs a hand-written shim
issues.description:
An agent replaying a mutation against a Python test file gets `UNTRUSTWORTHY: could not read the test counts of the baseline run` before a single mutation is applied. `unittest` prints `Ran 19 tests in 0.177s` / `OK`, and `pytest` prints `19 passed in 0.18s`; `replay.py` reads only the vitest/Jest `Tests  N failed | M passed (T)` line, so both are unreadable to it.

This surfaced while fixing [GAM-288](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-288/t612-mutation-replays-replaypy-reports-a-genuine-red-replay-as) (T612): proving that the skill's own new tests actually guard the parser fix required wrapping the runner in a throwaway shell script that re-printed `Ran N tests` as a vitest-shaped summary line. The mutations reddened correctly once wrapped, so nothing was left unproven — but the next agent has to invent that shim again, and an agent that does not think of it will read the refusal as "this cannot be replayed".

## Why it is worth fixing

Test-quality class, and specifically the friction that makes an agent skip the replay. `replay.py`'s refusal message is deliberately absolute ("Run the command by hand"), which is right when the summary is genuinely garbled and wrong when the runner is simply one the parser was never taught. The two Python scripts in `.claude/skills/` are the only Python under test today, but they include `replay.py` itself — the tool the constitution leans on — and its tests now run in CI as the `skill-scripts` job.

## Why it happens

`counts()` (`.claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/replay.py:105`) matches `SUMMARY_LINE_RE` (line 40), which anchors on a literal `Tests` label followed by `:` or two spaces. Neither Python runner emits anything of that shape. `SEGMENT_RE` (line 43) already accepts the words `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, `todo` and `pending`, so only the line-level anchor is missing, not the vocabulary.

The near-miss to warn about: it is tempting to loosen `SUMMARY_LINE_RE` until it matches pytest's `19 passed in 0.18s`. Doing that by dropping the label anchor would make the pattern match arbitrary prose in a stack trace, and the whole point of [GAM-288](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-288/t612-mutation-replays-replaypy-reports-a-genuine-red-replay-as) was that a summary read half-right is worse than one refused. A pytest/unittest shape needs its own anchored pattern, tried in turn.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `.claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/replay.py` | 40 | `SUMMARY_LINE_RE` — the vitest/Jest line anchor, the only shape recognised |
| `.claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/replay.py` | 105 | `counts()` — raises `SummaryParseError` when no line matches |
| `.claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/replay.py` | 132 | `counts_or_die()` — turns that into the exit-2 refusal an agent sees |
| `.claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/test_replay.py` | 33 | `SummaryParsing` — where the new shapes' fixtures belong |

## The one constraint

Whatever is added must keep [GAM-288](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-288/t612-mutation-replays-replaypy-reports-a-genuine-red-replay-as)'s rule intact: a shape not fully understood raises rather than returning a count. `unittest`'s failure line is `FAILED (failures=7)` with no total on it and the count on a separate `Ran N tests` line, so a Python reader has to combine two lines and then cross-check them the way the vitest path cross-checks against its declared total — not read one and assume the rest.

## Size and tier

One extra pattern pair plus a combining step (~30 lines), and fixtures for the four shapes: unittest OK, unittest FAILED, pytest all-pass, pytest with failures. No schema change, no write path, no signature change — `counts()` keeps returning `(failed, passed, skipped)`.

STANDARD under item 26: the change is well under FAST's ~20-line ceiling only if the combining step is trivial, and it is not.

Decide deliberately: whether pytest's `19 passed, 3 skipped in 0.18s` (no declared total) may be accepted at all, given that the cross-check [GAM-288](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-288/t612-mutation-replays-replaypy-reports-a-genuine-red-replay-as) added has nothing to check against there.

## Suggested priority: low urgency, low cost

Worth doing the next time anyone touches `replay.py`, not before.

1. It affects agents, not users, and it has been hit exactly once. The workaround is a four-line shell shim and the refusal message that precedes it is honest — nothing is silently wrong.
2. Nothing is blocked on it. [GAM-288](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-288/t612-mutation-replays-replaypy-reports-a-genuine-red-replay-as) shipped with all three of its mutations replayed.

It stops being deferrable when a second Python script under `.claude/skills/` acquires tests, or when a `skill-scripts` CI failure needs replaying under time pressure.

## Verification note

Measured on `claude/next-ready-task-pw1k2y` at `0d5adbd`, 2026-08-09. `python3 .claude/skills/mutation-replay/scripts/test_replay.py` prints `Ran 19 tests in 0.177s` then `OK`; `replay.py` run against it without the shim exits 2 at the baseline. Line numbers above are from that commit. pytest is **not installed** in this environment, so its output shape is quoted from its documented format and is unverified here — check it before writing the fixture.

Filed under constitution item 20 as a deliberate deferral from [GAM-288](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-288/t612-mutation-replays-replaypy-reports-a-genuine-red-replay-as) (T612).

issues.title: Linear → Claude dispatch is built and unit-tested but not live — 7 owner steps remain (PAT, secrets, webhook)
issues.description:
Moving an issue `Backlog → Todo` does not start an agent yet. The code that would do it is merged and tested; nothing is connected to it. Dispatch is still the manual two-step it was before — drag the card, then separately go and start an agent.

Seven steps stand between here and a working loop, and every one of them needs a credential or an admin session no agent has.

## Why it is worth fixing

This is the payoff of the dispatch build. Until it is done, the webhook is code nobody runs — the same class as the 224 Edge Function tests that CI had never executed (found during this build, now fixed).

Nothing is *broken* without it. Manual dispatch works. The cost is per-dispatch friction, not an outage.

## What is already done

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| `supabase/functions/linear-dispatch/` | signature verification, replay window, 8-rule event filter, GitHub dispatch |
| Tests | 45, green, guards proven by mutation |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | `repository_dispatch` → `claude-code-action@v1` |
| `supabase/config.toml` | `[functions.linear-dispatch] verify_jwt = false` |
| CI | new `edge-functions` job — 269 Deno tests across 6 function directories |

The four items that could have invalidated the design were resolved before any code was written; the evidence is in `docs/swarm/2026-08-09-linear-webhook-dispatch.md` §2.

## What remains

Full runbook with the exact commands is §6 of that document. In order — step 3 before step 1, or the first deliveries hit nothing:

1. ~~Create a **fine-grained GitHub PAT**, scoped to this repo, **Contents: read & write**.~~ **DONE 2026-08-09** — `volt-linear-dispatch`, owner `gamitch`, no expiration. Verified: `GET /user` → 200, `POST /dispatches` → 204.
2. ~~Add repository secrets.~~ **DONE 2026-08-09** — `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (subscription auth, chosen over an API key; the workflow input was changed to match), `LINEAR_DISPATCH_API_KEY` (Read + Write + Create comments, limited to Gamitch), `CLAUDE_PR_TOKEN`. The OAuth token was verified by a temporary smoke workflow that authenticated for real against the API — it first caught a whitespace character in the secret from a wrapped terminal paste, which would otherwise have surfaced at step 6 as an opaque auth failure.
3. **DONE 2026-08-09** — merge the workflow to `main`. PR #132, merged as `71d6ac9`. Verified on `main`: `claude-linear-dispatch.yml` present with `on: repository_dispatch, types: [linear-issue-dispatch]`, the edge function present, and `[functions.linear-dispatch] verify_jwt = false` in `supabase/config.toml`.
4. `supabase functions deploy linear-dispatch` + three `supabase secrets set` calls.
5. Create the Linear webhook (Settings → API → Webhooks), Issues only, copy the signing secret into step 4.
6. Move one real issue `Backlog → Todo` and confirm the Actions log says `Verified human actor`.
7. Edit an issue already in `Todo` and confirm it returns `{"dispatched": false, "reason": "STATE_UNCHANGED"}` with no workflow run.

## This issue auto-closed on merge, and item 28f says it should not have

PR #132 deliberately did **not** use the `Closes GAM-310` magic word, because four of the seven steps were still outstanding. It carried the identifier in its **title only**.

It closed anyway. Linear moved this issue `Backlog → In Progress` when the PR opened and `→ Done` when it merged, and assigned it. Reopened by hand to `In Progress`, which is the honest state — the owner is working steps 4–7 now.

**This contradicts constitution item 28f**, which states that an identifier in the title or branch name *"links only"* and *"on its own it leaves the issue sitting in* `In Review` *after merge"*. Observed behaviour: the title alone both links **and** closes. It also means the migration doc's outstanding item *"enable the Linear automation PR merged → Done"* is already done — the automation is live.

The consequence matters for every agent following item 28: **omitting the magic word is not a way to avoid closing an issue.** An agent that finishes part of a multi-step issue and opens a PR naming it will have that issue closed on merge whatever it does. Either the identifier must be kept out of the PR title entirely, or partial work needs its own issue.

## A second constraint, found by merging two sessions' notes

**The retry schedule and the replay window are in direct tension.** Linear retries a failed delivery at 1 minute, 1 hour and 6 hours. The function's `isFresh` rejects anything more than 60 seconds from `webhookTimestamp`. So if Linear does not re-stamp the timestamp on retry, the 1-hour and 6-hour retries arrive as `STALE_DELIVERY` and retrying is defeated — precisely when it would matter, since a retry only follows a real failure.

The window stays at 60s: that is Linear's own published guidance, and widening it to six hours would trade a certain security property for a speculative reliability one. **Recovery is by re-dragging the card** — `Todo → In Progress → Todo` fires a fresh transition and dispatches normally.

Whether Linear re-stamps on retry is unverified and needs one real failed delivery to settle.

## The one constraint

**The PAT must be owned by a human GitHub account.** `github.actor` on the triggered run becomes the PAT's owner, and `claude-code-action`'s `checkHumanActor` throws unless `octokit.users.getByUsername(actor).type === "User"` (read from `src/github/validation/actor.ts`). A GitHub App installation token or a machine account resolves to type `Bot` and the run dies before Claude starts.

The error message it produces talks about bots and `allowed_bots`, so it reads like a configuration problem rather than the token-identity problem it is. `allowed_bots` **is not the fix** — it would admit bot-triggered runs generally, discarding the loop protection instead of satisfying it.

Two more that waste an afternoon each:

* `repository_dispatch` only runs workflows from the **default branch**, and a dispatch matching no workflow still returns **204**. Step 3 before step 6.
* Supabase's JWT rejection happens *before* function code runs, so a misconfigured `verify_jwt` produces **no log line at all**. Step 4's check distinguishes the two 401s: `INVALID_SIGNATURE` is ours and correct; a 401 about a missing JWT means the config did not take (`supabase/cli#4059`).

## Size and tier

Roughly 30 minutes of console work: one token, four secrets, one deploy, one webhook form, two verification moves. No code changes. No schema change, no write path, no signature change.

**Tier: FAST.** No packet, no worker, no checker — but verification is not reduced: steps 6 and 7 are the verification, and step 7 (the negative case) is the one worth not skipping. A filter that drops everything looks identical to one with nothing to do.

`gate/human` because no machine can create a PAT or a Linear webhook. The dispatch filter itself skips `gate/human`, so this issue cannot dispatch an agent at itself.

## Suggested priority: medium urgency, low cost

Do it when manual dispatch starts costing more than 30 minutes of setup — which is soon, but not today.

1. Nothing is blocked. Manual dispatch works and is what everything has used so far.
2. Blocks nothing else. No issue depends on this landing.

**Stops being deferrable** when the queue is being worked by agents often enough that the manual step is the bottleneck, or if the built code starts to rot — an unrun webhook decays silently, which is the whole argument for doing it while the context is fresh.

## Verification note

Written 2026-08-09 against `main` at the time of the build. Every constraint above was measured rather than inherited:

* `tier/fast` **is not a label name, and the filter was written wrong because of it.** The workspace stores a label *group* `tier` whose children are named bare — `fast`, `standard`, `heavy`, `unreviewed`. The slashes in every project document are synthesised by `scripts/linear-export.mjs`. The original filter matched `name.startsWith('tier/')` and would have matched nothing, ever, skipping every issue with the plausible-sounding reason `NO_TIER_LABEL`. Caught by reading the live label set; reverting the fix turns 6 tests red.
* **Free-plan webhooks were the largest open risk and are available.** Linear's pricing matrix lists "API and webhook access" as a Core row; creation requires workspace admin, and on the Free plan all members are admins.
* **Not yet verified end to end.** Steps 1–5 of the human-actor chain each check out individually; the composition needs one real dispatch. That is step 6, and it is the only thing that can prove it.

issues.title: kpi_views.sql's two views never got T801's catalog-comment RLS correction -- D010 chose header-prose only
issues.description:
No user-visible surface. `\d+ v_season_kpis` / `obj_description('public.v_season_kpis'::regclass)` in the live Postgres catalog still returns nothing for either KPI view — the only correction of the RLS misconception lives in a migration file's prose, not in the database a reader can actually query.

## Why it is worth fixing

Documentation-accuracy class, same family as T204/T801/T1300 (GAM-307). No behaviour changes and no user sees a difference; the cost is that a future reader who inspects the schema directly — `\d+`, `psql`, a DB client, or a script that reads `obj_description()` — sees no correction at all for these two views, only the original wrong claim's absence of any comment (the views were never commented in the first place; the false claim lives only in the migration's block comment, not a `comment on view`). A reader who trusts what the catalog itself says has nothing pointing them at the correction.

## Why it happens

Two different, both-legitimate closures fixed the same false RLS claim for two different sets of views, using two different mechanisms:

* **D010** (`docs/swarm/dispute-log.md:898`) found `supabase/migrations/20260723000000_kpi_views.sql:137-152` claiming `v_season_kpis`/`v_season_kpi_team_counts` "run under the querying session's own RLS" because neither carries a `security definer`/`security barrier` clause. False — the real per-view knob is `security_invoker` (PG15+, defaults off, zero real occurrences under `supabase/`), so both views execute as their owner and do not apply caller RLS to their base tables. Closed 2026-08-04, **option B**: correct the claim in the *header prose* of the next new migration, because constitution item 10 forbids editing the applied `kpi_views.sql` in place. That correction landed in `supabase/migrations/20260804000001_widen_rsvp_read_all_authenticated.sql:62-72`.
* **T801** (`docs/swarm/task-ledger.md`, search `T801`) found the same false claim, plus a second one, in `dashboard_views.sql`'s nine views. Closed 2026-08-04/05 via a *different* mechanism, **option (a)**: a new additive migration, `supabase/migrations/20260805000000_dashboard_views_comment_corrections.sql`, using `comment on view ...` / `comment on column ...` to write the correction directly into the Postgres catalog — queryable with `\d+` or `obj_description()`, not just readable in a migration file.

D010 never considered option (a); it was offered only "edit in place" (A, rejected — item 10) vs. "header of next migration" (B, chosen). T801's catalog-comment mechanism did not exist yet when D010 closed. Nobody has since asked whether it should be extended to the two KPI views, and grep confirms it was not: `grep -n "v_season_kpis\|v_season_kpi_team_counts" supabase/migrations/20260805000000_dashboard_views_comment_corrections.sql` returns nothing.

**This is not a re-litigation of D010's substantive risk call.** George's ruling that the schema itself should not change (`security_invoker` not worth the risk, views expose only season aggregates with no PII) stands and is not in question. The only open question is whether the *documentation mechanism* T801 established one day later should be applied consistently to the two views D010 covered.

## Where it renders / lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `supabase/migrations/20260723000000_kpi_views.sql` | 137-152 | Original false RLS claim, applied migration, cannot be edited in place (item 10). |
| `supabase/migrations/20260804000001_widen_rsvp_read_all_authenticated.sql` | 62-72 | D010's chosen correction — header prose only, not a catalog comment. |
| `supabase/migrations/20260805000000_dashboard_views_comment_corrections.sql` | 100-125 | T801's `comment on view` pattern for the nine `dashboard_views.sql` views — the precedent this row asks whether to extend. |

## The one constraint

Any correction goes in a new additive migration — constitution item 10 makes editing an applied migration file a BLOCKER, which is exactly why both D010 and T801 took the shape they did.

## Size and tier

One new migration, `comment on view` for two views only (mirrors T801's own two-statement shape, just fewer views). No schema change, no write path, no signature change — comment-only, same as T801's migration, which the ledger records as `self-verified (4 assertions + 4 mutations, live PG16)` at what reads as FAST-tier rigor rather than a full HEAVY packet.

Likely **tier/fast** or **tier/standard** despite touching a migration file: item 26 lists "a migration or metric-view SQL" as a HEAVY trigger, but T801 itself — the direct precedent for this exact shape (comment-only additive migration, `comment on view`, no view definition or data touched) — was closed by the orchestrator directly rather than through a full premise-gate/worker/checker cycle. Whoever picks this up should judge the tier fresh per item 28d rather than default to either reading; note the tension either way.

The implementer must decide (or escalate) whether to reuse T801's own `20260805000000...` correction text verbatim (same fact, same wording) or write new, KPI-view-specific wording — a judgment call, not something to default into.

## Suggested priority: low urgency, low cost

Do it whenever someone is next touching `kpi_views.sql` or wants the two documentation-correction mechanisms in this repo to agree with each other.

1. No user sees anything different either way. Nobody has ever queried these views' catalog comments directly as far as the record shows.
2. Nothing is blocked on it.

Stops being deferrable if a future migration or generated-docs process starts reading view catalog comments programmatically (mirroring how T703's residual was found because *reading* stale prose, not running it, was what mattered) — at that point an inconsistent correction mechanism between the two view families becomes a real trap.

## Verification note

Checked against `main` (`fcaa66d`) on 2026-08-10, while working GAM-307 (T1300). All three citations above (D010's location and closure, T801's migration and its two-statement pattern, the grep showing the KPI views are absent from it) were re-verified directly rather than taken from GAM-307's own filing text, which first raised this gap. GAM-307 separately corrected `src/lib/supabase/loaders/kpi.ts`'s own stale copy of the same false RLS claim (a TypeScript comment, in scope for that row and already shipped) — that fix is unrelated to and does not substitute for the SQL-catalog question this row asks.

issues.title: Two live dispatch policies exist only as file comments — no constitution item, so nothing triages them
issues.description:
Every Linear-dispatched run now picks its orchestrator model from a rule that exists only as a YAML comment, and avoids a delegation trap documented only in `SWARM-QUICKSTART.md`. Neither is a constitution item.

An agent that reads `constitution.md` end-to-end — which is what the dispatch prompt tells it to do first — will not find either one.

## Why it is worth fixing

This is item 20's class, applied to the process rather than to code: a decision recorded in a comment is not triaged. Item 20 exists because three correct scope deferrals were recorded only in comments and each shipped a defect; item 24 records the same shape turned on the ledger, *"a record written once, never triaged, silently drifting from reality."*

The concrete exposure is narrow but real. Nothing binds the next person editing `claude_args` to keep the subagent tool in the allowlist, and dropping it is silent — it produces a run that starts, works, and delivers one model playing every role. That failure has been measured once: [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says)'s run spent $9.16 and 24.5 minutes to produce no branch, no commit and no PR. The model mapping is equally unprotected: anyone editing the YAML can change which tier gets a frontier orchestrator, with no amendment and no record.

## Why it happens

Both policies were written during a dispatch-failure investigation on 2026-08-10 (PR #138) by an agent that is not `boss-architect`. Authority Boundaries reserve constitution edits to `boss-architect` and `boss-arbiter`, so the agent that found the gap structurally could not close it — it could only record each policy where it was permitted to write, and flag the ratification as outstanding.

That is the rule working correctly and the record ending up incomplete. Closing it is a boss-agent act, not a documentation fix.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 278 | the `--model` expression: `opus` for `heavy`/`unreviewed`, `sonnet` for `standard`/`fast` |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 226-275 | that policy's whole rationale, and its own note that ratification is outstanding |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 280 | the `Task,Agent` grant the delegation trap is about |
| `SWARM-QUICKSTART.md` | 108-127 | "Model Selection — how it actually works" |
| `SWARM-QUICKSTART.md` | 128-157 | "Automation caveat", including its own "not a constitution item" disclaimer |
| `docs/swarm/constitution.md` | 22-24 | Authority Boundaries — why the filing agent could not do this itself |
| `docs/swarm/constitution.md` | 69-80 | item 18, which covers the **worker's** model and nothing else |

## The one constraint

**Do not widen item 18 to absorb this.** Item 18's `model: "opus"` override is per-dispatch and its trigger depends on what the task turns out to touch — migrations, RLS or `security definer`, metric-view SQL, auth/session/role logic. The item says so explicitly: *"The override goes on the dispatch call, not in the agent definition — there is one worker prompt, not two."* No label and no config file can express that, which is exactly why the workflow does not try. A new item belongs **beside** item 18, governing the orchestrator, not inside it.

Second constraint, item 3 (rules live in one place): ratifying means the two comment blocks **shrink to pointers**, not that the text is duplicated into `constitution.md` and left in the files as well. Two copies of a rule is the state item 3 exists to prevent.

## Size and tier

Two constitution items, roughly 30-50 lines of `docs/swarm/constitution.md`, plus trimming two comment blocks to pointers. No code, no schema, no write path.

Tier unjudged, because item 28c makes that the picker's first act. One input to that judgement: it cannot be FAST as item 26 defines it — FAST requires *"a named mutation exists that turns a test red"*, and no test covers `constitution.md` or a workflow YAML. That constraint is itself worth a separate row.

## Suggested priority: medium urgency, low cost

Ratify before the next hand touches `claude_args`.

1. **Nothing is broken today.** Both policies are live and behaving correctly in the merged files; the risk is drift, not malfunction. No agent has been observed misreading them — the automation caveat is four hours old at filing.
2. **Nothing is blocked on it.** No row cites this.

It stops being deferrable the next time anyone edits `claude_args`, or the next time a dispatched run has to be diagnosed — whichever lands first. Both are exactly the moments the missing rule would have done its work.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`f2ca7e5`) on 2026-08-10. All line numbers above are post-merge and current. Two things worth separating, because they are not the same kind of decision:

* **The orchestrator-model policy is already owner-authorized.** The owner's words are quoted verbatim at `claude-linear-dispatch.yml:241-248`. Ratifying it is transcription into the constitution's own house form, not a new decision.
* **The automation caveat is NOT owner-authorized.** It is a measured finding written up by the investigating agent. Turning it into a binding item is a genuine new decision and should be treated as one, not waved through alongside the first.

issues.title: `RESUME-HERE.md` is the first file nine kickoff prompts tell an agent to read, and the word "Linear" appears in it zero times
issues.description:
A fresh orchestrator session is told to read `docs/swarm/RESUME-HERE.md` before anything else. It is 1,337 lines, its newest UPDATE section is dated 2026-08-05, and it contains no occurrence of the string "Linear" — in any case.

Line 9 tells the reader what to do next: *"read this, then* `constitution.md`*, then the open rows in* `task-ledger.md`*."* Item 29 froze `task-ledger.md` four days after that sentence was written.

## Why it is worth fixing

An agent that follows the file works from a frozen ledger and never learns the `Todo` column exists. Item 28 was authorized because of the mirror-image failure — its own rationale reads *"A queue nobody is told to consume is a document, not a dispatch system."* This is the same gap from the other side: an agent told, in detail and with authority, to consume the wrong one.

The blast radius is the orientation step, not the work, so nothing corrupts. What it costs is the first several turns of any session that starts this way, and a plausible wrong model of where work comes from carried into everything after.

## Why it happens

Items 28 and 29 moved dispatch to Linear and froze the ledger on 2026-08-09. `AGENTS.md` was updated the same day. `RESUME-HERE.md` was not, and neither was `KICKOFF-PROMPTS.md`.

**The staleness is already disclosed — but only in the Codex-branded file.** `AGENTS.md:92-95` says `RESUME-HERE.md` and `state-summary.md` *"predate the Linear migration and are not a dispatch source; use them only when a current document points to a specific entry."* That is accurate and sufficient for any agent that reaches it. Nothing in `RESUME-HERE.md` itself says so, and the nine kickoff prompts that name it carry no such warning.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `docs/swarm/RESUME-HERE.md` | 9 | "read this, then `constitution.md`, then the open rows in `task-ledger.md`" |
| `docs/swarm/RESUME-HERE.md` | 16 | the newest UPDATE, dated 2026-08-05 — four days before items 28-30 |
| `docs/swarm/KICKOFF-PROMPTS.md` | 56, 143, 236, 350, 476, 570, 650, 718, 884 | nine prompts opening "Read in this order before doing anything: docs/swarm/RESUME-HERE.md" |
| `AGENTS.md` | 92-95 | the existing disclosure — accurate, and in the file written for Codex |

## The one constraint

**Do not rewrite or delete the history.** `RESUME-HERE.md` is provenance for pre-migration work and is cited by name from live ledger rows — T063b, T183 and T403 each point at it for reasoning that exists nowhere else. Item 29's argument for freezing the ledger rather than deleting it applies here unchanged.

The fix is a banner at the top saying what supersedes what, in the shape `SWARM-QUICKSTART.md` now carries. A rewrite would destroy the record; a deletion would break the citations.

Second trap: the file's own convention is that dated UPDATE sections supersede downward, newest first. A banner must sit **above** the 2026-08-05 UPDATE and say it is not one, or the next reader will treat it as just another dated entry and read past it.

## Size and tier

One banner of roughly eight lines at the top of `RESUME-HERE.md`, plus a one-line warning in the nine `KICKOFF-PROMPTS.md` prompts — or one line in a shared preamble if those prompts can share one. No code, no schema, no write path.

Tier unjudged, because item 28c makes that the picker's first act.

## Suggested priority: medium urgency, low cost

Fix it before the next session is started from a kickoff prompt.

1. **No agent has been observed misled by it.** The dispatch prompt points at `AGENTS.md`, not at this file, so dispatched runs get the accurate disclosure at `AGENTS.md:92`. The exposure is to sessions the owner starts by hand from `KICKOFF-PROMPTS.md`, which is how this file is actually reached. [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says)'s failed run is **not** evidence either way — its transcript was never captured, so what it read is unknown and should not be claimed.
2. **Nothing is blocked on it.** No row cites this.

It stops being deferrable at the next hand-started session, which is a matter of days rather than weeks.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`f2ca7e5`) on 2026-08-10. Every figure above was measured rather than recalled: 1,337 lines, 92,064 bytes, `grep -ci linear` returns 0, newest UPDATE at line 16.

* **A correction worth keeping.** The investigating session first characterised this as undisclosed staleness. That was wrong: `AGENTS.md:92-95` discloses it plainly. The finding that survives is narrower — the disclosure lives only in the Codex-branded file, while the file itself and all nine kickoff prompts still read as current. The original framing would have sent an implementer to write a disclosure that already exists.
* **Nine call sites, not two.** An earlier count in the same session said two. `grep -n RESUME-HERE docs/swarm/KICKOFF-PROMPTS.md` returns nine, at the lines tabled above. An implementer working from the earlier number would have left seven prompts untouched.

issues.title: A dispatched run reports `success` while its work is still "running in the background" — and the process takes it
issues.description:
Dispatch run 31354278407 finished green. It had written a HEAVY task packet, run a premise gate that proved six RLS paths against a real PostgreSQL cluster, and got back a REVISE. Then it ended its turn with this sentence:

> Round 2 is running in the background.

The process exited and took round 2 with it. Nothing was pushed, no PR was opened, and the issue was left in `In Progress`. GitHub shows a green tick.

## Second instance, 2026-08-10, run 31385764526 — and it is not a turn-budget problem

Reproduced on the run that finally did the real work. Final report opens:

> Worker complete and independently verified on the critical path. **The checker is still running.**

```json
{ "subtype": "success", "is_error": false, "num_turns": 54, "total_cost_usd": 28.583486399999988 }
```

Job green at 12:56:43. No PR. [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) left `In Progress`. The `checker-reviewer` was spawned and died with the process — **54 turns of 300 and 59 minutes of 120**, so neither cap was close to binding. The agent simply ended its turn with a subagent in flight.

**What changed since the first instance is the blast radius, not the bug.** PR #141's run-log requirement meant this run left everything behind: the worker's commit `4460dec` (four files, +715/−44), eight run-log commits recording each milestone, and an uploaded artifact. Nothing needed hand-salvaging. The failure cost one checker round, not a run.

That is the argument for fixing this at the assertion rather than treating the run log as sufficient: durability turned a total loss into a partial one, but the run still reports success while a required chain step never happened, and item 28e's `In Review` never arrives.

## Why it is worth fixing

This is strictly more dangerous than the `error_max_turns` failure it replaced. That one failed loudly and cost $9.16; this one costs $11.36, produces genuinely valuable work, reports success, and discards it. A green run that delivered nothing reads as "done" on every surface a human checks.

The class is evidence-honesty: the run's own exit status contradicts its own final sentence, and the exit status is what everything downstream believes.

## Why it happens

The run's last message announces work it has not finished, in the present continuous. Whatever it dispatched — a round-2 gate — was still in flight when the agent's turn ended, and the SDK returns as soon as the turn does. There is no post-run assertion anywhere in the workflow that anything survived: not that a branch was pushed, not that a PR exists, not that the issue moved off `In Progress`.

`error_max_turns` is caught because the action itself raises it. Nothing raises "the agent stopped mid-chain", because from the SDK's point of view it did not stop — it returned normally.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 88-280 | the `Work the issue` step — succeeds on any non-error SDK return |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 174-198 | the artifact and session-id steps, the only post-run steps, and both are `if: always()` bookkeeping rather than assertions |
| `docs/swarm/constitution.md` | 451-456 | item 28e — "on completion move the issue to `In Review`", the condition that was not met and not checked |

## The one constraint

**Do not make this a turn-budget problem.** It is not, and there are now two measurements: run 31354278407 stopped at **44 turns of 200**, and run 31385764526 at **54 turns of 300** with half its 120-minute clock unused. Raising anything makes no difference, and reading this as "needs more room" would repeat the diagnosis error that produced the 80-turn cap in the first place.

The other trap is asserting on the wrong signal. A PR is not the right check — a correct refusal to proceed (which the dispatch prompt explicitly invites) produces no PR and must not fail the run. The honest assertion is narrower: **the issue must not still be in** `In Progress` **when the run ends.** `In Review` means finished, `Todo` means correctly declined; `In Progress` means the agent stopped holding a claim it never released.

## Size and tier

One post-run step in the workflow that reads the issue's state through `scripts/linear/client.mjs` and fails the job if it is still `In Progress`. Roughly 15-25 lines of YAML plus a small script path. No schema, no write path, no source change.

Tier unjudged, because item 28c makes that the picker's first act. Note it cannot be FAST as item 26 defines it — no test covers a workflow YAML, so no named mutation can turn one red. That gap is `GAM-312`'s territory.

## Suggested priority: high urgency, low cost

Do this before the next heavy row is dispatched.

1. **It has already cost real work once, today.** Run 31354278407's packet and gate verdict survived only because they were pulled out of the run artifact by hand and committed in PR #139. Left alone they would have expired on 2026-09-09 with nobody aware anything was missing.
2. **Nothing is blocked on it**, but everything dispatched after it is exposed. The failure is silent by construction, so the second occurrence will be found the same way the first was — by someone looking for an unrelated reason.

It stops being deferrable at the next HEAVY dispatch, because that is the tier where the chain is long enough to be interrupted partway.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`f2ca7e5`) on 2026-08-10. Every figure is quoted from the run's own transcript rather than inferred:

* result object: `{"subtype": "success", "is_error": false, "num_turns": 44, "duration_ms": 1891393, "total_cost_usd": 11.356751750000003}`
* `git ls-remote --heads origin` has no `claude/gam-304-wire-rsvp-controls`, the branch the packet names
* `list_pull_requests(state=open)` returned `[]`
* [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) state history shows `In Progress` from 04:03:43Z with no later transition

**One thing deliberately not claimed:** whether round 2 would have succeeded. It never ran, so its verdict is unknown, and no part of this row depends on guessing it.

issues.title: Any branch named `claude/gam-nnn-*` closes that issue on merge — item 28f says it only links, and that is false here
issues.description:
[GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) was marked `Done` at 04:02:01Z by a pull request that did not touch a single line of its work. It stayed closed for twenty seconds and was rescued only by an unrelated move back to `Todo`.

The PR was #138, a CI-workflow change. Its author deliberately omitted `Closes GAM-304` from the body for exactly this reason. It made no difference.

## The inverse also happens, and it is worse — measured 2026-08-10

The PR that actually fixed [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) did **not** close it. It moved the issue *backwards*, and the owner closed it by hand.

Every merge against this issue, from its own state history:

```
04:02:01  #138 merged   In Progress -> Done          <- touched none of its code
04:56:38  #139 merged   In Progress -> Done          <- touched none of its code
05:29:22  #140 merged   In Progress -> Done          <- touched none of its code
11:54:43  #141 merged   In Progress -> Done          <- touched none of its code
14:00:04  #143 merged   In Review   -> In Progress   <- the actual fix, body line 1 `Closes GAM-304`
14:18:16  owner, by hand           -> In Review -> Done
```

So the magic word item 28f prescribes did not fire, while four unrelated branch-name links each closed the row. **The automation is not merely over-eager; on the one occasion it mattered it did the wrong thing in the other direction.**

**Hypothesis, not verified:** the automation reacts to the *aggregate* state of all linked PRs rather than to the merge event alone. Six PRs are attached to [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) (#138-#143), every one linked by an identifier in its branch name. When #143 merged, #142 was still **open**, so a rule of the shape "issue has an open linked PR -> In Progress" would produce exactly the observed regression. The four earlier closes all happened when the merging PR was the last one open.

If that is right, the branch-naming convention does more than risk a wrong close: **every branch that merely mentions an identifier permanently joins the input set the automation computes from.** Six PRs on one issue, five of which were never its work.

This needs confirming in the Linear workspace's automation settings, which are outside the repository. Do not design a fix before reading them.

## Why it is worth fixing

An issue silently reaching `Done` is the worst failure this tracker has, because `Done` is the one state nobody re-reads. Item 28e forbids an agent closing its own issue on the grounds that self-certification is not verification; this closes an issue with no agent involved at all, on evidence that amounts to a substring in a branch name.

The near miss was total. Had the `Todo` move not happened to follow twenty seconds later, [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) would read `Done` today, its RSVP controls would still discard every student's answer, and the row that says so would be closed.

## Why it happens

Two mechanisms that are individually correct and jointly wrong:

1. `WORKFLOWS.md` rule 2 and item 28g require the issue identifier in the branch name. Linear links a PR to an issue on that identifier.
2. Item 28g asks the owner, once and outside the repo, to enable the Linear automation *PR merged → Done*. It is evidently enabled.

Link plus automation equals close. The PR body never enters into it, so omitting the magic word protects nothing.

**This makes item 28f factually wrong in this workspace.** It states, of an identifier in the title or branch name: *"links only"*, and *"on its own it leaves the issue sitting in* `In Review` *after merge."* Measured behaviour is that it closes.

The rule reads correctly in isolation — it is describing Linear's magic-word feature accurately. What it does not account for is the automation item 28g itself asks for, two subsections later, changing what a bare link does.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `docs/swarm/constitution.md` | 458-472 | item 28f — the "links only" claim, now false |
| `docs/swarm/constitution.md` | 485-488 | item 28g — the owner action that enables the automation making it false |
| `docs/swarm/WORKFLOWS.md` | rule 2 | requires the identifier in the branch name |

Measured instance, from [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says)'s own state history:

```
In Progress  02:29:11Z -> 04:02:01Z
Done         04:02:01Z -> 04:02:21Z   <- PR #138 merged
Todo         04:02:21Z -> 04:03:43Z   <- unrelated move, undid it by luck
```

## The one constraint

**Do not fix this by dropping identifiers from branch names.** The convention is load-bearing and its rationale is recorded in item 28g: a session-scoped name looks reserved and is not, and two sessions once worked one mutable ref because of it. Removing the identifier trades a rare wrong-close for a recurring collision.

The real distinction is between a branch that *does* an issue's work and one that merely *mentions* it — investigations, salvage, follow-ups and infrastructure fixes. Nothing in the naming scheme expresses that difference today, and Linear has no way to infer it.

## Size and tier

Either a correction to item 28f's wording plus a stated convention for non-work branches, or a change to the automation's scope in Linear, or both. Constitution edits are `boss-architect` / `boss-arbiter` only. No code.

Tier unjudged, because item 28c makes that the picker's first act.

## Suggested priority: high urgency, low cost

Correct item 28f before anyone relies on it.

1. **It has fired once and is live right now.** PR #139 sits open on the same branch, `claude/gam-304-failure-p3y021`, and will close [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) again on merge. Its body carries a warning as the first line, which is a mitigation and not a fix.
2. **Nothing is blocked on it**, but every investigation branch named after an issue is exposed, and those are common — a branch is routinely named for the issue being *investigated* rather than *implemented*.

It stops being deferrable at the merge of PR #139, which is imminent.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`f2ca7e5`) on 2026-08-10. The state history above is quoted from Linear rather than reconstructed, and PR #138 appears on [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) as attachment `523ffc77-c7a2-4117-acf3-5b28264ba169` — the link that carried the close.

* **The filing agent caused this.** The branch name was assigned to the session at startup, but the hazard was foreseeable and was not flagged before merging. It was discovered afterwards, while reading the state history for an unrelated reason — which is precisely how a silent failure gets found, and the argument for fixing it rather than remembering it.
* **Not verified: whether the automation is scoped or global.** That it is enabled is inferred from behaviour, not read from Linear's settings, since that is outside the repository. Confirm in the workspace before designing around it.

issues.title: Item 19 requires recording the premise-gate verdict; the dispatch path has no mechanism, so the first real one lived only in a 30-day artifact
issues.description:
The first premise gate ever run from the Linear dispatch path returned REVISE with 1 BLOCKER, 3 MAJOR, 4 MINOR and 1 NIT, backed by a PostgreSQL cluster it built itself. None of that reached the issue. `list_comments` on [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) returns `{"comments": []}`.

Item 19 requires the opposite, in four words: *"Record the verdict alongside the plan."*

## Why it is worth fixing

The verdict is the most expensive artifact the heavy tier produces and the only one that is pure evidence. This one proved all six RLS paths on `rsvps`, including the `on conflict do update` path a repeat answer takes — a policy distinction the issue body never mentions — and executed the consequence, showing a discarded `going` holds planned hours at `0 h` instead of `2.0 h`.

Item 19a prices a gate round at roughly 105-130K opus tokens. Losing the record means the next agent pays that again to learn what is already known. Worse, it pays it *without knowing* a previous round exists, so it cannot tell a fresh finding from a repeat.

## Why it happens

Nothing in the path writes it anywhere durable. The verdict is a subagent return value: it lands in the orchestrator's context, informs the revised packet, and then exists only inside the run's execution transcript — an artifact with **30-day retention**.

Item 24 joins recording to merging, so a merge would have carried it. Nothing merged. Item 19 says to record the verdict but names no destination, and predates dispatch entirely — it was written for a session where the orchestrator was a human-supervised process with a ledger to hand. Item 29 then froze that ledger, and Linear became where state lives, but item 19's instruction was never re-pointed at it.

The dispatch prompt does not mention recording verdicts either.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `docs/swarm/constitution.md` | 82-92 | item 19 — "Record the verdict alongside the plan", no destination named |
| `docs/swarm/constitution.md` | 93-98 | item 19a — prices a round at ~105-130K opus tokens, which is what is being discarded |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 116-172 | the dispatch prompt — never mentions recording a verdict |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 174-183 | the artifact step, which is where the verdict actually ends up, at 30-day retention |

## The one constraint

**A Linear comment and a git file are not interchangeable, and the choice matters.** Item 29's reasoning applies directly: Linear is the source and git is the backup, kept precisely because *"it is a hosted service on a free plan, and if the account lapses the history goes with it."* A verdict recorded only as a comment inherits that fragility; one recorded only in git is invisible to the owner deciding what to work on.

Second trap: the verdicts are large. This one is roughly 24 KB. Pasting that into an issue body would bury the defect the issue is about, which is exactly what item 30a exists to prevent. A comment summarising the verdict with a pointer to the committed file is likely the shape, but that is a design decision, not a foregone one.

## Size and tier

A step or convention that persists the verdict at the moment it is returned — a Linear comment, a committed file under `docs/swarm/active/`, or both. Roughly one prompt addition plus a documented destination. Possibly a constitution amendment to item 19 naming that destination, which is `boss-architect` / `boss-arbiter` territory.

Tier unjudged, because item 28c makes that the picker's first act.

## Suggested priority: medium urgency, low cost

Fix it before the second heavy dispatch, not the tenth.

1. **It has cost nothing yet, by luck.** This verdict was recovered by hand and committed in PR #139 while investigating an unrelated failure. That recovery is not repeatable at scale and depended on somebody happening to download a run artifact.
2. **Nothing is blocked on it.** No row cites this.

It stops being deferrable at the next HEAVY dispatch. Every one from here produces a verdict with a 30-day fuse and no destination.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`f2ca7e5`) on 2026-08-10.

* `list_comments(issueId: GAM-304)` → `{"comments": [], "hasNextPage": false}`. No verdict, no note, nothing.
* The verdict's existence and content are quoted from the run 31354278407 transcript, artifact `claude-run-GAM-304-31354278407`, now committed in PR #139.
* **The count was corrected to "3 MINOR" and then corrected back.** "4 MINOR" is right. The first correction counted `### MINOR-n` headings, found three (`MINOR-5`, `MINOR-6`, `MINOR-7`), and declared the gate's own severity line wrong. It was not: the fourth MINOR is graded inline in the required-revisions list rather than given a heading — *"Asymmetric banner placement — the author's falsifying condition HOLDS (graded MINOR, not fatal)"* — at `docs/swarm/active/GAM-304-premise-gate-round1.md:101`. Both the orchestrator's packet header and the later round-2 agent independently read it as four.

  Kept because it is this row's argument in miniature. Checking a verdict's own summary required reading the whole verdict, the whole verdict existed only inside an expiring artifact, and a confident recount from the wrong index produced a wrong "fix". **The merge commit of PR #139 carries the incorrect "3 MINOR" claim** and is not being rewritten; this note is the correction of record.
* `verification-log.md` **was not checked.** It is one of the four files Authority Boundaries put off-limits to the filing agent, so whether a parallel gap exists there is unestablished and should be confirmed by whoever picks this up.

issues.title: An escalated row has no reply address: `gate/human` is machine-settable, hand-clearable only, and sends the owner no notification
issues.description:
[GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says) escalated to the owner at 05:18:48Z with a decision-ready comment and three numbered options. The owner received no notification of it, and had they answered, nothing would have read the answer.

It stayed workable only because a session happened to be watching. Left alone it would have sat in `In Progress` indefinitely, looking exactly like an agent still working.

## Why it is worth fixing

The machine can put a row into a state only a person can leave, and then tells that person nothing. `gate/human` is designed to be used often — it is the correct outcome whenever item 19a's two-round cap is reached, whenever a premise needs a ruling, whenever scope is genuinely the owner's call. Every one of those produces a silently stalled row.

The failure is invisible on every surface: the workflow run is green, the issue reads `In Progress`, and `In Progress` is indistinguishable from healthy work in progress. Nothing accumulates in a queue anyone looks at.

This is the escalation half of item 28's own diagnosis — *"A queue nobody is told to consume is a document, not a dispatch system"* — turned around. Here the queue is one row deep and the person who must consume it is never told.

## Why it happens

Three mechanisms, each correct alone:

1. **The trigger is a state transition only.** `filter.ts:273` requires the new state to be `Todo`; `:283` requires `stateId` in `updatedFrom`. An escalated row is in `In Progress`, so nothing fires.
2. `gate/human` **blocks dispatch outright.** `filter.ts:308` returns `HUMAN_GATED`. Even moving the row to `Todo` would not dispatch it while the label is on.
3. **Comments cannot trigger anything, by design.** `filter.ts:255-256` drops any payload where `type !== 'Issue'`, and the file's own note at `:25-26` records that Linear delivers Comment payloads to this same endpoint and they are rejected.

So the two mechanisms that make an escalated row *safe* are the two that make it *unreachable*, and the channel the escalation was actually written in is the one provably not listened to.

**And the notification does not fire either.** The escalation comment is authored by *George Mitchom* — `LINEAR_DISPATCH_API_KEY` is the owner's own personal key, so every agent comment appears under the owner's name, and Linear does not notify you about your own comments. The one signal that does reach the owner is incidental: PR #140 is authored by `claude[bot]`, so a PR-opened email fires — for a pull request whose title reads like a routine docs commit.

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `supabase/functions/linear-dispatch/filter.ts` | 273 | new state must be `Todo` — an escalated row is `In Progress` |
| `supabase/functions/linear-dispatch/filter.ts` | 283 | `updatedFrom` must contain `stateId` — a comment changes no state |
| `supabase/functions/linear-dispatch/filter.ts` | 255-256 | `NOT_AN_ISSUE_EVENT` — Comment payloads are dropped |
| `supabase/functions/linear-dispatch/filter.ts` | 308 | `HUMAN_GATED` — the label blocks dispatch even from `Todo` |
| `.github/workflows/claude-linear-dispatch.yml` | 116-186 | the dispatch prompt — tells an agent how to escalate, never how the owner unblocks it |

## The one constraint

**Do not fix this by making** `gate/human` **dispatchable.** `filter.ts:71-73` states the reason: *"a machine may not take it… taking a row gated on a human is the kind of quiet over-reach the constitution exists to prevent."* The label must keep working. What is missing is a *documented, deliberate* human action that clears it — not an automatic one.

Second trap: a comment webhook sounds like the natural fix and is the riskiest option here. Anyone who can comment could then trigger a dispatch, and the escalation comments are long-form prose an agent would have to *interpret* as authorization. A label the owner applies — one explicit, unambiguous act — is far safer than parsing intent from free text.

## Size and tier

The cheap fix is one paragraph. Ranked by cost:

1. **Tell the owner the ritual.** The escalation comment offered three options and never said how to enact one. Adding *"to authorize: remove* `gate/human`*, then move the issue to* `Todo`*"* to the dispatch prompt closes most of the gap for the price of four lines of YAML.
2. **A saved Linear view filtered on** `gate/human`**.** This is the "waiting on me" queue that does not exist today. Zero code, outside the repo.
3. **A separate Linear user for the dispatch key**, so agent comments notify the owner instead of appearing as their own writing. Outside the repo, and it changes every agent comment's author — check nothing keys off that first.

Tier unjudged, because item 28c makes that the picker's first act.

## Suggested priority: high urgency, low cost

Do (1) before the next `gate/human` escalation, which is likely the next HEAVY row.

1. **It has fired once and was caught only by luck.** [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says)'s escalation was resolved because a session was actively watching the run. That is not a control, it is an accident, and it will not repeat.
2. **Nothing is blocked on it today**, but it silently blocks anything that escalates from here. Unlike `GAM-314`, where the loss is visible once someone reads a transcript, this failure looks identical to healthy work forever.

It stops being deferrable the first time an escalation happens while nobody is watching — which is the normal case, since dispatch exists precisely so runs happen unattended.

## Verification note

Re-checked against `main` (`ac02959`) on 2026-08-10. Every citation above was read from `filter.ts` at that HEAD rather than recalled, and the three guards were confirmed against the file's own explanatory comments.

* **The notification claim is inference from one observation, not a settings read.** The escalation comment's author id is `6a1e0bbe-d8e7-4d62-b3e0-895e674b62fc`, identical to [GAM-304](https://linear.app/gamitch/issue/GAM-304/t809-studenthomes-sign-up-cant-go-control-writes-nothing-and-says)'s `createdById` and `assigneeId` — so the agent writes as the owner. That Linear does not notify a user about their own comment is standard behaviour but was **not** verified in this workspace's notification settings. Confirm before relying on (3) as the fix.
* **Not established: whether Linear's webhook can even subscribe to Comment events here.** `filter.ts` rejects them, which proves the current subscription does not act on them; it does not prove the subscription could not be widened. Irrelevant to the recommended fix, but it matters if someone reaches for the comment-webhook option the constraint above argues against.

issues.title: StudentHome's per-row RSVP spinner can never render — `isLoading` is dead code and its comment says otherwise
issues.description:
A student's per-row "Sign up" spinner never appears. The button is passed `isLoading={isThisRowPending}`, and `isThisRowPending` cannot be true for a button that is still on screen — so the code is inert and the comment above it describes an affordance the app does not have.

Nothing is broken for the user: the row visibly disappears and every sibling control disables, so the in-flight write is still legible. What is wrong is the record. This is the same shape as item 20's three cited failures — an inert control whose inertness is recorded only in a comment — except that here the comment does not even say it is inert.

## Why it happens

`withLocalRsvpOverride` commits the optimistic RSVP override in the **same batched render** as `setIsRsvpSubmitting`/`setPendingSessionId`. `getUnansweredOutreachOpportunities` then treats any answered RSVP as no-longer-unanswered, so the clicked `SignupOpportunityRowItem` is torn out of the tree in the very commit that sets the flag. The `Button` instance never renders again with `isThisRowPending === true`.

Measured, not reasoned: a DOM probe during an in-flight write counted `SIGNUP_BUTTON_COUNT_BEFORE=2` → `SIGNUP_BUTTON_COUNT_DURING=1`, with no `aria-busy` on any button anywhere in the tree. Reproduced on both the `going` and the `declined` paths.

**This is not a jsdom artifact and not a test-harness limitation — the spinner is unreachable for a real user too.**

## Where it lives

| File | Line | What it does |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1327 | `isThisRowPending`, provably always `false` while mounted |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1335, 1342 | `isLoading={isThisRowPending}` on both buttons |
| `StudentHome.tsx` | 1321-1323 | the comment claiming `isLoading` "is additionally scoped to THIS row" |
